title: Processes & event transport
summary: 20 · Process lifecycle, forks and event transport In one sentence: A process can create children. Seeing events from two PIDs does not prove there were only two processes. Key terms Term Meaning ------ PID The operating system's p
text: 20 · Process lifecycle, forks and event transport In one sentence: A process can create children. Seeing events from two PIDs does not prove there were only two processes. Key terms Term Meaning ------ PID The operating system's process ID. Wrapper event lines include it so events from a parent and its observed children stay separate. ACK A final status message from an observed process, reporting its last event number and whether any writes failed. Example. If a child prints nothing and never writes to the wrapper file, the event reader can't discover it by looking at recorded PIDs. The parent and the observed PIDs might have complete logs while that child stays unknown. Complete history for observed event PIDs is not a census of every descendant of a fork. Level 1 · Intuition The debugger follows one inferior. The allocation wrapper can also write PID-labelled events from forked children. These are different scopes. A child that forks, logs no allocation and exits silently may be invisible. "Every observed PID's events were verified" can never mean "every descendant was discovered." {{diagram:partial}} Level 2 · From wrapper file to scoped coverage How events are written The C wrapper writes one completed line per event to C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE. Each line contains: Field Meaning ------ PID Which process Sequence number The next event for that PID Operation What was called Allocation ID The tracked ID Address and result What came back What a fork does to IDs - After a fork, the child resets its inherited logger lock and counters. So parent and child can both have a local allocation ID 1. - In the final JSON, Rust can combine PID and local ID into a wider ID, (pid << 32) local_id, so that observed processes' lifetimes stay distinct. - Older journal rows may still show the local IDs. - This is a change in representation within one trace. It is not a link between independent program runs. How the reader decides history is complete - On normal exit, a process may write a final ACK with its last event number and any write failures. A crash or _exit may not. - The reader detects incomplete lines, missing sequence numbers, missing ACKs and caps, and marks the history partial when appropriate. What "complete" is scoped to process_scope="verified_observed_pids_only" means the engine checked: 1. the processes that actually supplied event logs, plus 2. the inferior GDB followed. When heap_history.complete=true, the available event sequence and transport checks passed for that limited scope only. It does not turn unobserved_process_coverage="unknown" into "all children observed." Point Consequence ------ GDB's saved stack and variable snapshots Belong to the followed inferior, not automatically to every child that wrote allocation lines Two different PIDs in an imported trace Don't by themselves prove a parent-child relationship An observed child sends no final ACK The engine lowers heap-history confidence; it does not invent a GDB snapshot of that child Worked fork cases From a fresh audit of the phase8dr_fork.c fixture: Mode Heap events Event PIDs complete Note --------------- observed 6 2 scoped complete Both processes supplied events silent 4 1 scoped complete Despite a silent child: it never wrote to the log, so it was never observed incomplete 6 2 false The child's final ACK is missing All three have unobserved_process_coverage="unknown". Level 3 · Implementation and typed view Layer Where to look ------ C cte_after_fork_child, cte_write_all, cte_emit_locked, and the normal-exit status writer in c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c Rust src/allocation_tracker.rs::{EventTailer, verify_event_status, HeapTimeline::global_id}; src/trace.rs assembles HeapHistoryCoverage; src/supervisor.rs controls subprocess groups, cancellation, subreaper ownership and best-effort cgroup handling Parser TraceStore::heap_process_scope() returns HeapProcessScope::Unknown, VerifiedObservedPidsOnly { observed_event_pids, followed_inferior_pid, observed_history_complete }, or Unsupported. validate_deep() verifies annotations against recorded events. process_coverage().unobserved_descendants stays unavailable on sound traces json {"complete":true,"process_scope":"verified_observed_pids_only","unobserved_process_coverage":"unknown"} This is an illustrative subset of heap_history. It is not an all-process claim and not a complete JSON object for the model. The identity tables(schema.htmlidentity-domains) explain why per-PID sequences and global allocation IDs are not stops or event positions. Warning: The engine is not a security sandbox. With no delegated cgroup, descendants that escape the owned group may evade tree-wide limits. Neither RLIMIT_NPROC nor a global fork census is used.

title: Budgets, gaps & export
summary: 21 · Timeouts, budgets, coverage and export In one sentence: The recording has several budgets, each with a different job. Before interpreting a shortened trace, ask what was limited. Key terms Term Meaning ------ Snapshot limit A
text: 21 · Timeouts, budgets, coverage and export In one sentence: The recording has several budgets, each with a different job. Before interpreting a shortened trace, ask what was limited. Key terms Term Meaning ------ Snapshot limit A bound on how many stopped-state snapshots can be kept. Journal vs export The JSONL journal grows during capture. The final JSON is a separate document made afterward, with its own byte limit. Example. A capped journal can be 1,961 bytes while the final JSON is 22,883 bytes. That doesn't break the cap: the first cap applied only to the journal. Even a successful JSON export limit doesn't constrain the memory already used to assemble the trace. Level 1 · Intuition A finite budget produces a useful partial recording rather than pretending missing data was observed. Different caps protect different things: journal bytes, JSON document size, debugger commands, snapshot reads, tool time and parser page size. They are not one universal memory limit. A crash, timeout or cap is an outcome. It does not automatically corrupt the records already captured. {{diagram:partial}} Level 2 · Budgets across stages Time - The clock starts before the engine even checks which tools are available. - Each compiler, debugger or analysis step must finish before the whole session's deadline. - GDB commands also have their own command-count and time checks. - "The program never stopped again" and "GDB never replied to my command" are different errors, reported differently. Cancellation and cleanup - Ctrl-C or a normal termination signal asks the supervisor to cancel tools and save partial JSON when possible. - An abrupt kill may leave an unfinished journal. - The engine tries to manage child process groups and bound read pipes. - OS limits such as prlimit apply to the program GDB stopped, and optional cgroups can help with descendants. These reduce resource risk. They do not make arbitrary C safe to run as a security sandbox. The limits Limit Default Governs (not equivalent to RAM) ------:--- timeout_seconds 10 s Entire pipeline; per-stage limits clamp to it max_steps 1,000 Source/dual progression; separate from instruction cap max_instruction_events 100,000 Attempted instruction recording max_source_checkpoints 1,000 Selected source-state records max_trace_bytes 128 MiB JSONL journal byte accounting, not final JSON max_trace_memory_bytes 32 MiB Resident serialized-record accounting, not total Rust RSS max_json_export_bytes 128 MiB Each formatted final JSON document max_snapshot_memory_bytes 1 MiB Budget of captured bytes at a checkpoint max_gdb_commands 1,000,000 MI queries and control commands MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE 128 Trace Parser TP-7 results in a single request What happens when a limit is hit - The recorder writes down which scope the limit covered and why it stopped or truncated data. - It keeps explicit trace_gaps for stretches of instructions it can't show exactly. - Heap events and optional source/type metadata can be partial for different reasons. - storage.finalized only means the JSONL journal was closed. It does not mean the C program finished successfully. - In --journal-only mode, the final trace may omit in-memory instruction arrays. The journal can be read in order, but it alone cannot recreate all the final reports needed for a full TraceStore. A measured example of why caps differ The final audit set --max-trace-bytes 2048: Run Result ------ Journal 1,961 bytes Separately exported JSON 22,883 bytes, correctly marked partial Second run with --max-json-export-bytes 8192 Exited with max_json_export_bytes exceeded and wrote no JSON Neither test establishes a peak process-RAM limit. See parser ingestion limits(parser-ingestion.htmllevel-2-architecture-and-compatibility). Level 3 · Enforcement sites and results File Role ------ src/resource_limits.rs::{ExecutionLimits::validate, limit_stopped_inferior, CgroupGuard} Limit validation and enforcement src/supervisor.rs::{scope, stage_deadline, request_cancel} Deadlines and cancellation src/recorder.rs::{Recorder::truncate, Recorder::checkpoint, Recorder::event} and src/storage.rs::{Journal::append, Journal::finalize, recover} Distinguish retained records from journal contents and total attempts src/models.rs::RecordingData Holds the serialized result src/json_export.rs::{preflight, export_json_cancellable} Bounds each emitted JSON document without first assembling a giant output string. This does not bound the already-assembled DebugSessionTrace or parser RSS sh target/release/c-trace-engine fixtures/c/infinite_loop.c \ --trace-mode dual --max-steps 60 --timeout 35 \ --no-pretty --output /tmp/visual-c-limit.json A capped trace can have execution_status=step_limit_reached, retained events, gaps and coverage.complete_for_scope=false. Consumers should read validation findings(parser-validation.html) and confidence(parser-semantic.html). They should not treat compiled_successfully=true as complete execution. Warning: The Trace Parser's input cap defaults to 512 MiB. This prevents oversized input buffering but does not make deserialization or trace assembly constant-memory. The 128-record page bound constrains query outputs, not the whole trace.

title: Entry, configuration & errors
summary: 22 · Engine entry, configuration, and errors In one sentence: The front door. Command-line arguments become a tracing request (TraceConfig), and errors become meaningful exit results. Key terms Term Meaning ------ CLI Command-line
text: 22 · Engine entry, configuration, and errors In one sentence: The front door. Command-line arguments become a tracing request (TraceConfig), and errors become meaningful exit results. Key terms Term Meaning ------ CLI Command-line interface: the flags and file names you pass when starting c-trace-engine. Configuration precedence The rule that decides who wins when a CLI flag and a config-file value set the same thing. Example. You pass a C file and --max-steps 50. main converts them into a TraceConfig, and the tracing code receives those values instead of re-reading command-line text. A bad flag is an input error. A compiler diagnostic is a recorded C build result. They are not the same failure. The big picture The executable is a thin adapter over the library. It: 1. parses flags, 2. builds a TraceConfig, 3. awaits trace::trace_program, then 4. exports the returned DebugSessionTrace. Outcome What you get ------ A compilation rejection A trace result (with diagnostics) A configuration, tool or export failure An error, possibly with no usable trace Next boundaries: compilation(engine-compiler-deep.html), process ownership(engine-supervision-deep.html), export(engine-export-deep.html). File 1 · src/main.rs: from CLI to exit status Principal function: async fn main() - ExitCode (src/main.rs:22-80) - Cli::parse() belongs to Clap (the argument-parsing library). to_config() is the first engine-specific step that can fail. - The CLI owns the effective config, clones it into the tracing call, then borrows the resulting trace for a synchronous JSON export. - After tracing, it installs an independent SIGINT watcher and passes its AtomicBool to export_json_cancellable. It aborts that watcher once export returns (src/main.rs:34-59). - This export watcher is distinct from the supervised collection-time SIGINT/SIGTERM token. rust let config = cli.to_config()?; // schematic: main prints the error and returns exit 1 let trace = trace::trace_program(config.clone()).await?; let output = json_export::export_json_cancellable( &trace, config.pretty, config.limits.max_json_export_bytes, config.output_file.as_deref(), &mut std::io::stdout().lock(), Some(&cancelled), ); This shortens the actual match arms at src/main.rs:26-79. main does not itself return Result. Exit codes Situation Exit code ---:---: Bad config, operational tracing error, failed export, or inability to install the export signal watcher (message on stderr) 1 Export succeeded and execution_status == CompileFailed (a diagnostic JSON trace is still emitted) 2 Any other successfully exported trace, including crashes and timeouts 0 (src/main.rs:59-78.) So a shell exit of 0 does not certify complete execution. There's no main.rs unit test. The final audit(../stage1-final-audit.md) independently exercised compile-failure exit 2 and export-cap exit 1. File 2 · src/lib.rs: the public crate boundary Item Detail ------ Principal exports pub use config::{BuildConfig, TraceConfig}; pub use error::{EngineError, Result}; pub use models::DebugSessionTrace; pub use resource_limits::ExecutionLimits; (src/lib.rs:49-52) Public modules cli, compiler, supervisor, processor, storage, json_export, trace (src/lib.rs:25-47) Ownership The library owns no global trace instance: callers supply a TraceConfig and own the returned trace Embedding You can call trace_program without Clap or main's stdout/exit-code policy Tests None in lib.rs; behavior is tested in the modules and integration suite The module map at src/lib.rs:8-23 is orientation, not an execution guarantee. File 3 · src/cli.rs: flag precedence and source validation Principal items: - derive(Parser, Debug) pub struct Cli (src/cli.rs:21-192) - pub fn to_config(&self) - Result<TraceConfig (src/cli.rs:194-383) - fn file_build(file: &ConfigFile, source: &Path) - BuildConfig (src/cli.rs:385-399) How to_config decides things Step Rule ------ 1. Config file Reads and deserializes the optional --config first. Unreadable or invalid JSON is EngineError::Config. 2. Primary source Chosen in this order: --source, then the positional source, then the JSON file's source. (Clap forbids giving both CLI forms together.) 3. Lists Copies the file's build lists, then appends repeated CLI --add-source, --define, --library, etc. 4. Scalar settings Replaced only when the matching CLI option is present (src/cli.rs:199-240). 5. Source check The primary source is checked to be a file, relative to build.working_directory when set. This does not validate every auxiliary input or canonicalize the stored path (src/cli.rs:242-256). rust let source = self.source.clone() .or_else( self.source_positional.clone()) .or_else( file.source.clone()) .ok_or_else( EngineError::Config("no source file given ...".into()))?; let mut build = file_build(&file, &source); build.defines.extend(self.define.iter().cloned()); let mut program_args = file.program_args.clone(); program_args.extend(self.arg.iter().cloned()); program_args.extend(self.program_args.iter().cloned()); This abbreviated walkthrough follows src/cli.rs:211-261. The real missing-source message also names the supported CLI forms. Details worth knowing - Arguments after -- and repeated --arg go to the inferior (your C program), not to GCC. - Limits start from file.limits.unwrap_or_default(), and each CLI scalar that is present overrides one field (src/cli.rs:263-293,330-359). - --no-pretty, --keep-temp and --clang-ast are one-way switches. When unset, the file or default value stays in force (src/cli.rs:295-301,378-380). - --journal-only turns off retained instruction events, and Clap requires --journal with it. trace_program_inner also refuses journal-only configuration without a path for non-CLI callers (src/cli.rs:154-157,306-312; src/trace.rs:172-176). - An invalid --memory-region syntax or byte count gives a Config error before tracing (src/cli.rs:319-329). - Tests: positional_source, missing_source_is_config_error, flag_accumulation_and_program_args, limit_flags_override_defaults, config_file_merge_precedence (src/cli.rs:415-550). File 4 · src/config.rs: request types and defaults Type / function Location What it is --------- BuildConfig src/config.rs:20-45 Project inputs and linking options user_sources(&self) - Vec<PathBuf src/config.rs:47-56 Collects primary plus additional sources, dropping empty paths TraceConfig + impl Default src/config.rs:58-112 Adds inferior args/cwd, limits, output destination, tool overrides, optional AST, tracing policy ConfigFile src/config.rs:114-144 A different, flat JSON-file schema with optional scalars and deny_unknown_fields SanitizerTrigger src/config.rs:154-174 Defaults to OnCrashOrValgrindError TracingConfig + Default src/config.rs:176-221 Defaults: Dual mode, static disassembly on, global discovery on, resident instruction events retained Things to watch for: Don't paste a serialized TraceConfig into --config. ConfigFile has different keys. - BuildConfig deliberately places user compiler flags after the engine defaults, and that ordering can change observation fidelity. - These are owned, cloned configuration values, not global mutable knobs. - There are no tests in config.rs; CLI merge tests and ExecutionLimits validation cover adjacent behavior. - A comment on TraceConfig::output_file mentions stdout_json, but no such field exists. The current CLI writes stdout on a successful export (src/config.rs:70-75; src/main.rs:50-57). File 5 · src/error.rs: the failure vocabulary Principal type and alias: pub enum EngineError and pub type Result<T = std::result::Result<T, EngineError (src/error.rs:10-59). Variant Meaning ------ Config Bad configuration MissingTool A required tool isn't available Deadline { operation } A deadline expired Cancelled The session was cancelled LimitReached A configured limit was hit Io, Json I/O and JSON failures (converted via from) others GDB/MI, allocation-event, Valgrind and resource-limit stage errors from converts I/O, JSON and MI-parse errors rather than flattening everything into strings. The caller decides whether an error is returned directly or recorded in a partial trace: - A GCC source error produces CompilationOutput { success: false, diagnostics }, then CompileFailed. - probe_tool can return MissingTool, and the CLI exits 1 (src/compiler.rs:99-128,518-527; src/trace.rs:336-350). error.rs has no local tests; CLI, compiler and supervisor tests exercise the error branches. A bare EngineError never proves that a serialized trace was produced. For the wire vocabulary, continue with model and exporter internals(engine-export-deep.html). For limits governing the request, see supervision(engine-supervision-deep.html). Diagram notes Diagram What it shows ------ The CLI boundary<br{{diagram:d2-cli}} main owns process exit policy; trace_program owns the bounded session; export is a separate fallible operation. Configuration precedence<br{{diagram:d2-config}} Defaults, JSON-file settings and explicit CLI values meet in Cli::to_config; later stages consume the owned effective configuration. Session control flow<br{{diagram:d2-session}} Compilation, static metadata, the GDB stop loop, optional diagnostics and trace assembly are distinct phases under one deadline. Failure propagation<br{{diagram:d2-error}} A compile failure can produce a trace; an operational error or export-cap failure need not produce a usable JSON document.

title: Compiler & diagnostics
summary: 23 · Compiler invocation and diagnostic evidence In one sentence: The code-level story of how GCC commands are assembled, started and interpreted. Key terms Term Meaning ------ Argv The exact list of arguments given to an OS proce
text: 23 · Compiler invocation and diagnostic evidence In one sentence: The code-level story of how GCC commands are assembled, started and interpreted. Key terms Term Meaning ------ Argv The exact list of arguments given to an OS process. Reading it is safer than imagining what shell command ran. Diagnostic fallback If GCC can't produce one structured warning format, the engine tries another supported one instead of silently losing errors. Example. The debug GCC command includes the wrapper source and the --wrap linker switches. The separate sanitizer command uses different flags. A warning from either build has a file, line and message when GCC supplies them. A compiler subprocess timing out is not the same event as GCC finishing and rejecting invalid C. The big picture The engine builds an instrumented debug executable before any debugger run, then attempts a separate sanitized executable. - Compilation success is a prerequisite for runtime evidence. - Sanitizer build success is not proof that a sanitizer later found or reproduced a defect. The request is assembled in entry/configuration(engine-entry-deep.html), and subprocesses are owned by supervision(engine-supervision-deep.html). Step 1 · Options and tool probes (src/compiler.rs) CompileOptions holds { sanitized, sanitizer_variant, include_alloc_tracker, tracker_source, output_path }, with three constructors (src/compiler.rs:28-73): Constructor Use ------ debug(output_path, tracker_source) The debug build sanitized(output_path) A sanitizer build sanitized_with_variant(output_path, variant) A specific sanitizer variant CompilationOutput retains: success, native exit code, binary path, parsed diagnostics, raw stderr, the selected format, and an optional sanitizer variant (src/compiler.rs:75-97). The orchestrator creates the tracker source and passes it to compile_project. The debug build wraps malloc/calloc/realloc/free; sanitized builds omit the tracker (src/trace.rs:226-237; src/compiler.rs:543-566). Probing tools Function Location Behavior --------- probe_tool(tool, version_arg) - Result<String src/compiler.rs:99-128 Requires a successful status; returns the first stdout line; turns most spawn/probe failures into MissingTool, preserving cancellation detect_diagnostics_format(cc) - DiagnosticsFormat src/compiler.rs:130-158 Tries -fdiagnostics-format=json, then sarif-stderr, then falls back to Text Both launch processes through supervisor::output with a three-second stage deadline and 1 MiB per-pipe capture. Format detection tests candidate commands and recognizes an unsupported-argument message, rather than comparing a hard-coded GCC version. A probe that returns output without that message can still select the attempted format, because the later parse has a text fallback. compile_project itself probes gcc --version. trace_program_inner also probes required GCC and GDB before creating the session directory (src/compiler.rs:535-537; src/trace.rs:203-229). Step 2 · Assembling the exact argv Signature: fn build_argv(build: &BuildConfig, opts: &CompileOptions, diag_flag: Option<&str) - Vec<String (src/compiler.rs:392-452). Every argument is passed individually to tokio::process::Command, never interpolated into a shell. The order matters: text gcc -g -O0 -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fsanitize=address,undefined -fdiagnostics-format=json -fdiagnostics-format=sarif-stderr -Wl,--wrap=malloc -Wl,--wrap=calloc -Wl,--wrap=realloc -Wl,--wrap=free -D... -I... compiler_flags... source_file additional_sources... tracker_source object_files... -L... linker_flags... -l... -o output_path Brackets mark conditional or vector segments, not literal shell syntax. Fact Detail ------ Sanitizer vs wrapper Mutually exclusive in the standard constructors User compiler flags Come after -g -O0 -fno-omit-frame-pointer, so they can override defaults Linking options Come after the inputs (src/compiler.rs:396-450) program_args Absent, since they're for the inferior Working directory compile sets current_dir only when build.working_directory is present (src/compiler.rs:471-475) Validation Only checks the primary source path is nonempty; GCC handles unresolved extra inputs and linkage Output paths Debug: <session_dir/<output_name or program_debug; sanitized: _asan (src/compiler.rs:539-565) Step 3 · Running GCC and handling failures Signature: pub async fn compile(build, cc, opts, format) - Result<CompilationOutput (src/compiler.rs:454-527). It runs the command via supervisor::output(&mut cmd, supervisor::deadline(), 8 1024 1024). Situation Result ------ Timeout or cancellation An engine error, not a fabricated GCC diagnostic Nonzero GCC status Normally Ok(CompilationOutput { success: false, ... }); exit code -1 if no numeric code exists Success Requires both a successful process status and no parsed error, linker-error or fatal error diagnostics (src/compiler.rs:478-526) Output beyond the capture cap The output carries output_truncated, but compile does not propagate that flag into CompilationOutput. So diagnostics or stderr beyond the cap can't be claimed complete trace_program_inner separately clamps the whole build future to compiler_timeout_seconds within the global deadline (src/trace.rs:230-238). Process cleanup can briefly outlast a deadline. Step 4 · The sanitizer fallback builds rust let debug_result = compile(build, "gcc", &debug_opts, format).await?; if !debug_result.success { return Ok((debug_result, not_built())); } for variant in "address,undefined", "address", "undefined" { let opts = CompileOptions::sanitized_with_variant(asan_out.clone(), variant); let result = compile(build, "gcc", &opts, format).await; // Schematic: actual loop breaks on a successful variant or an engine error. } This follows pub async fn compile_project(build, session_dir, tracker_source) - Result<(CompilationOutput, CompilationOutput) (src/compiler.rs:529-581). Behavior Detail ------ Variant order Combined ASan/UBSan, then ASan-only, then UBSan-only A failed variant's output Does not become the returned sanitizer result If none succeeds The returned sentinel is not_built() (with an error string in raw_stderr only when a compile call returned Err) Debug build vs sanitizer failure The successful debug build is retained even if optional sanitizer compilation fails If the debug build failed trace_program_inner records its diagnostics and stops without snapshots (src/trace.rs:291-350); optional sanitizer unavailability is marked separately Sanitizer runs, when triggered, are separate executions, not observations of the GDB process. See diagnostics(engine-diagnostics.html). Step 5 · Normalizing diagnostic formats Parser Location Handles --------- parse_legacy_gcc_json(stderr) src/compiler.rs:232-259 Legacy GCC JSON: first location/caret, flattens child notes parse_sarif(stderr) src/compiler.rs:317-366 SARIF: first physical location, maps camel-case region fields text_diagnostics(stderr) src/compiler.rs:368-390 Plain-text fallback Rules shared by all three: - Legacy JSON and SARIF each support consecutive documents from multiple translation units. - A missing location becomes <unknown/zero, never a guessed source position. - If structured parsing fails, it falls back to a single text diagnostic (up to 4,000 characters). Known linker phrases map to linker-error; any other nonempty stderr maps to error. - The normalized payload is CompilerDiagnostic { file, line, column, kind, message } (src/models.rs:50-59). Tests: gcc_legacy_caret_locations_and_streams_are_preserved and gcc_sarif_stream_and_camel_case_region (src/compiler.rs:595-611). The final audit(../stage1-final-audit.md) independently confirms a live compilation failure produced diagnostics without debugger events. Reminder: No compiler output or tool version is evidence that a source expression executed. Runtime and static metadata have separate provenance (see schema(schema.html)). Diagram notes Diagram What it shows ------ Compilation lifecycle<br{{diagram:d2-compile}} GCC invocation, bounded output capture, diagnostic normalization and optional sanitizer variants. Build artifacts<br{{diagram:d2-build-artifacts}} The wrapped debug executable is the only binary GDB executes; sanitizer artifacts and Clang syntax are separate.

title: GDB controller & stop loop
summary: 24 · GDB/MI2 controller and the recorded stop loop In one sentence: The machinery that sends GDB commands and waits for replies while the program runs and pauses. Key terms Term Meaning ------ Token A number attached to a debugger
text: 24 · GDB/MI2 controller and the recorded stop loop In one sentence: The machinery that sends GDB commands and waits for replies while the program runs and pauses. Key terms Term Meaning ------ Token A number attached to a debugger command so its reply can be routed back to the command that asked. Asynchronous stop A separate GDB message announcing the program paused, possibly after a command was already acknowledged. Example. GDB may answer 4^running to command 4. That only means it started the requested continuation. A later stopped tells us where the program actually paused. A missing reply must never let late output answer the next command. A missing stop is a different timeout condition. The big picture The debugger subsystem does two separate jobs: 1. Own one GDB process and turn its MI2 output into typed debugger facts. 2. Run the stop loop that decides what to retain. A command acknowledgement is never treated as a stopped event. Piece File ------ Orchestration src/trace.rs Process, token and PTY machinery src/gdb_mi.rs Syntax decoding src/mi_parser.rs Part 1 · Orchestration around GDB (src/trace.rs) Principal signatures: - pub(crate) async fn trace_program_inner(config: TraceConfig) - Result<DebugSessionTrace (src/trace.rs:167) - pub async fn run_gdb_phase(config, limits, classifier, binary, event_file, event_status_file, reader, timeline, notes, type_metadata) - Result<GdbPhaseResult (src/trace.rs:1113-1124) Who does what Function Does ------ trace_program_inner Probes tools, writes the C tracker source, compiles, optionally extracts static metadata, then calls run_gdb_phase with the event/status paths (src/trace.rs:203-439) run_gdb_phase Creates the Recorder, clones the UserCodeClassifier, records the injected allocator source as instrumentation_file, optionally creates a cgroup, builds GdbLaunchOptions (src/trace.rs:1125-1189) Startup failures GdbSession::launch is called at src/trace.rs:1191-1212. Failure Becomes ------ Launch failure after the wall deadline expired Timeout Launch failure otherwise DebuggerFailure An output limit OutputLimitReached Missing main breakpoint A recorded limitation, not a fabricated source checkpoint (src/trace.rs:1226-1249) The stop loop The loop starts at src/trace.rs:1371. Each iteration follows a strict evidence order: Action Reference --------- 1 Increment stop_id; check command and terminal conditions 2 Drain EventFileReader::read_new src/trace.rs:1387-1405 3 Mark transport damage 4 Ingest rows into HeapTimeline 5 Journal newly observed events with Recorder::allocations(..., stop_id) 6 Only then classify an exit, signal, user-code stop or non-user frame Why heap events come first: allocation events logged before this stop must be known before the snapshot is taken. Case Handling ------ Fatal signals Capture state and a crash report (src/trace.rs:1441-1518) Resource vs benign signals Distinguished by classify_signal (src/trace.rs:2031-2063) Nonterminal limits Break to cleanup and a gap Normal exit / crash Separate terminal branches (src/trace.rs:1954-2024) After termination, a final read_new preserves destructor and exit-handler events (src/trace.rs:1977-1991). Then finish_phase, debugger counters, profiling categories and recorder.finish() produce GdbPhaseResult (src/trace.rs:1991-2024). If multiple threads were observed, the recorder is truncated to selected-thread-only coverage. Part 2 · Session types and launch (src/gdb_mi.rs) Principal types Type Location Owns --------- GdbSession :270-318 The child process, stdin, shared routing state, async receiver, activation map, caches Shared :117-138 Pending oneshot waiters, stream accumulation, program buffer, EOF flag, module epoch StoppedInfo :139-164 The typed asynchronous stop GdbLaunchOptions :165-178 Binary, cwd, args, env, limits MiCommandResponse :179-221 The tokened record plus stream text CheckpointReads :222-269 The per-stop byte-read reuse map Launching GDB Signature: pub async fn launch(opts: &GdbLaunchOptions) - Result<GdbSession (src/gdb_mi.rs:389-512). - Refuses cancelled or expired sessions. - Creates a PTY (a pseudo-terminal, so the inferior's output can be captured) and enables subreaper ownership. - Starts gdb --nx --quiet --interpreter=mi2 <binary with stdin/stdout piped and stderr null (:396-423). - GDB gets its own process group and kill_on_drop(true). No inferior rlimits are installed on GDB itself (:411-416). - The reader task and PTY task are spawned before session configuration (:446-450). Configuration commands sent at launch (:483-505) Command Why ------ -gdb-set pagination off, confirm off No interactive prompts debuginfod enabled off No network symbol fetching mi-async on, non-stop off Asynchronous stops, all threads stop together style enabled off Plain output may-call-functions off GDB won't call functions in the inferior auto-load off No auto-loaded scripts Set the inferior TTY; optionally pass program arguments A configuration failure kills the session rather than returning a half-configured debugger. The inferior inherits C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE and C_TRACE_EVENT_STATUS_FILE from run_gdb_phase (src/trace.rs:1176-1187). Part 3 · Command tokens and asynchronous stops execute pub async fn execute(&mut self, command: &str) - Result<MiCommandResponse (src/gdb_mi.rs:533-621) 1. Checks cancellation, poison, deadline and command cap. 2. Allocates next_token. 3. Registers a oneshot in Shared.pending. 4. Clears stale stream text. 5. Writes "{token}{command}\n". 6. Waits only for that token's result. A response timeout sets poisoned = true, because a late stream can't safely be matched to a later command (:600-608). wait_stopped pub async fn wait_stopped(&mut self, timeout: Duration) - Result<StoppedInfo (:624-671) - Loops over the asynchronous channel and returns only MiRecord::Exec { class: "stopped" }. - Records selected_thread, handles notifications such as gdb-eof, and buffers unrelated async records up to 4,096 (:624-670). - StoppedInfo::is_exit, is_signal, value and error_message classify the record (:139-191). Reader and routing Component Behavior Location --------- reader_task 16 MiB line bound; EOF fails every pending command and emits gdb-eof src/gdb_mi.rs:2302-2338 handle_line Ignores blank lines and GDB prompts; sends malformed lines to the bounded console log :2340-2372 route_record Sends tokened ^ results to the matching waiter; routes async records to the async channel; tracks module/thread/inferior notifications; treats console/log stream text as diagnostics :2374-2445 PTY reader Owns the master fd, appends inferior output to ProgramBuffer, notifies waiters when the output cap is first exceeded :2447-2484 An asynchronous token is not a command acknowledgement, even if the numbers happen to match. Part 4 · Frame and variable capture Types Type Location Role --------- UserCodeClassifier src/gdb_mi.rs:1550-1559 Distinguishes instrumentation runtime, user code, system library and unknown frames CaptureOptions :1698-1717 Variable/read/aggregate budgets, optional DWARF ObservationTypes, caller-frame limits, the transient-stop optimization CapturedState :1740-1749 Owns frames, variables, caller frames, memory usage and errors capture_state (src/gdb_mi.rs:1840-2227) pub async fn capture_state(session, opts, reads) - Result<CapturedState Step What it does Reference --------- 1 Handles the derived-chain transient stop :1847-1862 2 Otherwise runs -stack-list-frames 0 200, parses bounded frames, computes an activation path oldest-to-youngest :1864-1910 3 A truncated chain clears activation continuity instead of reusing sliding prefixes :1889-1895 4 Non-user frames return after frame/activation bookkeeping :1911-1913 For user frames, it then: - executes -stack-list-variables --all-values, - computes duplicate-name counts over the full list, and probes lexical symbols for the selected cap (:1914-1947), - keeps duplicate lexical declarations as separate variables with activation/scoped identities. An unresolved collision becomes unresolved:..., not a guessed value (:1981-2051), - otherwise uses fresh probe address/size/target data, falling back to &name, sizeof(name) or console whatis (:2054-2127). Variable identity is static:<scope:<name or activation:<id:<scope:<name (:2129-2171). prepare_variable_memory preserves GDB's runtime extent and picks aggregate vs scalar read limits (:1719-1736). The actual bytes are read by recorder::capture_variable_memory (src/recorder.rs:45-185). Caller frames capture_caller (src/gdb_mi.rs:1753-1834) never changes GDB's selected frame or thread, records per-caller errors, and assigns separate activation IDs. capture_or_empty in trace.rs keeps a stop even if capture fails (src/trace.rs:2164-2175). Part 5 · Memory, globals, shutdown and failure Function Behavior Location --------- evaluate Runs -data-evaluate-expression src/gdb_mi.rs:1104-1118 read_memory_bytes_partial Validates address/range, returns empty for size zero, runs -data-read-memory-bytes, parses a contiguous prefix with an error :1136-1179 parse_memory_read Combines contiguous segments in address order but never bridges holes (tests at :3330-3390) :1415-1497 capture_global (recorder.rs) Proves static storage for qualified names when possible, evaluates the symbol, and caches only file-qualified globals within a module epoch src/recorder.rs:512-647 shutdown Tries -gdb-exit, waits up to 3 seconds, kills the group on failure, aborts reader tasks, reaps src/gdb_mi.rs:1199-1216 kill The forced path The module epoch advances when library-loaded/unloaded notifications arrive (src/gdb_mi.rs:2418-2421), which invalidates cached globals. Tests and limits src/gdb_mi.rs tests cover: token/async separation, late results, malformed records, bounded frames, recursive caller shadowing, partial memory reads, budget exhaustion, output cap and module epoch (:2494-3732). The MI parser has independent stream/result tests (src/mi_parser.rs:699-1043). These prove implementation branches, not that every C execution reaches every branch. No DWARF location expression is evaluated here; static metadata only qualifies observations. See MI2 parser(engine-mi-deep.html), recorder(engine-recorder-deep.html), stack/memory(engine-stack-deep.html) and failure walkthrough(engine-walkthroughs.html). Diagram notes Diagram What it shows ------ Stop-loop choices<br{{diagram:d2-stop}} Heap ingestion precedes capture; exit, signal, user-code and non-user frames follow different branches. Checkpoint construction<br{{diagram:d2-checkpoint}} A retained frame plus bounded variable/byte capture become one snapshot and source-checkpoint index. MI command lifecycle<br{{diagram:d2-mi-cycle}} Tokened results and asynchronous stops are separate channels.

title: MI2 parser & transport
summary: 25 · GDB/MI2 lexer and record parser In one sentence: MI2 looks like text, but it has a grammar. This parser turns one complete GDB line into typed fields before the engine interprets it. Key terms Term Meaning ------ Lexer The fi
text: 25 · GDB/MI2 lexer and record parser In one sentence: MI2 looks like text, but it has a grammar. This parser turns one complete GDB line into typed fields before the engine interprets it. Key terms Term Meaning ------ Lexer The first pass that splits characters into pieces: numbers, commas, quoted strings, braces. Record One parsed GDB message. ^done is a command result; stopped reports the program stopped. Example. For 4^done,frame={func="main"}, the lexer sees token 4, the result marker and a frame field. The parser builds a structured result for command 4, not a new program stop. A partial or malformed line never becomes a valid frame or a fabricated checkpoint. The big picture src/mi_parser.rs decodes one complete line of GDB's machine interface into a typed MiRecord. - It is not the Trace Parser's JSON reader. It parses debugger protocol syntax before any engine evidence exists. - The caller in src/gdb_mi.rs supplies newline-terminated lines from GDB's stdout. - Malformed input is logged, never converted into a stop. Part 1 · Tokens and typed values Type Location Represents --------- Token src/mi_parser.rs:55-73 An optional numeric command token, MI punctuation (^ = ~ @ & , { } ), a decoded quoted string, or a bare identifier MiValue :80-85 A constant, a tuple of results, or a list MiResult :88-92 A variable=value binding MiListItem :96-99 Distinguishes a plain list value from an inline result MiRecord :117-137 Result, Exec, Notify and Stream { Console \ Target \ Log } variants The parser deliberately preserves unknown record classes and fields instead of discarding them. Protocol extensions stay visible, without the engine inventing an interpretation. Part 2 · Lexing Function Location Job --------- lex_line(input: &u8) - Result<Vec<Token, MiParseError src/mi_parser.rs:361-390 Skips ASCII whitespace, tracks byte offsets for errors, repeatedly applies next_token next_token(input: &u8) - IResult<&u8, Token :340-358 Tries number, quoted string, identifier, then each punctuation token lex_quoted_string :259-329 Decodes C-style escapes lex_ident / lex_number :216-258 MI identifier characters / the decimal command prefix Escapes decoded: \n, \r, \t, \\, \", \', \e, \b, \f, \v, \a, \0, and two-digit \xHH. - An unknown escape degrades to the escaped character. - An unterminated string is an error. The GDB reader adds a separate 16 MiB line bound and UTF-8-lossy conversion before calling parse_line (src/gdb_mi.rs:2302-2323). The parser itself expects a complete line; a partial line must never be parsed as a record. Part 3 · Recursive-descent parsing Signature: pub fn parse_line(line: &str) - Result<Option<MiRecord, MiParseError (src/mi_parser.rs:559-637) Blank lines and (gdb) prompts return Ok(None). Otherwise it lexes, optionally consumes a leading number as the token, then dispatches on the first punctuation: Prefix Produced record ------ ^class,... MiRecord::Result class,... MiRecord::Exec =class,... MiRecord::Notify ~"text" console stream @"text" target stream &"text" log stream The helper functions Function Location Requires / accepts --------- expect_class :639-647 An identifier parse_to_end :665 Zero or more comma-separated result bindings parse_result :474-493 name=value parse_value :428-471 A quoted constant, tuple, list, or bare identifier parse_result_list :496-521 The MI list-of-results comma forms parse_list_items :524-557 Disambiguates name=value from a plain value by looking one token ahead Worked example This is an illustrative MI fragment, not captured output: text 4^done,frame={level="0",func="main",file="main.c",line="7",address="0x401136"} Stage What happens ------ Lexer Produces Number(4), Caret, Ident("done"), Comma, Ident("frame"), Equal, LBrace, then the quoted fields and separators parse_line Consumes the token, emits a Result with token Some(4) and class done, stores a tuple under frame gdb_mi::route_record Sends it only to the pending command 4 A following stopped,reason="end-stepping-range",frame={...} is an Exec record. It is delivered through the asynchronous stop channel and can never acknowledge command 4. Failure behavior and tests MiParseError distinguishes (src/mi_parser.rs:34-53): - unterminated strings, - unexpected tokens, - trailing characters, - unknown records, and - token overflow. The GDB reader logs the line and error in a bounded console buffer and continues. A malformed line never fabricates a frame or a completion. EOF fails all pending commands (src/gdb_mi.rs:2328-2337). Tests cover simple, result, exec, notify and stream records; empty containers; deep nesting; escapes; unknown classes; real GDB transcript fixtures; whitespace; token overflow; and seeded mutations (src/mi_parser.rs:699-1043). They validate syntax preservation. They do not claim GDB produced a particular record in a live session. See the GDB controller(engine-gdb-deep.html) for token routing and stop consumption. Diagram notes Diagram What it shows ------ MI parsing pipeline<br{{diagram:d2-mi-parse}} Lexing, recursive value parsing, typed record classification and caller routing.

title: Recorder & journals
summary: 26 · Recorder, resident accounting, and journal append In one sentence: The recorder is the notebook used during debugging. It appends observations and records where the notebook could not keep up. Key terms Term Plain meaning ---
text: 26 · Recorder, resident accounting, and journal append In one sentence: The recorder is the notebook used during debugging. It appends observations and records where the notebook could not keep up. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Checkpoint A saved view of the program at a particular observed stop, including bounded variables and heap state. Gap An explicitly marked stretch whose exact instruction events were not retained. It is not a guessed list of instructions. Example. If stepping skips a library call, the recorder saves the known stop and a gap marker. It does not invent one event per unknown library instruction. What not to assume: Resident memory, streamed journal bytes and exported JSON have separate accounting and limits. The big picture src/recorder.rs is the engine's write boundary for retained observations. It owns the resident RecordingData, a create-new JSONL Journal, the resident-byte counter, the disassembly cache and per-journal counters. It also performs the bounded stopped-inferior byte reads for variables and configured memory regions. It does not decide when a source checkpoint is semantically warranted; run_gdb_phase does that. Construction and resident accounting Principal type: Recorder { data, config, limits, cache, journal, resident, module_epoch, journaled_allocations } (src/recorder.rs:194-203). Signature: pub fn new(config: &TracingConfig, limits: &ExecutionLimits) - Result<Self (:206-236). It initializes coverage with user-code scope, stop_model="gdb_all_stop", and limitations that explicitly say startup/excluded code is a gap, memory is exact only at its recorded stop, and readable bytes do not establish initialization (:207-220). It opens the optional journal and appends the configuration record before any observation (:221-225). fn reserve(&mut self, size: usize) - Result<() (:251-257) rejects a resident addition above max_trace_memory_bytes. This is resident record accounting, not process RSS and not the JSONL cap. truncate(reason) clears complete_for_scope and appends a de-duplicated reason (:238-249). finish records resident bytes, journal bytes, calls journal.finalize(), and marks incomplete if finalization fails (:461-469). Checkpoints, allocations, gaps and instructions Signatures: - pub fn checkpoint(&mut self, snapshot: &ExecutionSnapshot) - Result<() (src/recorder.rs:259-265) serializes to measure, reserves, journals "checkpoint", then pushes snapshot.step_index into source_checkpoints. - pub fn allocations(&mut self, events: &HeapEvent, stop_id: u64) - Result<() (:267-285) journals only newly seen events, wrapping each as observed_at_stop plus the event. The stop is when the engine noticed the row, not a proven allocation call time. - pub fn gap(&mut self, start: Option<String, end: Option<String, origin: &str, reason: &str) - Result<() (:287-305) creates a TraceGap at the current instruction_count and journals it. - pub fn event(&mut self, event: InstructionEvent) - Result<() (:446-459) reserves/journalizes the attempt, increments instruction_count, and retains the event only if configured. An empty resident array therefore does not imply zero attempts. A checkpoint is an index into the snapshot vector, not a duplicated snapshot object in the journal or final JSON. A gap records an interval of unsupported/unrecorded execution; its unknown instruction count is not guessed. Disassembly cache and module epoch Signature: pub async fn disassemble(&mut self, session: &mut GdbSession, stop: &StoppedInfo) - Result<Option<u64 (src/recorder.rs:307-373). It returns None when static disassembly is disabled. It clears the address-to-instruction_id cache when the session's module epoch changes (:315-318), which prevents a reused address from inheriting instructions from a previous module mapping. A cached address increments disassembly_cache_hits; otherwise it requests a bounded 128-byte window with -data-disassemble -s <addr -e <end -- 2 (:322-335). Each returned asm_insns item becomes a DisassembledInstruction with a new table ID, module identity containing PID/module epoch, raw address, opcodes, text and function (:340-369). Every inserted instruction is reserved, journaled and appended to disassembly_table. The result is the ID for the originally requested address, not an execution claim. The module epoch is advanced by GDB library notifications (src/gdb_mi.rs:2418-2421). Bounded variable and configured-memory reads Signature: pub(crate) async fn capture_variable_memory(session: &mut GdbSession, var: &mut VariableInfo, reads: &mut CheckpointReads, budget: &mut MemoryBudget) (src/recorder.rs:45-185). It first sets initialization_status="unknown", preserves GDB's runtime size when DWARF did not supply it, and creates MemoryEvidence from the requested extent (:51-59). The branches are deliberately distinct: - no address: unavailable; - address but no extent: unknown; - invalid/overflowing range: unknown; - zero extent: full with an empty byte string; - exhausted object/checkpoint/read budget: unattempted with the limiting field; - otherwise chunk reads up to the allowed bytes, reusing CheckpointReads when possible (:60-138). Each chunk is requested through read_memory_bytes_partial; a cached chunk increments saved_memory_reads, while a real read decrements remaining_reads when set (:104-121). A short response or error stops the loop and preserves the prefix. Status becomes full, partial, unreadable, truncated or unattempted according to bytes and failure (:141-176). The raw prefix is stored, the reason/limit recorded, and set_validity derives the variable's validity. Captured bytes do not prove initialization, and a partial read is not a zero-filled object. pub async fn selected_memory(&self, session: &mut GdbSession) - Vec<MemoryObservation (:375-445) handles configured memory_regions. It evaluates each address expression, caps size by per-read and snapshot budgets, and records Valid, Truncated, Unreadable or Unavailable with an error when appropriate. It never silently extends a read past the requested region. capture_global (:512-647) evaluates a named global, proves static storage for qualified names when possible, and caches only file-qualified global metadata within a module epoch. Function-local statics stay on the query path. Globals use identity="symbol:<name"; a file-qualified name is not a runtime activation ID. Outcome classification and tests pub fn event_outcome(before: &StoppedInfo, after: &StoppedInfo) - &'static str (src/recorder.rs:492-510) returns completed only for an observed end-stepping-range; faulted only for a synchronous signal at the same PC; interrupted for another signal; otherwise unknown. A missing after-stop is not completion. Tests cover cap/no-overwrite behavior, torn last records, cache/quota behavior, partial reads and invalid references (src/recorder.rs:656-687; src/gdb_mi.rs:2590-3228). The recorder's journals are ordered evidence, not a reconstructable final trace; see journal/export(engine-export-deep.html). Diagram notes Memory read evidence {{diagram:d2-memory}} A bounded chunked read preserves raw prefix bytes and explicit partial/unreadable status.

title: Frames, variables & memory
summary: 27 · Stack frames, variables, and observed memory In one sentence: This chapter explains why the same local name can refer to different storage in different function calls. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Call frame The debugg
text: 27 · Stack frames, variables, and observed memory In one sentence: This chapter explains why the same local name can refer to different storage in different function calls. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Call frame The debugger's record of one active function call: function name, position, and where it is stopped. Lexical scope The part of a function's source where a declaration is in scope. Two nested blocks may both declare value. Example. In recurse(3) calling recurse(2), both frames can display a local named value. Their activation IDs and observed frame positions keep them apart. What not to assume: A visible name or matching address does not by itself prove two observations refer to one lifetime. The big picture Stopped-state capture answers a narrow question: at this observed GDB stop, what did the selected frame, selected caller frames, globals and bounded byte reads show? It does not reconstruct an object graph or prove that a source declaration was instantiated. src/gdb_mi.rs owns frame/variable extraction; src/recorder.rs performs byte reads; src/memory.rs qualifies addresses and pointer candidates; src/trace.rs assembles snapshots. Frames and activation identity StackFrameInfo is the serialized frame record produced by gdb_mi::frame_from_tuple and parse_frames (src/gdb_mi.rs:1302-1345). capture_state requests at most 200 frames with -stack-list-frames 0 200, marks whether the chain was truncated, and builds an activation path from oldest to youngest (src/gdb_mi.rs:1864-1910). The selected frame is frame zero. Recursive calls with the same function name receive different activation IDs because the path is positional and compared with the prior path; a truncated chain clears continuity rather than reusing a sliding prefix (:1889-1907). A variable's identity is activation:<activation:<scope:<name for locals or static:<scope:<name for static storage (src/gdb_mi.rs:2129-2171). When lexical probing fails, a storage-based identity may include an address, but an unresolved collision becomes unresolved:...; equal names or equal addresses do not establish identity. caller_frames repeat this with separate activation IDs and never change GDB's selected frame (:1753-1834). Recursive C illustration This is a small illustrative input, not a captured trace: c int recurse(int value) { int local = value; return value ? recurse(value - 1) : local; } int main(void) { return recurse(3); } If the engine retained three recursive activations, their frames may all print func="recurse" and a variable named local. The activation IDs distinguish the three recorded frames; a same-name static would use static identity, not an activation. This page does not claim that this example was compiled or run for DOC-2. Variable observation and raw bytes capture_state first obtains -stack-list-variables --all-values, counts duplicate names over the full list, and probes lexical symbols for the configured cap (src/gdb_mi.rs:1914-1947). If a duplicate has multiple lexical declarations, each declaration is retained with its own scope/identity; if association fails, the variable remains an explicit unresolved collision (:1981-2051). For ordinary variables, fresh probe address/size/target data is preferred, with &name, sizeof(name) and console whatis as fallbacks (:2054-2127). prepare_variable_memory preserves the runtime size and selects aggregate vs scalar limits (src/gdb_mi.rs:1719-1736). recorder::capture_variable_memory then reads chunks within the per-object, per-read and checkpoint budgets, retaining a raw-byte prefix plus MemoryEvidence (src/recorder.rs:45-185). A short read is a prefix, not a zero-filled or initialized object. set_validity marks the variable's bytes status, and initialization_status remains unknown. Process maps and pointer candidates Signatures: pub fn address(text: &str) - Option<u64, pub fn storage_region(pid: u32, addr: u64) - Option<&'static str and pub fn executable_bias(binary: &Path, pid: u32) - Option<u64 (src/memory.rs:5-100). storage_region reads /proc/<pid/maps and returns stack, heap, code or another mapping class. executable_bias compares the ELF's load addresses with the observed mapping to subtract relocation bias. These are process observations at capture time, not C type facts. Signature: pub fn enrich_snapshot(snapshot: &mut ExecutionSnapshot, timeline: &HeapTimeline, pid: Option<u32) (src/memory.rs:145-205). It builds the set of observed objects from frame-zero variables, globals, and caller variables only when the caller's retained frame is on this snapshot's call stack and its activation matches (:162-187). It then computes pointer targets without cloning variable/value/byte buffers. A target can be null, a heap address candidate, a stack/global containing object, or unresolved. pointer_target (:260-340) treats points_to == 0 as null. For a heap address, it asks the timeline for all address candidates and uses the newest only as an address match; multiple historical occupants yield ambiguous_reuse, a freed block yields known_freed_address, and otherwise address_only. It records base, offset and within-extent, but allocation_id is not pointer provenance. For non-heap addresses, it finds a containing observed object; recursive statics are deduplicated only with identical identity and extent, never by name or address alone (:299-315). Reconciliation after the run refresh_heap_targets (src/memory.rs:212-249) runs after terminal transport verification. It widens local heap IDs when multiple PIDs were observed, but does not resolve a historical pointer through later frees/reallocs/reuse. If history is incomplete it sets active=None, allocation_id=None and provenance_status="history_incomplete". This preserves the distinction between what was observed while stopped and what the final timeline later knew. Snapshot assembly and failure push_snapshot (src/trace.rs:2179-2304) checks max_snapshot_count, computes remaining memory budget after variable reads, reads alive observed heap blocks up to max_heap_blocks_per_snapshot, captures a bounded stdout head, and appends an ExecutionSnapshot with step_index, stop/frame metadata, call stack, variables, caller frames, heap blocks and program output. capture_or_empty preserves a stop even if capture_state fails (src/trace.rs:2164-2175). Missing frame, metadata, read or budget produces explicit partial state; no fabricated values are inserted. Tests and boundaries Tests cover truncated recursive chains, caller shadowing, partial/unreadable memory, quota accounting, module changes and pointer candidate ambiguity (src/gdb_mi.rs:2590-3228; src/memory.rs:363-943). Static DWARF can supply a type or fallback extent, but GDB remains authoritative for the stopped value; captured bytes do not establish initialization. See GDB capture(engine-gdb-deep.html), recorder(engine-recorder-deep.html) and identity contracts(identity-contracts.html). Diagram notes Frame and activation identity {{diagram:d2-frame}} Recursive activations remain distinct even when function and variable names repeat. Capture scope and invalidation {{diagram:d2-cache}} Module epochs and stop-local reuse prevent stale live observations; static metadata is separate.

title: DWARF extraction
summary: 28 · GCC DWARF extraction and observation association In one sentence: DWARF is the compiler's description of the finished executable. This page explains how that description becomes trace-local type and declaration entries. Key t
text: 28 · GCC DWARF extraction and observation association In one sentence: DWARF is the compiler's description of the finished executable. This page explains how that description becomes trace-local type and declaration entries. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ ELF The executable file format of the debug program; DWARF sections live inside it. DIE A debug-information entry: one DWARF record for something such as a type, variable or member. Example. A GCC-produced struct entry can say that member count starts four bytes into the struct. It cannot say that a particular stopped instance's bytes were initialized. What not to assume: Missing or compiler-dependent DWARF facts stay missing; the engine should not replace them with a guessed textbook layout. The big picture src/dwarf.rs reads compiled metadata from the actual GCC debug executable, not the original C text or a GDB location expression. The registry belongs to one trace; its DIE identifiers are not runtime object identities. trace_program calls extract_excluding(&debug_build.binary_path, &tracker_source) after successful compilation, rejects a registry with no project CU, constructs an Arc<ObservationTypes for stop capture, and finally calls associate(&mut trace) after capture (trace.rs:351-366(../../src/trace.rsL351-L366), trace.rs:423-439(../../src/trace.rsL423-L439), trace.rs:944-955(../../src/trace.rsL944-L955), trace.rs:2728-2760(../../src/trace.rsL2728-L2760)). See AST extraction(engine-ast-deep.html) and fusion(engine-fusion-deep.html) for the other two static-evidence steps. The registry and its identities TypeRegistry holds provider/artifact, retained UnitInfo CUs, TypeEntry types, Declaration records, counters and limitations; compilation_units_scanned also counts excluded CUs. UnitInfo records CU name, compilation directory, DWARF version and address size. A type has a CU ID, DIE offset, kind, size/encoding, optional referenced type, members, dimensions and enumerators; a declaration has a kind, source file/line/column, containing function, lexical scope_id, optional type and origin explanation (dwarf.rs:26-124(../../src/dwarf.rsL26-L124)). debug:u<absolute-CU-header-offset and debug:u...:o<unit-relative-DIE-offset are generated during the two scans; these distinguish identically named types and statics in different translation units (dwarf.rs:535-574(../../src/dwarf.rsL535-L574), dwarf.rs:625-647(../../src/dwarf.rsL625-L647), tests/dwarf_registry.rs:169-214(../../tests/dwarf_registry.rsL169-L214)). A declaration's scope_id comes from the parent DIE stack, not from its name; shadowed value declarations retain distinct lexical parents (dwarf.rs:632-647(../../src/dwarf.rsL632-L647), dwarf.rs:775-818(../../src/dwarf.rsL775-L818), tests/dwarf_registry.rs:151-167(../../tests/dwarf_registry.rsL151-L167)). ELF sections and the two DIE passes extract(path: &Path) and extract_excluding(path: &Path, instrumentation_source: &Path) return Result<(TypeRegistry, ExtractionMetrics), String through extract_impl; the latter excludes only a CU whose recorded name is the exact injected source path, not a user file sharing its basename (dwarf.rs:577-631(../../src/dwarf.rsL577-L631)). load_dwarf checks the object is at most 64 MiB and has .debug_info or .zdebug_info, parses it with object::File, takes the object's endianness, locates normal or legacy compressed sections, caps aggregate decoded section bytes before decompressing, and gives gimli EndianRcSlices backed by owned Rc bytes. No borrowed object-file buffer escapes this reader boundary (dwarf.rs:478-533(../../src/dwarf.rsL478-L533)). index_dies(&Dwarf<R, Instant) first traverses CU headers and all DIEs with next_dfs, recording every absolute .debug_info DIE offset as a CU-qualified key. This supports forward and cross-CU DebugInfoRefs; at most 512 units, 150,000 DIEs and five seconds are accepted (dwarf.rs:15-24(../../src/dwarf.rsL15-L24), dwarf.rs:535-575(../../src/dwarf.rsL535-L575)). extract_impl reopens the unit iterator without reloading sections; OriginResolver caches parsed units by absolute header offset, while a depth-indexed parent stack supplies the current aggregate, function and lexical scope. It retains recognized type tags and variable, parameter and subprogram declarations, counting otherwise unsupported DIE tags rather than promoting them to known facts (dwarf.rs:603-681(../../src/dwarf.rsL603-L681), dwarf.rs:775-819(../../src/dwarf.rsL775-L819)). Subprogram DIEs serve source-level function correlation but are excluded from runtime variable matching (dwarf.rs:782-810(../../src/dwarf.rsL782-L810), dwarf.rs:1052-1068(../../src/dwarf.rsL1052-L1068)). Specification and abstract-origin chains OriginResolver::resolve starts with attributes on the concrete DIE, follows DW_AT_specification preferentially or DW_AT_abstract_origin, and fills only missing name, source file, line, column and type from each referenced DIE. UnitRef stays in the current CU; absolute DebugInfoRef uses the DIE index to find the owning CU header, converts to a unit offset and loads that entry. The visited key is (absolute CU-header offset, unit DIE offset); four hops maximum, a cycle, an unsupported form or a missing target marks the chain failed. Cross-CU and same-CU hop descriptions are retained when supplemental facts were actually used; unsuccessful chains increment unresolved_origin_references and remain limitations, not file/line guesses (dwarf.rs:181-211(../../src/dwarf.rsL181-L211), dwarf.rs:213-423(../../src/dwarf.rsL213-L423), dwarf.rs:648-657(../../src/dwarf.rsL648-L657), dwarf.rs:859-863(../../src/dwarf.rsL859-L863)). source_file resolves the DIE's line-table file through directory and CU compilation directory, canonicalizing if possible; absolute_source_path instead requires an absolute path for qualified-symbol identity, with lexical normalization if the file moved (dwarf.rs:424-476(../../src/dwarf.rsL424-L476)). A real GCC -O2 -gdwarf-5 -flto test exercises cross-CU abstract origins and checks filled source attributes (tests/dwarf_registry.rs:271-310(../../tests/dwarf_registry.rsL271-L310)). Layout is metadata, not a memory read type_kind recognizes base, pointer, array, struct, union, enum, typedef, qualifiers, function and unspecified DIEs. TypeEntry.byte_size comes from DW_AT_byte_size, except pointer size can use the CU address size; DW_AT_type resolves only UnitRef or indexed DebugInfoRef (dwarf.rs:163-191(../../src/dwarf.rsL163-L191), dwarf.rs:678-701(../../src/dwarf.rsL678-L701)). For struct/union children, Member preserves numeric byte offset, bit size, DW_AT_data_bit_offset and legacy storage-relative DW_AT_bit_offset separately. Missing union location yields an explicitly marked implicit zero; an unhandled member-location expression makes the parent runtime_dependent instead of calculating an offset (dwarf.rs:73-88(../../src/dwarf.rsL73-L88), dwarf.rs:702-728(../../src/dwarf.rsL702-L728)). Array subranges store signed bounds and numeric count (or derive it from ordered bounds); C's default lower bound is zero. A nonnumeric bound/count sets runtime_dependent, while missing static information is unavailable. Enumerators retain signed or unsigned constants, including negative values (dwarf.rs:729-774(../../src/dwarf.rsL729-L774)). The second resolution pass clears any type/member/declaration reference absent from the retained type set and records the count; excluded-CU references therefore do not masquerade as valid types (dwarf.rs:820-874(../../src/dwarf.rsL820-L874)). The real-GCC layout test covers bit offsets, union zero offsets, enums, multidimensional arrays and VLAs (tests/dwarf_registry.rs:36-149(../../tests/dwarf_registry.rsL36-L149)); none of these fields identifies an active union member or proves initialization. Linking stopped variables without guessing The immutable, trace-local ObservationTypes::new(&TypeRegistry) builds location and qualified-symbol lookups before GDB runs. It skips declaration-only and subprogram DIEs, follows at most 64 typedef/qualifier links to find size/aggregate/pointer shape, and withholds size on missing, cyclic or runtime-dependent paths (dwarf.rs:876-971(../../src/dwarf.rsL876-L971)). At each stop gdb_mi::prepare_variable_memory preserves GDB's original size in runtime_size_bytes, calls enrich(&mut VariableInfo, func), and selects the aggregate memory-read budget; requested globals also pass this lookup to recorder::capture_global (gdb_mi.rs:1719-1736(../../src/gdb_mi.rsL1719-L1736), recorder.rs:629-646(../../src/recorder.rsL629-L646)). enrich accepts one compatible (declaration_file, declaration_line, variable name) candidate with matching function. The alternate symbol route is only for GDB-qualified names without a declaration line: a quoted file qualifier must normalize to the same full absolute path; bare names and ambiguous location hits cannot fall back to a guessed symbol. A unique match sets type_ref/declaration_ref and missing location fields; DWARF size is a fallback only if an address exists and GDB supplied no size. It returns aggregate shape for the capture budget; is_pointer reports known pointer shape, not pointee extent (dwarf.rs:973-1040(../../src/dwarf.rsL973-L1040), tests/dwarf_registry.rs:379-529(../../tests/dwarf_registry.rsL379-L529)). After capture, associate(&mut DebugSessionTrace) - u64 makes a separate conservative pass over top-frame variables, caller-frame variables and globals, requiring exact file/line/name, compatible function, valid type and exactly one declaration; it attaches only the two DWARF IDs (dwarf.rs:1042-1105(../../src/dwarf.rsL1042-L1105)). The synthetic ambiguity test leaves both IDs absent and preserves observed values (tests/dwarf_registry.rs:312-377(../../tests/dwarf_registry.rsL312-L377)); the stop-time test preserves a runtime size over the static fallback (dwarf.rs:1157-1187(../../src/dwarf.rsL1157-L1187)). Failure and scope Missing debug sections, invalid/oversized objects, traversal/retention limits, deadline expiration and zero eligible units return an error rather than a plausible empty registry; trace_program retains the runtime trace and adds an analysis note instead (dwarf.rs:480-490(../../src/dwarf.rsL480-L490), dwarf.rs:545-567(../../src/dwarf.rsL545-L567), dwarf.rs:870-874(../../src/dwarf.rsL870-L874), trace.rs:353-367(../../src/trace.rsL353-L367), tests/dwarf_registry.rs:573-597(../../tests/dwarf_registry.rsL573-L597)). Unsupported tags, unresolved references and dynamic layout expressions remain explicit partial metadata. DWARF is compiled layout/declaration evidence; GDB observation remains the authority for stopped-state bytes, values, extents and execution. See metadata overview(engine-metadata.html) and evidence boundaries(identity-contracts.html). Diagram notes DWARF extraction flow {{diagram:d2-dwarf}} Object loading, CU/DIE scans, bounded reference resolution and conservative observation association. Origin/reference resolution {{diagram:d2-origin}} Cross-CU references are followed through indexed DIE offsets with a four-hop and cycle bound.
