title: Clang AST provider
summary: 29 · Optional Clang source-syntax extraction In one sentence: Clang's AST describes what the source code says. It is useful for navigation, but its expressions are not an execution log. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ AST Abst
text: 29 · Optional Clang source-syntax extraction In one sentence: Clang's AST describes what the source code says. It is useful for navigation, but its expressions are not an execution log. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ AST Abstract syntax tree: a structured version of source constructs such as function calls, declarations and fields. Source span The file and character range where Clang located a written construct. Example. If the source contains if (0) malloc(40);, Clang can still find the malloc expression. The debugger may never execute it. What not to assume: Macros, flags and same-line calls can make a source-to-event match ambiguous. Keep candidates visibly different from confirmed events. The big picture src/clang_ast.rs is an opt-in, bounded second compiler's syntax view. trace_program invokes analyze(&BuildConfig, clang_path, Option<&TypeRegistry) only when config.clang_ast is true and time remains; it stores one session-level SourceMetadataRegistry, including per-translation-unit failure reasons, without withholding GDB execution when Clang fails (trace.rs:368-391(../../src/trace.rsL368-L391)). GCC DWARF and GDB retain layout and runtime authority; see DWARF extraction(engine-dwarf-deep.html) and fusion(engine-fusion-deep.html). Registry, spans and trace-local IDs SourceMetadataRegistry owns provider/version, cross-provider incompatibility reason, AstUnit statuses, source declarations/expressions, heap-call candidates and ambiguities, timing and limitations. SourceDeclaration records kind/name/type spelling, name position, function and optional initializer-expression ID; SourceExpression records kind/span/type/operator, access syntax, callee/classification, operand IDs, declaration references and sizeof operand. Optional DWARF IDs, type evidence and DwarfMemberRef are links, not C execution evidence (clang_ast.rs:22-163(../../src/clang_ast.rsL22-L163)). SourceSpan uses source byte offsets, line/column and direct versus macro_expansion provenance, with optional spelling location. Neither source ID (tu0:d..., tu0:e...) nor Clang's raw node ID is a runtime activation ID: extract assigns serial IDs in retained traversal order, then resolves temporary raw IDs into these serialized references (clang_ast.rs:86-163(../../src/clang_ast.rsL86-L163), clang_ast.rs:578-586(../../src/clang_ast.rsL578-L586), clang_ast.rs:646-706(../../src/clang_ast.rsL646-L706), clang_ast.rs:800-813(../../src/clang_ast.rsL800-L813)). Repeated analysis on the test fixture checks stable (ID, kind, start offset) triples (tests/clang_ast.rs:251-289(../../tests/clang_ast.rsL251-L289)). Invocation and option fidelity clang_flags(&BuildConfig) - Result<Vec<String, String forwards build definitions/includes and classified compiler options in order: language mode, preprocessing/include flags, -f/-m/-pthread, and supported optimization levels; it drops -g and warnings, but rejects unclassified flags and missing option arguments rather than silently analyzing a different preprocessed program (clang_ast.rs:178-225(../../src/clang_ast.rsL178-L225)). Clang receives -Xclang -ast-dump=json -fsyntax-only -x c -O0, then the forwarded flags and user source. The -O0 baseline plus user optimization order matters for macros such as __OPTIMIZE__; the GCC/Clang fixture independently checks that -O2 chooses optimized_branch (clang_ast.rs:290-301(../../src/clang_ast.rsL290-L301), tests/clang_ast.rs:15-79(../../tests/clang_ast.rsL15-L79)). Accepted compiler-specific -f, -m or -pthread can still mean different things to GCC and Clang: analyze retains syntax but sets cross_provider_correlation_unavailable, withholding DWARF correlation; fusion also honors this gate (clang_ast.rs:248-256(../../src/clang_ast.rsL248-L256), clang_ast.rs:386-390(../../src/clang_ast.rsL386-L390), tests/clang_ast.rs:556-597(../../tests/clang_ast.rsL556-L597)). Acceptance is not proof of semantic equivalence. analyze uses build.user_sources() rather than the generated wrapper and analyzes at most 16 TUs in canonical path order, with an eight-second shared budget, per-Clang three-second deadline, tool-only 512 MiB best-effort memory limit, 1 MiB input source and 8 MiB output cap. Supervisor cancellation, timeout, truncated output, nonzero Clang status or warnings that a configured argument was unused/unsupported make that TU unavailable; malformed JSON does too (clang_ast.rs:228-390(../../src/clang_ast.rsL228-L390)). An extraction failure after some records are retained marks the unit partial, while unsupported expression nodes also mark partial with children retained; the unit reports byte, node, parse and registry timings. A failed Clang binary still leaves a compiled runtime trace (tests/clang_ast.rs:438-506(../../tests/clang_ast.rsL438-L506)). JSON traversal and conservative source ranges span(node, path, &LineIndex) computes byte-based positions from Clang expansion offsets and token lengths, rejects zero/out-of-range spans and included-header or foreign-file locations, and records spelling location separately for macros. LineIndex::line_column derives line/column from the source bytes instead of trusting a foreign file's position (clang_ast.rs:397-488(../../src/clang_ast.rsL397-L488)). extract(&Value, &Path, &u8, unit_id, &mut AstUnit, &mut SourceMetadataRegistry, deadline) - Result<(), String walks inner nodes with an explicit depth/function/record stack, bounded to 100,000 nodes and depth 96; skipped header spans are not traversed into user records (clang_ast.rs:14-20(../../src/clang_ast.rsL14-L20), clang_ast.rs:560-636(../../src/clang_ast.rsL560-L636)). It retains VarDecl, ParmVarDecl, FunctionDecl, FieldDecl and selected calls, operators, subscripts, members, casts, conditionals, declaration references and literals, with limits of 2,048 declarations and 4,096 expressions. An unrecognized expression/operator/literal increments unsupported_nodes; unsupported wrapper nodes may still expose supported children. visible_child_ids traverses at most 64 descendant nodes through nonselected wrappers, and a deferred pass resolves operand IDs, referenced declarations and initializer IDs only if retained (clang_ast.rs:490-558(../../src/clang_ast.rsL490-L558), clang_ast.rs:637-813(../../src/clang_ast.rsL637-L813)). direct_callee follows at most eight first-child wrappers to a DeclRefExpr; malloc/calloc/realloc/free is classified as a standard allocator only if that declaration ID was observed among header FunctionDecls. Otherwise calls are direct_other or indirect_or_unknown, not inferred from spelling alone. MemberExpr preserves dot/arrow syntax, base type spelling and member name; sizeof preserves whether its argument is a type or expression (clang_ast.rs:504-537(../../src/clang_ast.rsL504-L537), clang_ast.rs:569-575(../../src/clang_ast.rsL569-L575), clang_ast.rs:700-794(../../src/clang_ast.rsL700-L794)). The GNU-expression fixture verifies partial extraction rather than false completeness (tests/clang_ast.rs:508-524(../../tests/clang_ast.rsL508-L524)). Declaration matching against GCC When DWARF exists and the provider gate permits it, correlate_declarations indexes DWARF declarations by canonical (file, line, column, name, function) and a separate line-only key. FunctionDecl matches subprogram, VarDecl/ParmVarDecl match variable/parameter; FieldDecl is deliberately left for the parent-type/member resolver in fusion(engine-fusion-deep.html). It selects one compatible exact-position DIE, preferring a declaration-only subprogram DIE over a definition. A fallback to one line match is allowed only when at least one side lacks a column, never when two present columns disagree. Zero or multiple results remain unresolved or ambiguous; a type link is kept only if the matched type ID exists in the registry (clang_ast.rs:816-945(../../src/clang_ast.rsL816-L945), clang_ast.rs:386-390(../../src/clang_ast.rsL386-L390)). Focused tests cover duplicate exact matches, missing-column fallback, fields and function declaration preference (clang_ast.rs:1087-1153(../../src/clang_ast.rsL1087-L1153), clang_ast.rs:1210-1275(../../src/clang_ast.rsL1210-L1275)). This is a static location correlation, not proof that a declaration was instantiated at a stop. Heap calls are source-line candidates correlate_heap_calls(&mut SourceMetadataRegistry, &HeapEvent, &Path) clears prior candidates/ambiguities, indexes calls by canonical file and every covered line up to start+64, with separate direct/macro buckets. Only events whose attribution says resolved_return_address_minus_one and have source file/line qualify; operation must match (malloc/calloc with allocation, realloc with reallocation, free with free). One direct compatible call with no compatible macro call yields unique_direct_call_on_resolved_line_not_exact_execution; multiple calls or macro-only calls yield explicit ambiguity (at most eight displayed expression IDs). Empty match stays empty; cancellation or 250 ms stops the event loop with a limitation (clang_ast.rs:947-1054(../../src/clang_ast.rsL947-L1054)). The real mixed direct/macro free test demonstrates why one return-address line cannot choose a particular call (tests/clang_ast.rs:190-249(../../tests/clang_ast.rsL190-L249)); synthetic tests distinguish one candidate, multiple calls, macro-only and the eight-ID cap (tests/evidence_fusion.rs:355-440(../../tests/evidence_fusion.rsL355-L440)). No call candidate supplies runtime argument values, allocation identity or expression execution. See heap instrumentation(engine-heap.html) and evidence constraints(identity-contracts.html). Diagram notes Clang AST pipeline {{diagram:d2-ast}} Optional bounded Clang syntax extraction is retained independently of GCC/GDB runtime evidence. Syntax versus runtime {{diagram:d2-ast-runtime}} A source expression or declaration link is not proof that a particular dynamic call executed.

title: C allocator runtime
summary: 30 · C allocator runtime: interception and transport In one sentence: This is the implementation of the C allocation detour. Its job is to record calls it intercepts without changing what the allocator returns. Key terms Term Plai
text: 30 · C allocator runtime: interception and transport In one sentence: This is the implementation of the C allocation detour. Its job is to record calls it intercepts without changing what the allocator returns. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ --wrap A linker feature that routes a linked malloc call to __wrap_malloc; the wrapper calls __real_malloc after recording it. Event ACK A separate end-of-process status line giving the last event number and failed-write count, when normal shutdown permits it. Example. The program calls malloc(24). The wrapper calls the real allocator once, assigns an ID if it can track the result, and writes a PID/sequence-tagged line to its own file. Rust later reads that file. What not to assume: A missing final ACK, a torn write or a silent fork child lowers certainty. The wrapper does not intercept every internal library allocator. The big picture The debug executable links c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c through linker --wrap references to malloc, calloc, realloc, and free. It records operations actually intercepted by the linked executable, not every allocation in the process. src/allocation_tracker.rs::ALLOC_RUNTIME_C embeds this translation unit and write_runtime_source(session_dir: &Path) - Result<PathBuf writes it into the session directory (src/allocation_tracker.rs:30-38). trace_program_inner(config: TraceConfig) - Result<DebugSessionTrace hands that file to compiler::compile_project (src/trace.rs:167,226-237); run_gdb_phase(...) supplies the event and status paths in the inferior environment (src/trace.rs:1113-1124,1171-1189). For reconstruction and the meaning of verified history, see Heap timeline(engine-heap-deep.html); for other executions, see Independent diagnostics(engine-diagnostics-deep.html). Source file: c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c Lifecycle, lock and table cte_init(void) is constructor priority 101 (c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c:293-317). An absent/empty C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE or failed event-file open leaves g_fd=-1: wrappers pass through. Otherwise it opens the event file append-only with mode 0600, optionally opens the independent C_TRACE_EVENT_STATUS_FILE the same way, and registers pthread_atfork(NULL, NULL, cte_after_fork_child). Registration failure closes the descriptors and disables instrumentation. The status-file open can fail independently: events can still be written, but there can be no valid terminal ACK. cte_fini(void) (:319-337) attempts the status line only if both descriptors are valid, on normal destructor execution, then closes them. _exit, a crash, or a killed process need not run it. State is process-local static storage: g_table has CTE_TABLE_SLOTS=1<<17 entries, each {addr,id,size} with address zero marking an empty slot; g_seq and g_ids count emitted attempts and issued allocation IDs respectively; g_write_failures counts failed event emissions (:64-82). static unsigned long cte_hash(unsigned long x) (:161-169) mixes address bits. static cte_slot cte_find(unsigned long addr) probes linearly until an empty cell or match (:171-181). static int cte_insert(unsigned long addr, unsigned long id, unsigned long size) finds an empty cell or returns zero when full (:183-196); the wrapper still emits the event on overflow. static void cte_remove(unsigned long addr) clears the matching cell and reinserts the following cluster so searches do not stop too early; there are no tombstones (:198-218). The Rust timeline can match an unindexed predecessor by (pid,address), but neither table overflow nor address equality establishes pointer provenance. cte_lock(void) and cte_unlock(void) (:108-126) use a test-and-set spinlock around real allocator calls, table changes, ID/sequence updates and writes. g_busy is a thread-local reentry guard: allocation inside tracking calls the real allocator without another event. cte_after_fork_child(void) (:136-143) atomically releases the inherited lock, resets counters, and sets g_child_reset; the child's first lock clears its inherited address table (:117-120). Clearing is deferred out of the child callback. No prepare/parent lock is taken across foreign atfork handlers. Forking inside an allocator or a foreign handler that later acquires the lock is unsupported; the wrapper cannot make libc allocation after a multithreaded fork generally safe (:128-135). CTE_TESTING enables fault/lock hooks only in test builds (:84-97,145-154), not in production. Wrappers and state transitions Each wrapper passes through if g_busy or g_fd<0, otherwise sets the guard, captures __builtin_return_address(0), locks, calls the corresponding __real_ once, saves errno, emits an event, adjusts the table, unlocks, restores errno, and returns the real result. The captured PC is a return address, not intrinsically a verified source expression; tail calls/inlining can make it unreliable (:41-47,343-467). Qualified C signature Branch and ownership result ------ void __wrap_malloc(size_t size) (:343-361) Issues a local ID even on NULL; emits ok or failed, inserting {address,id,size} only for non-NULL. void __wrap_calloc(size_t nmemb, size_t size) (:363-385) Calls real calloc with original operands. Computes nmembsize only if representable; on overflow records byte size 0, status overflow, and both original operands. Otherwise records ok or failed, inserts only non-NULL. A zero-size successful allocation can have size zero and a real nonzero address. void __wrap_realloc(void ptr, size_t size) (:387-443) Looks up the old address before calling real realloc under the same lock. ptr==NULL: fresh ID, new or failed. Same returned address: fresh ID, ok_same if table-held or new if predecessor untracked; replace/insert table entry. Non-NULL moved result: fresh ID, ok_moved, remove old and insert new. NULL with non-NULL old pointer and size==0: zero, old ID, remove old (glibc contract used here). NULL with nonzero size: failed, old ID, leave original entry intact. IDs are new for successful in-place as well as moving realloc, not merely for address changes. void __wrap_free(void ptr) (:445-467) Looks up address and size, calls real free, emits ok for table-held, unknown for non-NULL untracked, or null for NULL; removes only a tracked entry. ID zero marks missing table identity. Calling free on an invalid pointer remains the C program's undefined behavior; logging is not a safety mechanism. The table maps addresses, not ownership of pointers. A later successful allocation can reuse a freed numeric address with a different lifetime ID. If the C table filled, a free unknown or a realloc with old_id=0 can still be paired with a live observed address by Rust, provided its history is reliable (reconstruction(engine-heap-deep.htmlsource-file-src-allocation-tracker-rs)). Internal allocations inside unwrapped shared libraries, custom allocators, and strdup internals are not intercepted (:41-46). Event rows, partial writes and terminal ACK static void cte_emit_locked(const char kind, unsigned long id, unsigned long addr, unsigned long size, unsigned long old_id, unsigned long old_addr, unsigned long caller, const char status, unsigned long nmemb, unsigned long element_size) increments g_seq, formats a line into a 320-byte stack buffer, and calls cte_write_all (:265-287). Decimal fields are pid seq id size old_id and, for calloc only, nmemb element_size; hexadecimal without 0x fields are addr old_addr caller. The 10-field format is pid seq kind id addr size old_id old_addr caller status; calloc appends two operands for 12 fields (:9-25,273-281). Status values actually emitted include overflow as well as ok, failed, ok_same, ok_moved, new, zero, null, unknown (:343-467); the introductory C comment's status list omits overflow, but the code and Rust reader include it. The following is illustrative, not captured output. The first row could represent an intercepted 24-byte malloc in PID 100; the second a free of that tracked address. The separate ACK reports the last issued sequence and zero failed writes: text alloc_events.txt (illustrative; comments are not part of the actual file) 100 1 malloc 1 1000 24 0 0 4011b6 ok 100 2 free 1 1000 24 0 0 4011d0 ok alloc_event_status.txt (illustrative) 100 2 0 static int cte_write_all(int fd, const char buf, size_t len, int event) retries short writes, retries EINTR at most eight times, and fails on zero write or any other error (:224-263). No rollback of bytes already appended is possible: a partially written row may be completed by a later append and must not be trusted merely because it has a newline. cte_emit_locked increments g_write_failures (saturating at ULONG_MAX) for a failed/oversized emission (:282-286); the destructor writes pid seq write_failures\n through the separate status descriptor (:322-330). The reader verifies ACKs against observed sequences and the followed inferior; a clean-looking prefix cannot prove a failed last event did not exist. A missing ACK, nonzero failure count or wrong sequence downgrades completeness, rather than erasing observed rows (verification(engine-heap-deep.htmltransport-and-coverage)). Neither transport nor ACK authenticates files against hostile modification. Tests and boundaries tests/heap_instrumentation.rs:152-334 compiles real wrapped C fixtures: normal ACK, PID-local child restart and lock-holder fork, multithread serialization, partial/EINTR retry, terminal EIO/zero/repeated-EINTR/partial-then-error, missing/failed ACK and failed status-file open. The terminal-write test feeds actual C files to EventFileReader and verify_event_status, demonstrating why a contiguous prefix alone is insufficient (:261-305). The later release closure(../trace-engine-v2.2-release-closure.mdfork-child-heap-history-contract) documents observed, silent and unacknowledged children; a silent child with no event/ACK is not discoverable. This is Linux/GCC/glibc-oriented instrumentation on a 64-bit unsigned long target (c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c:55-58), not an all-allocator, all-libc or all-process census. Diagram notes Allocator wrapper sequence {{diagram:d2-wrapper}} A linked wrapper calls the real allocator once, updates a fixed table and appends a PID-local event. Event and ACK transport {{diagram:d2-transport}} The C runtime writes a dedicated event file and separate terminal status; Rust consumes complete rows and checks ACKs. Fork and PID scope {{diagram:d2-fork}} A child resets inherited allocator state; an unlogged silent descendant remains unknown to the Rust reader.

title: Heap reconstruction
summary: 31 · Heap event reader and lifetime reconstruction In one sentence: This Rust code turns individual wrapper log lines into an ordered account of allocation lifetimes. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Event tailer A reader that
text: 31 · Heap event reader and lifetime reconstruction In one sentence: This Rust code turns individual wrapper log lines into an ordered account of allocation lifetimes. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Event tailer A reader that takes new, complete lines from the event file rather than rereading all of it as a new history. Heap timeline The accumulated view of which tracked block was created, resized, freed or still observed. Example. An allocated event starts ID 1. A later free closes ID 1. A new allocation can reuse the same address but must become ID 2; the timeline does not merge them. What not to assume: Missing lines or process acknowledgements mean the timeline has an observed prefix, not necessarily complete history. The big picture The C wrapper produces PID-local allocation telemetry; Rust owns incremental input, checked sequence history, block lifetimes and final serialization. Read the C runtime(engine-allocator-deep.html) for when a row is emitted and independent diagnostics(engine-diagnostics-deep.html) for why a Valgrind error is not a primary-run allocation event. The GDB-followed inferior's snapshots and events from other processes have different observation scopes. Source file: src/allocation_tracker.rs Parsing and incremental input parse_event_line(line: &str) - Result<RawEvent (src/allocation_tracker.rs:82-160) accepts exactly 10 whitespace-separated fields, or 12 only for calloc. It parses PID as u32, sequence/IDs/size/calloc operands as decimal u64, and addresses/caller as hexadecimal u64; unknown kind/status, malformed numbers, out-of-range PID and wrong field count yield EngineError::AllocationEventParse. RawEvent retains PID, sequence, kind/status, old and new IDs/addresses, caller PC and optional calloc operands (:44-80). A syntactically valid row is not by itself proof of a complete event stream. EventFileReader::new(path: PathBuf) - Self and EventFileReader::read_new(&mut self) - Vec<RawEvent (:262-275,293-400) track file offset, partial bytes, parse-error count and first 50 messages. Each call opens the event file, checks loss after prior observations (disappearance, smaller size, Unix device/inode replacement, seek/read failure), then reads at most 1 MiB plus a sentinel byte. Exceeding that per-stop cap keeps the bounded prefix but permanently quarantines subsequent input. Only newline-terminated lines parse; an unfinished tail up to 4096 bytes is buffered without rereading it from disk, and a larger line is rejected. incomplete_line(&self) - bool reports a pending/oversized tail; transport_damaged(&self) - bool reports definitive malformed/oversized/truncated input (:277-284). A short line can still be in flight at one stop; a trailing partial line at the final read means incomplete history. This reader is bounded, not a general-purpose recovery protocol for torn writes. Ordered timeline and ownership HeapTimeline::new(limits_max_blocks: usize) - Self sets a block cap and an event-retention cap of four times that value (:431-486). HeapTimeline::ingest(&mut self, ev: &RawEvent) (:521-756) uses (pid,id) and (pid,address) for live lookup. Per-PID sequences must begin at 1 and increase by one. Duplicates or out-of-order rows are counted but not ingested as state transitions; a gap is counted/recorded (up to 50 gap details) and marks that PID incomplete (:523-566). Malformed transport quarantines all PIDs, including future first-seen PIDs; after a PID gap it still retains subsequent raw-derived event records but no longer infers block changes for that PID. history_complete(&self) - bool and is_pid_complete(&self, pid: u32) - bool also reflect transport/retention limits (:501-519). On a reliable prefix, successful malloc/calloc calls add_block(&mut self, ev: &RawEvent, alloc_type: &'static str, realloc_from: Option<u64), which rejects zero IDs/addresses, repeated IDs, overlapping live base addresses or exhausted block retention (:583-604,768-808). Overflow calloc is an AllocationFailed event with unknown byte size, preserving both operands; failed allocation creates no block. retire_block(&mut self, idx: usize, seq: u64) marks the block freed, stores its free sequence and subtracts live bytes (:758-766). push_event(&mut self, event_type: HeapEventType, ev: &RawEvent, detail: Option<String) records the per-PID usage, raw caller and completeness qualification until the event cap (:810-855). Per-PID usage is an observed ledger, not total OS heap consumption. realloc behavior is branch-specific (:606-699). new from NULL starts a block. An untracked predecessor that returns the same address is also new: if Rust has a live block for that PID/address (for example, C table overflow), it retires/links the observed predecessor; otherwise it starts at the first observed block. ok_same retires the old block and creates a linked new lifetime under the current wrapper's fresh ID; historical input using the old ID simply resizes its existing lifetime. ok_moved retires the address/ID-matched old block and links the new block with realloc_from_id. zero records the glibc realloc(ptr,0) free as a terminal Reallocated event with the old ID when found, not a new lifetime; failed records failure and preserves the old live block. The same numeric address can later have multiple historical block candidates: address_candidates(&self, pid: u32, addr: u64) - Vec<&BlockState deliberately returns all observed containing extents, not pointer-origin proof (:882-895). For free (:700-746), ok retires the matching live block or marks the PID incomplete if none exists; null is an observed no-op. unknown may resolve by live (pid,address) despite a full C table. If it matches only a previously freed address, the detail says possible double free because unobserved reuse remains possible; otherwise it is an untracked address. alive_blocks(&self, pid: u32) - Vec<&BlockState returns no asserted live blocks when that PID is incomplete (:861-873). Caps and gaps preserve observed prefixes, not guaranteed final ownership. Transport and coverage verify_event_status(path: &Path, timeline: &HeapTimeline, inferior_pid: Option<u32) - Vec<String (:178-260) independently reads at most 1 MiB of status data. It requires a final newline and strict decimal pid seq failures lines, no PID zero or duplicate ACK; each observed event PID and the followed inferior (including one with zero events) must have one ACK with its last observed sequence and zero failures. It reports unexpected ACKs, mismatches and missing ACKs (up to 50 messages). It cannot discover a descendant with no events or ACK. An ACK cannot mend a malformed event stream; failure after the last logged row is detectable only because sequence/failure ACK checking is separate. At src/trace.rs:478-483, status errors quarantine the timeline, while retained events survive. pids_seen(&self), needs_pid_widening(&self) and global_id(&self, pid: u32, local_id: u64) - u64 (:897-921) leave IDs local for one observed PID; for multiple observed PIDs, nonzero IDs serialize as (pid << 32) local_id, while zero stays zero. ingest flags any local ID above u32::MAX in a multi-PID history as id_widening_overflow, so completeness is false rather than claiming unique serialized identity (:548-552). Event sequence numbers remain local to the process; interleaved file order is not a universal heap clock. Caller location and final state resolve_caller_locations(binary: &Path, callers: &u64) - Result<HashMap<u64, CallerInfo batches distinct PCs (512 per addr2line -f -C -e invocation) with supervised output/deadline; unknown ?? or zero line leaves the caller unresolved (:936-985). apply_caller_locations(timeline: &mut HeapTimeline, resolved: &HashMap<u64, CallerInfo) annotates blocks/events without replacing their raw return PCs (:1004-1031). Its caller trace_program_inner subtracts executable load bias and one byte from the recorded return address before resolution, then maps the resolved location back to the raw PC (src/trace.rs:590-636). A resolved file/line identifies an attributed call site, not which expression on a multi-call source line executed. Orchestration in src/trace.rs run_gdb_phase(...) - Result<GdbPhaseResult receives the reader/timeline and paths (src/trace.rs:1113-1124). At each observed stop it calls read_new, quarantines damaged transport, ingests rows and records their count before capturing source state (:1371-1405). It performs one final read after termination for destructor/exit-handler events (:1977-1991). trace_program_inner checks terminal ACKs, distinguishes tracker timeout/cancellation/failure from completed collection (:478-483,517-588), and builds JSON events and heap state (:851-943). final_events(timeline: &HeapTimeline) - Vec<HeapEvent widens IDs as needed (:2600-2614); backfill_snapshots(...) attaches resolved locations and adjusted IDs without rewriting historical pointer observations (:2564-2597); build_heap_state(...) carries forward only bytes actually read at earlier snapshots, including historical bytes of freed blocks (:2658-2694). Event-to-checkpoint correlation reports bracketing intervals, not an exact stop or source expression (:2616-2656). heap_history.complete requires timeline completeness, no parser errors/partial line, and a terminal debugger outcome (:891-933); status errors already quarantine the timeline. Its process_scope="verified_observed_pids_only", observed_event_pids, followed_inferior_pid and unobserved_process_coverage="unknown" qualify that claim. An observed child missing an ACK makes it incomplete; a silent child cannot be inferred. Partial events remain available, with heap usage and lifetime status downgraded (:860-870,979-1006). Neither heap telemetry nor checkpoint bytes prove pointer origin or active union member. Tests and interpretation The module's tests exercise parsing, calloc overflow and zero sizes, success/failure/zero realloc, address reuse, table-overflow fallback, PID widening, sequence gaps, transport corruption and caps (src/allocation_tracker.rs:1053-1788); seeded_reuse_sequences_match_independent_live_byte_accounting checks deterministic live-byte transitions (:1133-1218). Real wrapped C transport tests live in tests/heap_instrumentation.rs:152-334; tests/heap_provenance.rs:48-90,131-185 checks ACK and observed/silent forks. The release closure(../trace-engine-v2.2-release-closure.mdfork-child-heap-history-contract) confirms scoped completeness, not a census of all processes. The older V2 contract(../v2.mdmemory-and-value-validity) describes the recording background; where its in-place realloc wording differs, the current wrapper and timeline branches above govern. Diagram notes Event to lifetime {{diagram:d2-lifetimes}} Sequence checks precede block transitions; final lifetimes are reconstructed from retained events, not address equality. Realloc branches {{diagram:d2-realloc}} Failure, same-address success, moved success and terminal zero-size free produce different lifetime transitions.

title: Valgrind & sanitizer internals
summary: 32 · Independent Valgrind and sanitizer diagnostics In one sentence: Diagnostics are additional, separate experiments on the C program. This page follows their launches and saved reports. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Indepe
text: 32 · Independent Valgrind and sanitizer diagnostics In one sentence: Diagnostics are additional, separate experiments on the C program. This page follows their launches and saved reports. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Independent execution A new run, distinct from the GDB run. Address and allocation order may change. Stage status A separate result for each tool: succeeded, failed, skipped or timed out, with partial evidence if available. Example. A sanitizer reports a use-after-free at line 30. Preserve that report and its own status. Do not translate its pointer into a GDB-run allocation ID from a different execution. What not to assume: Failure to launch Valgrind is not evidence that Valgrind ran and found no bug. The big picture Diagnostic passes rerun the program: they do not observe the same allocation lifetimes or memory addresses as GDB's primary run. The C instrumentation and verified PID-local event stream are described in Allocator runtime(engine-allocator-deep.html) and Heap timeline(engine-heap-deep.html). trace_program_inner(config: TraceConfig) - Result<DebugSessionTrace first builds a debug executable with the wrapper and a distinct sanitized executable (src/trace.rs:226-237,313-320), then schedules independent analyses after the GDB phase (:640-849). The program's execution outcome is not replaced by a Valgrind failure. Source file: src/valgrind.rs Launch and report ownership run_valgrind(binary: &Path, program_args: &String, working_directory: Option<&Path, limits: &ExecutionLimits, xml_path: &Path, _event_file: &Path, valgrind_path: Option<&str) - Result<ValgrindRun (src/valgrind.rs:39-133) executes valgrind --tool=memcheck --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all --track-origins=yes --xml=yes --xml-file=<path <debug-binary <args. An explicit tool path overrides PATH. It removes C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE so wrapper table roots cannot change leak classification; the _event_file argument is unused. Separate bounded stdout/stderr pipes and a separate XML file prevent client stderr from corrupting XML (:48-79); diagnostic resource limits, a process group and supervised deadline apply. ValgrindRun owns optional native report, failure reason, exit/timeout/cancellation, captured output and XML path (:28-37). Reading XML is capped by min(max_trace_memory_bytes,16 MiB) (:85-106); missing root or read/parse failure is a failure, not an empty clean report. parse_valgrind_xml(xml: &str) - Result<ValgrindReport (:168-262) uses roxmltree, requires a valgrindoutput root, and marks native output complete only if a FINISHED status exists. It reads heap_summary (bytes/blocks at exit, allocations, frees, bytes allocated), all_heap_blocks_freed, and each <error including leak-kind byte sums. Native missing numbers remain nullable in observed_summary; legacy numeric totals can default to zero and must not be read as observed zero (:179-258). parse_native_u64(text: &str) - Option<u64 strictly validates comma-grouped Valgrind counters such as 4,152 (:271-286). parse_error(node: roxmltree::Node) - ValgrindError captures kind, description, unique ID, nullable leaked bytes/blocks, primary and auxiliary stacks; parse_frame(node: roxmltree::Node) - ValgrindFrame retains IP/module/function/path/line when available (:288-374). Valgrind supplies native errors and summary, not a time-indexed GDB heap history. recover_errors(xml: &str) - Option<ValgrindReport (:139-166) scans for complete <error...</error fragments if the full XML parse fails, parses each fragment as XML, and returns only complete native errors. It never fabricates a heap summary; parse_error/output_complete qualify recovery. If nothing complete survives, there is no report. A timed-out run may have a partial report, never an automatically clean one (run_valgrind:85-133; src/trace.rs:705-757). Source-site candidates, not cross-run IDs pub fn correlate_with_allocations(report: &mut ValgrindReport, allocation_sites: &(String, u32, u64)) (src/valgrind.rs:376-429) is a retained public entry point, not called by trace_program_inner. It ignores tuple allocation IDs, clears existing related_allocation_ids, and, only when an absolute <dir/<file and an absolute primary source path have equal path and line (canonicalized where possible), emits an ID-free source_site_candidates entry with evidence="same_source_site_independent_run_not_allocation_identity". Different directories with the same basename, relative paths and matching addresses cannot prove the allocation. Old imported reports may still contain legacy IDs until explicitly re-correlated; the production pipeline does not generate these links (src/trace.rs:711-716). The later release closure(../trace-engine-v2.2-release-closure.mdf14-correction-of-the-premise-failure-repair) supersedes the earlier conditional audit(../trace-engine-v2.2-final-audit.md1-executive-assessment-and-verdict) on this helper. No exact cross-execution allocation-event ID is available. Source file: src/sanitizer.rs Triggered separate execution run_sanitized(binary: &Path, program_args: &String, working_directory: Option<&Path, limits: &ExecutionLimits) - SanitizerReport (src/sanitizer.rs:20-80) starts the separately built sanitized binary with the same args/directory, null stdin, bounded piped stdout/stderr, process group, diagnostic limits and supervised deadline. ASan replaces the allocator, so its addresses/events cannot be merged with wrapped GDB telemetry (:1-13). Spawn failure produces reproduction="skipped" and an explanation; otherwise the report includes native exit/timeout/cancellation, UTF-8-lossy output excerpts (stdout 4096, stderr 8192 bytes) and an output_complete flag based on truncation/timeout/cancellation (:38-69). truncate(s: &str, cap: usize) - String respects UTF-8 boundaries (:82-92). parse_sanitizer_output(stderr: &str, stdout: &str, report: &mut SanitizerReport) (:94-160) prefers SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer:; otherwise looks for ASan ERROR:/marker, then UBSan runtime error:. It records category, message, source file/line/column when parsable, and up to 32 textual stack frames; extract_asan_category(line: &str) - String and extract_location(line: &str) - Option<(String,u32,Option<u32) perform bounded text extraction (:188-211). Matching a report marker makes the native pass reproduced; absent a marker, timeout/cancellation/nonzero exit is inconclusive, while a successful clean exit is completed_normally (:69-79). These are outcomes of the sanitized run, not proofs that GDB's crash reproduced. Text parsing may have missing location evidence. matches_crash(report: &SanitizerReport, crash: &CrashReport) - bool (:162-186) compares recorded report/stack file+line against primary-crash backtrace file+line, accepting exact text or successfully canonicalized equal paths. It does not compare addresses/PIDs or establish exact operation identity. In run_sanitizer_pass(...) - Option<SanitizerReport (src/trace.rs:49-106), a native reproduced diagnostic becomes diagnostic_observed unless it matches an existing primary crash; only a matched crash receives asan_summary. Stage health distinguishes completed, failed, timed-out, cancelled and skipped passes. A matching site supports a crash correlation, not equivalence of run histories. Scheduling in src/trace.rs SanitizerTrigger offers never, on_crash, default on_crash_or_valgrind_error, and always (src/config.rs:155-168). If crash/always already meets the trigger and the sanitized build succeeded, trace_program_inner runs sanitizer before Valgrind so a slow memcheck cannot consume its session window (src/trace.rs:644-680). Otherwise it runs Valgrind when installed and within deadline, preserving native errors without allocation-ID correlation (:682-785); for a clean primary run in the default trigger, Valgrind errors can then request sanitizer (:787-849). The two passes never share an inferior process. Missing Valgrind, failed sanitizer build, exhausted deadline or cancellation produces an explicit skip/failure reason rather than a negative diagnostic (:392-414,777-847). trace.stage_results, sanitizer_report and valgrind_report are assembled independently (:1007-1009). The V2.1 recording contract(../v2.mddeadlines-processes-and-stage-health) describes stage-level budgets. Tests and caveats src/valgrind.rs:439-622 tests grouped/missing counters, complete-error recovery from truncated XML, UAF/leak fixture stacks and leak sizes, invalid XML, and site-only correlation including same-basename collisions and legacy IDs. src/sanitizer.rs:241-297 tests ASan overflow, UBSan location, clean output and Unicode-safe truncation. tests/release_closure_8dr.rs supplies a real GCC/Valgrind numeric-address collision oracle; equal numeric mappings across processes are not malloc identity, and current CLI Valgrind errors retain zero primary allocation links (release findings(../trace-engine-v2.2-release-closure.mdf14-correction-of-the-premise-failure-repair)). Neither a missing XML file, a truncated report nor a clean sanitized rerun proves absence of a bug in the primary run. There is no supported exact diagnostic-to-GDB heap-event join. Diagram notes Independent diagnostic processes {{diagram:d2-diagnostics}} Valgrind and sanitizer runs produce separate reports and never become primary-run allocation identities.

title: Evidence fusion internals
summary: 33 · Evidence fusion: bounded links between existing records In one sentence: Fusion adds references between existing records. It does not rewrite the values GDB saw or invent an executed source expression. Key terms Term Plain me
text: 33 · Evidence fusion: bounded links between existing records In one sentence: Fusion adds references between existing records. It does not rewrite the values GDB saw or invent an executed source expression. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Correlation Finding a carefully checked way to point from one provider's record to another provider's record. Candidate A plausible possible match that does not meet the requirements for an exact same-execution link. Example. A GDB variable can carry a unique DWARF declaration ID and then point to a matching Clang declaration. If two declarations compete, the link is left unset instead of choosing the first one. What not to assume: A Clang malloc on the same line as a heap event is still only a source-call candidate. The big picture src/evidence/ reconciles optional GCC DWARF, optional Clang syntax and recorded GDB/heap evidence. It does not run GDB or clone registries per checkpoint; it adds optional references, never overwrites observed values, addresses, extents, activation IDs or allocation lifetimes (evidence/mod.rs:1-11(../../src/evidence/mod.rsL1-L11)). trace_program calls dwarf::associate after heap history/observations are assembled, then evidence::fuse(&mut trace) exactly once in the normal pipeline (trace.rs:944-969(../../src/trace.rsL944-L969)). The extraction contracts are detailed in DWARF(engine-dwarf-deep.html) and Clang AST(engine-ast-deep.html). mod.rs: orchestrator, state and accounting fuse(trace: &mut DebugSessionTrace) returns immediately if both static registries are absent; otherwise it derives a working directory from session metadata or process cwd, initializes EvidenceFusionSummary, and treats AST as available only if a TU is complete or partial (evidence/mod.rs:18-50(../../src/evidence/mod.rsL18-L50)). If Clang marked cross-provider semantics unavailable, it skips DWARF/AST member and expression links, runtime-source links and heap-call correlation, even if syntax remains retained. Otherwise it borrows the trace's DWARF registry and mutably borrows source metadata to build one transient DwarfIndex, link fields and expressions, then borrows metadata for the runtime bridge and mutably borrows it for heap-call correlation. It always audits existing optional refs, counts remaining links, and writes elapsed fusion/validation microseconds to both profiling and summary (evidence/mod.rs:51-91(../../src/evidence/mod.rsL51-L91)). count_links counts declaration, type, expression, member and candidate/ambiguity refs plus visited runtime variables across top frame, caller frames and globals; it does not claim each counted link proves a syntax node executed (evidence/mod.rs:93-152(../../src/evidence/mod.rsL93-L152)). The missing-provider test distinguishes absent summary, empty syntax registry, and one usable partial TU (tests/evidence_fusion.rs:137-178(../../tests/evidence_fusion.rsL137-L178)). declarations.rs: CU-scoped type and member selection DwarfIndex::new(&TypeRegistry, &Path) borrows TypeEntrys and builds ID, canonical CU-file-to-unit, and (unit ID, kind/name) indexes. unit_file resolves a CU name against its compilation directory or cwd; artificial/empty names cannot be matched. unique_unit, unique_record and unique_member require one CU for the AST TU file, one complete named struct/union in that CU, then one member with the requested name (evidence/declarations.rs:13-86(../../src/evidence/declarations.rsL13-L86), evidence/declarations.rs:155-187(../../src/evidence/declarations.rsL155-L187)). member_link(&self, file, parent_spelling, member_name) - Option<(DwarfMemberRef, Option<&str) stores the parent type ID, index in the parent's serialized member vector, name and recorded byte offset; it returns the member's own type only if that type ID exists. unique_type is a separate fallback for one non-declaration-only named type in that same CU. spelling_key strips simple qualifiers and understands struct/union/enum tags but rejects pointers, arrays, function forms and multiword base spellings instead of parsing C types by guesswork (evidence/declarations.rs:88-130(../../src/evidence/declarations.rsL88-L130), evidence/declarations.rs:189-221(../../src/evidence/declarations.rsL189-L221)). link_source_members(&mut SourceMetadataRegistry, &DwarfIndex) applies that resolution only to FieldDecls with a parent spelling, recording unique_parent_type_and_member_name and any valid member type (evidence/declarations.rs:132-153(../../src/evidence/declarations.rsL132-L153)). Tests demonstrate struct Pair.x - member index 0/offset 0, rejection of pointer spellings, and refusal to choose between two complete Pair records (evidence/declarations.rs:269-332(../../src/evidence/declarations.rsL269-L332)). A member's byte offset is DWARF layout, not evidence of the active member of a union. source_links.rs: expression and stopped-variable bridges link_expressions(&mut SourceMetadataRegistry, &DwarfIndex) first indexes AST unit files and declaration IDs. For each expression it clears previous cross-provider links, then follows an existing referenced_declaration to its correlated DWARF declaration/type and optional member. A MemberExpr without a member link may use its AST base type spelling and member name through member_link. If type remains unknown, sizeof(type) operand spelling, then plain expression type spelling, can resolve through unique_type within the TU's GCC CU; dwarf_type_evidence records whether the path was declaration, member, sizeof or unique name. This selection is static typing evidence, not runtime execution (evidence/source_links.rs:15-93(../../src/evidence/source_links.rsL15-L93)). The real GCC/Clang integration test asserts valid type/member references and a JSON schema-2 roundtrip (tests/evidence_fusion.rs:270-353(../../tests/evidence_fusion.rsL270-L353)). link_runtime(Option<&SourceMetadataRegistry, &mut ExecutionSnapshot) - usize builds a borrowed DWARF-declaration-ID - optional AST-declaration-ID bridge. Two AST declarations claiming the same DIE replace the bridge value with None, never a first-match winner. It clears and attaches only VariableInfo.source_declaration_ref when the variable already has that exact serialized declaration_ref, visiting top-frame variables, caller frames and globals. It never uses a variable's address or a coincident source line as the runtime bridge (evidence/source_links.rs:95-144(../../src/evidence/source_links.rsL95-L144)). The duplicate-claim test with activation IDs 7 and 8 shows the collision leaves both source refs unset; removing the duplicate links the first observation without changing either activation (tests/evidence_fusion.rs:469-535(../../tests/evidence_fusion.rsL469-L535)). heap.rs: explicit delegation, not a second matcher correlate(registry: &mut SourceMetadataRegistry, events: &HeapEvent, cwd: &Path) is the entire heap fusion module: it delegates directly to clang_ast::correlate_heap_calls (evidence/heap.rs:1-10(../../src/evidence/heap.rsL1-L10)). That callee indexes canonical source lines of direct and expanded allocator calls, requires resolved return-address-minus-one attribution and compatible event operation, and returns either a unique-direct candidate or explicit multiple/macro-only ambiguity. It never attaches an allocation ID to a syntax expression or identifies which same-line call executed (clang_ast.rs:947-1054(../../src/clang_ast.rsL947-L1054), tests/evidence_fusion.rs:355-467(../../tests/evidence_fusion.rsL355-L467)). E.g., two free calls at one resolved line yield multiple_compatible_calls_on_resolved_line, not an exact event-expression link; macro-only free yields only_macro_expanded_calls_on_resolved_line (tests/evidence_fusion.rs:390-440(../../tests/evidence_fusion.rsL390-L440)). validation.rs: construction-time reference audit audit(&mut Option<SourceMetadataRegistry, Option<&TypeRegistry, &mut ExecutionSnapshot, &HeapEvent) - usize builds borrowed sets/maps of existing DWARF declaration and type IDs, then clears dangling AST declaration/type refs and invalid DwarfMemberRefs. valid_member verifies that parent is a struct/union and that the indexed serialized member has the same name and byte offset; an invalid FieldDecl member also clears its field type, while a member-derived expression type/evidence is cleared with an invalid member. Expression type evidence is absent when its type is absent (evidence/validation.rs:15-107(../../src/evidence/validation.rsL15-L107), evidence/validation.rs:183-197(../../src/evidence/validation.rsL183-L197)). The audit removes heap candidates with missing event/expression IDs, prunes ambiguity expression IDs and drops empty/out-of-range ambiguities. Finally it clears a runtime source_declaration_ref unless the source declaration still exists and its DWARF declaration equals the observed variable's declaration_ref, in top frame, caller frames and globals. The returned rejection count is recorded by fuse; this is an in-memory construction audit, not the import-time Trace Parser's deeper structural/relation validation (evidence/validation.rs:108-181(../../src/evidence/validation.rsL108-L181), evidence/mod.rs:77-90(../../src/evidence/mod.rsL77-L90), tests/evidence_fusion.rs:555-627(../../tests/evidence_fusion.rsL555-L627)). For example, a hand-edited trace whose existing expression ID points to the wrong declaration or whose valid call ID has an incompatible source line is caught by parser deep validation, not necessarily by this existence-focused construction audit (tests/evidence_fusion.rs:629-767(../../tests/evidence_fusion.rsL629-L767), parser validation(parser-validation.html)). Partiality and invariants No DWARF or AST means no summary; DWARF-only can still produce a summary with ast_available=false. Missing/failed Clang or unverified GCC/Clang flags preserve source syntax or absence as appropriate, while cross-provider links are withheld (evidence/mod.rs:33-75(../../src/evidence/mod.rsL33-L75), tests/clang_ast.rs:556-597(../../tests/clang_ast.rsL556-L597)). AST-on/off tests compare execution outcome, event shape and normalized runtime observations while allowing only additive metadata differences; that comparison checks preservation, not an independent proof of runtime truth (tests/evidence_fusion.rs:769-891(../../tests/evidence_fusion.rsL769-L891)). A unique compiler declaration is not a unique dynamic activation; a source initializer does not prove initialization; a source-line heap candidate is not the event's executed expression. See metadata overview(engine-metadata.html) and identity contracts(identity-contracts.html). Diagram notes Fusion inputs and audit {{diagram:d2-fusion}} Existing DWARF, AST and runtime records are matched conservatively; invalid references are removed before publication.

title: Supervision & resource limits
summary: 34 · Deadlines, child ownership, and resource limits In one sentence: The supervisor watches tools and deadlines so a failed child process does not masquerade as a completed trace. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Deadline The
text: 34 · Deadlines, child ownership, and resource limits In one sentence: The supervisor watches tools and deadlines so a failed child process does not masquerade as a completed trace. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Deadline The maximum allowed time for a supervised task or session. Process group A way to manage a tool and its child processes together when stopping or cancelling work. Example. If GDB stops responding, the supervisor records a timeout and tries to clean up its process group. Any already captured snapshots remain partial observations. What not to assume: Time, journal, JSON export, parser input and assembled process memory are different resource limits. The big picture Stage 1 uses a monotonic wall deadline, explicitly owned subprocesses, bounded captured output, and Linux inferior limits. These mechanisms limit accidental runaway work; they do not sandbox C code or certify that all forked processes were observed. Entry(engine-entry-deep.html) starts the pipeline; compiler(engine-compiler-deep.html) and diagnostic stages use the supervised subprocess path. src/supervisor.rs: deadline and cancellation context Principal signatures: pub async fn scope<T(seconds: u64, future: impl Future<Output = T) - T (src/supervisor.rs:106-132), pub async fn scope_until<T(end: Instant, future: impl Future<Output = T) - T (src/supervisor.rs:134-136), pub fn deadline() - Instant, pub fn remaining() - Duration, and pub fn stage_deadline(seconds: u64) - Instant (src/supervisor.rs:138-153). scope installs task-local DEADLINE and cancellation token, plus a signal task listening for SIGINT/SIGTERM; the signal task is aborted on drop. It does not itself wrap future in tokio::time::timeout: callers use deadlines in waits and commands. scope_until clamps a stage to the earlier of its own end or the enclosing deadline. If called outside a scope, deadline() supplies a 300-second fallback; do not treat that as the configured CLI timeout. trace_program validates limits before entering scope(config.limits.timeout_seconds.max(1), ...) (src/trace.rs:131-165), and stages clamp their own budgets afterward. request_cancel() wakes cancellation() via Notify; outside the scope cancelled() is false and cancellation() is pending (src/supervisor.rs:76-104). timeout_error(operation: &str) - EngineError names the exhausted operation (src/supervisor.rs:155-159). src/supervisor.rs: subprocess lifecycle Principal types/functions: OwnedChild::spawn(cmd: &mut Command) - io::Result<Self and OwnedChild::terminate(&mut self) (src/supervisor.rs:161-198); ProcessOutput { cancelled, status, stdout, stderr, timed_out, output_truncated } (src/supervisor.rs:200-207); pub async fn output(cmd: &mut Command, end: Instant, cap: usize) - Result<ProcessOutput (src/supervisor.rs:226-304). spawn requests a new process group, kill_on_drop(true), and Linux subreaper ownership. output rejects already-cancelled/expired launches, nulls stdin, pipes both output streams, and concurrently drains each to its own cap while continuing to read/discard bytes beyond the cap. It waits for the direct child's status and both pipes; a successful parent is not allowed to leave a grandchild holding a pipe open (src/supervisor.rs:209-280). rust tokio::select! { _ = cancellation() = { was_cancelled = true; owned.terminate().await; break; } _ = &mut stdout, if !out_done = out_done = true, _ = &mut stderr, if !err_done = err_done = true, result = owned.child.wait(), if status.is_none() = { / reap and kill group / } _ = tokio::time::sleep_until(end.into()) = { timed_out = true; owned.terminate().await; break; } } This is the decision point at src/supervisor.rs:253-280, abbreviated only in the parent-exit arm. On cancel/timeout terminate kills descendant process groups and the leader, waits/reaps for up to two seconds, and offers each unfinished pipe a further bounded 100 ms to retain already produced bytes (src/supervisor.rs:175-187,281-303). Drop also starts killing a group on early unwinding, but cannot promise the same asynchronous reaping as explicit termination. enable_subreaper, descendants, and reap_descendants (src/supervisor.rs:12-59) inspect Linux /proc with a defensive 4,096-descendant scan bound; they target known PIDs, not waitpid(-1) which might steal other Tokio children's status. output_truncated reports capture-cap exhaustion; status can remain None on cancellation/timeout. stage(started: Instant, begin: Instant, status: StageStatus, exit: Option<i32, reason: Option<String, complete: bool, partial: bool) - StageResult records timing/status/completeness, not proof of total process-tree coverage (src/supervisor.rs:306-325; src/models.rs:12-44). Tests cover cancellation waking a stalled wait while retaining partial stdout, timeout with inherited pipes, timeout output, and a parent that exits before its grandchild (src/supervisor.rs:327-409). src/resource_limits.rs: configured budgets versus enforcement Principal type/function: ExecutionLimits and pub fn validate(&self) - Result<() (src/resource_limits.rs:48-198). Defaults include 1,000 steps/snapshots, ten seconds whole-session wall time, 256 MiB inferior address space, 1 MiB captured program output, 10,000 allocations, 16 child processes, 128 MiB journal budget, 32 MiB resident-record accounting, and separate 128 MiB final JSON budget (src/resource_limits.rs:120-149). validate rejects a zero step/snapshot/read budget, zero or over-one-year timeout, inferior memory below 16 MiB or overflow, and zero command/journal/resident/export budgets; other counters need not all be positive (src/resource_limits.rs:152-198). These limits are not interchangeable: max_trace_bytes is journal accounting; max_json_export_bytes counts serialized UTF-8 including newline; max_trace_memory_bytes is not total Rust RSS. The final audit(../stage1-final-audit.md) measured a 1,961-byte capped journal with a 22,883-byte final JSON and a separate export-cap failure with no emitted JSON. Enforcement signatures: pub fn apply_pre_exec_limits(cmd: &mut Command, limits: &ExecutionLimits) (src/resource_limits.rs:200-225) installs RLIMIT_AS, CPU, FSIZE, NOFILE and CORE via a pre-exec hook for a directly launched inferior. pub fn apply_diagnostic_limits(cmd: &mut Command, limits: &ExecutionLimits) omits RLIMIT_AS for tool/ASan compatibility (src/resource_limits.rs:227-249). pub fn limit_stopped_inferior(pid: u32, limits: &ExecutionLimits) - io::Result<() applies prlimit to the GDB-stopped inferior, not GDB, after its initial main breakpoint; startup before that stop is not covered by this action (src/resource_limits.rs:251-276). These functions offer different paths; do not imply all three are applied to every child. set_rlimit intentionally ignores individual kernel failures and other limits remain in play (src/resource_limits.rs:278-291). RLIMIT_NPROC is deliberately absent because it is per real user, not per inferior tree (src/resource_limits.rs:36-41,220-222). Fixed file/open-file caps are 64 MiB and 256 descriptors (src/resource_limits.rs:29-34). set_process_group and kill_process_group arrange a group and send SIGKILL to group/leader best-effort (src/resource_limits.rs:293-307). Optional cgroup: CgroupGuard::create(limits: &ExecutionLimits) - Option<CgroupGuard, attach(&self, pid: u32) - bool, and kill_all(&self) (src/resource_limits.rs:309-380). Creation needs a writable delegated cgroup v2 subtree; it writes memory.max and pids.max, returning None if unavailable. Attachment can fail, cgroup.kill requires kernel support, and drop only attempts directory removal. A configured process count is therefore best effort, not an unconditional per-tree enforcement claim. No unit tests live in resource_limits.rs; the existing suite's subprocess/resource regressions and the V2 recording contract(../v2.md) exercise and qualify the integrated behavior. The release closure(../trace-engine-v2.2-release-closure.md) further narrows heap completeness to verified observed PIDs plus the followed inferior; a silent fork remains unknown. Diagram notes Resource boundaries {{diagram:d2-limits}} Deadline, output, GDB, journal, transport and export controls operate at different points and do not form one global memory bound.

title: Trace model, journal & export
summary: 35 · Trace model, validation, journal, and JSON export In one sentence: Recording in memory, writing a stream during the run and exporting a final JSON file are three separate steps. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ JSONL journ
text: 35 · Trace model, validation, journal, and JSON export In one sentence: Recording in memory, writing a stream during the run and exporting a final JSON file are three separate steps. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ JSONL journal One JSON object per line written while the program is observed; it can preserve a prefix of events. Preflight A size check before committing the final JSON file, so an oversized export is rejected before replacing an existing file. Example. If the final JSON would exceed its byte limit, export stops without presenting a partly valid final document. If the journal stopped earlier, it still cannot rebuild final reports it never contained. What not to assume: A final-document byte cap does not constrain the trace already held in RAM, and a successful file commit cannot be undone by a later stdout error. The big picture The engine constructs an owned schema-v2 DebugSessionTrace during collection. Structural validation, append-only JSONL recovery, and final JSON export are separate operations with separate budgets and failure semantics. The journal cannot reconstruct every final report; the final JSON is what the schema reference(schema.html) and downstream consumer load. src/models.rs: owned trace and evidence domains Principal types: DebugSessionTrace (src/models.rs:499-540), RecordingData (src/models.rs:734-755), ExecutionSnapshot (src/models.rs:65-94), InstructionEvent (src/models.rs:698-723), HeapEvent (src/models.rs:248-285), HeapHistoryCoverage (src/models.rs:757-782), ExecutionOutcome and ProgramOutcome (src/models.rs:925-950). DebugSessionTrace owns vectors of snapshots, heap events and final heap state, status, reports, notes, effective configuration/limits, and independent StageResults; recording is serde(flatten), so its instruction/disassembly/checkpoint/coverage/storage fields serialize at top level rather than as a nested JSON object (src/models.rs:501-539). Its Default constructs schema_version: 2, empty evidence and ExecutionFailure, not a successful trace (src/models.rs:897-923). trace_program_inner initializes this value with effective tracing configuration and limits, later fills compilation status and early-returns a CompileFailed trace with no synthetic snapshots when GCC rejects input (src/trace.rs:196-200,291-350). A status enum is a recorded outcome, not validation of absent observations. rust pub struct DebugSessionTrace { serde(default, flatten) pub recording: RecordingData, pub schema_version: u32, pub snapshots: Vec<ExecutionSnapshot, pub heap_events: Vec<HeapEvent, pub execution_status: ExecutionStatus, pub stage_results: StageResults, // Additional reports, configuration and evidence fields in src/models.rs:501-540. } This is a field projection, not a compilable redefinition. source_checkpoints are indices into the snapshots vector, instruction_count counts attempted events even when instruction events are not retained, and event_id differs from a disassembly instruction_id (src/models.rs:699-755). VariableInfo.address is pointer storage whereas points_to is its target; PointerTarget.address_match_allocation_id is a numeric address candidate, not allocation origin (src/models.rs:118-186,605-633). HeapHistoryCoverage.complete applies to verified observed event PIDs plus the followed inferior, not all forked descendants (src/models.rs:757-781). ScopeStatus::Active and readable bytes do not prove initialization (src/models.rs:579-603). Optional static registry/source links never prove an expression executed. schema_tests::legacy_trace_deserializes_as_schema_v2_with_unstarted_stages exercises defaults for old optional fields (src/models.rs:952-985); the final audit(../stage1-final-audit.md) qualifies the supported historical corpus, not all older files. src/processor.rs: structural check only Signature: pub fn validate(trace: &DebugSessionTrace) - Result<(), String (src/processor.rs:6-43). It borrows the trace without rewriting events or simulating registers. For each resident instruction event it requires event_id == vector position; when instruction_id exists it indexes disassembly_table and checks the stored address matches; it bounds any checkpoint_id against snapshots. If events are nonempty it compares their length with instruction_count, then checks every source_checkpoints index exists and its snapshot's instruction_position does not exceed the count (src/processor.rs:7-41). rust if !data.instruction_events.is_empty() && data.instruction_count != data.instruction_events.len() as u64 { return Err("instruction count mismatch".into()); } for id in &data.source_checkpoints { let checkpoint = trace.snapshots.get(id).ok_or("invalid source checkpoint")?; if checkpoint.observation.instruction_position data.instruction_count { return Err("checkpoint beyond timeline".into()); } } This excerpt is src/processor.rs:28-41. In journal-only mode an empty resident event array is not itself a mismatch. Passing this limited check does not prove heap provenance, execution completeness, or every semantic reference's integrity; use the parser validation guide(parser-validation.html) for imported semantic evidence. The unit broken_reference_and_duplicate_event_id_are_rejected tests noncontiguous IDs and invalid disassembly references (src/processor.rs:45-76). src/storage.rs: ordered JSONL, not final JSON Principal type/signatures: Journal { file: Option<File, bytes: u64, cap: usize }; Journal::new(path: Option<&Path, cap: usize) - Result<Self; append(&mut self, kind: &str, value: &impl Serialize) - Result<usize; finalize(&mut self) - Result<(); and recover(path: &Path) - Result<impl Iterator<Item = Result<serde_json::Value (src/storage.rs:8-70). A path is opened with create_new, so it never overwrites an existing journal; None still counts serialized bytes against the cap. append wraps a value as {"kind": ..., "data": ...}, serializes a complete newline-terminated record, checks max_trace_bytes before writing, and increments bytes after write_all (src/storage.rs:25-43). finalize appends a finalized footer outside the data cap and calls sync_data; the footer denotes journal closure, not completed execution. A write failure can still leave a partial last line, and no sync_data occurs on each append (src/storage.rs:44-51). recover incrementally reads with a 16 MiB per-read bound, ignores a final line without newline, and yields per-record JSON or I/O errors; it does not reconstruct a full DebugSessionTrace from a partial journal (src/storage.rs:54-70). Tests bounded_and_no_overwrite and torn_last_record_is_recoverable_and_existing_file_is_not_overwritten cover the cap, create-new behavior, and incomplete-last-line handling (src/storage.rs:72-97). The V2 contract(../v2.md) describes journal-only capture and retained-record accounting; storage.finalized is not a coverage flag. src/json_export.rs: count first, commit file, then stdout Principal signatures: preflight<T: Serialize(trace: &T, pretty: bool, limit: usize) - io::Result<usize (src/json_export.rs:72-76); export_json<T: Serialize, W: Write(trace: &T, pretty: bool, limit: usize, file: Option<&Path, stdout: &mut W) - io::Result<usize and its cancellation-aware form export_json_cancellable<T: Serialize, W: Write(trace: &T, pretty: bool, limit: usize, file: Option<&Path, stdout: &mut W, cancel: Option<&AtomicBool) - io::Result<usize (src/json_export.rs:139-168). serialize_limited streams serde JSON to a BoundedWriter, counts actual UTF-8 output including pretty whitespace and final newline, checks the byte budget on writes, and optionally checks cancellation (src/json_export.rs:9-70). preflight uses io::sink() so it counts without allocating a full JSON string or touching either destination. It does not cap the already assembled trace in memory. rust let bytes = serialize_limited(trace, pretty, limit, io::sink(), cancel)?; if let Some(path) = file { write_file_atomic(trace, pretty, limit, path, cancel)?; } serialize_limited(trace, pretty, limit, stdout, cancel)?; Ok(bytes) This is the actual ordering at src/json_export.rs:162-168. For a file, create_sibling makes a unique same-directory create_new temp file (up to 16 names), serialization writes through a BufWriter, flushes and sync_alls the file, checks cancellation, then renames over the target (src/json_export.rs:78-137). TempPath::drop removes an uncommitted temp on failure; an existing target is preserved on preflight/temporary-write failure. The rename commits the file before stdout starts; stdout I/O or cancellation after that point cannot roll back the committed file, and stdout itself can be partially written on I/O error. Repeated serialization assumes stable trace contents: a custom stateful Serialize implementation could change between preflight and destinations, so preflight is not a transaction over arbitrary mutable serializers. The CLI maps export errors to exit 1 (src/main.rs:50-77). Tests cover exact pretty/compact limits and UTF-8, legacy round-trip, preserving the existing file on one-byte excess or serialization error, broken stdout pipe with valid committed file, disk-full stdout, cancellation before rename, and unwritable file preventing stdout (src/json_export.rs:170-413). The final audit(../stage1-final-audit.md) confirms an 8,192-byte JSON export limit rejected a larger trace before emitting JSON; that result says nothing about trace-construction RAM or general stdout atomicity. Diagram notes Producer-side ownership {{diagram:d2-model}} Provider-owned records converge in one schema-2 DebugSessionTrace before export. JSON export ordering {{diagram:d2-export}} Counting preflight rejects oversized output before file commit; committed file output cannot be rolled back by a later stdout error.
