title: JSON and JSONL ingestion
summary: 47 · Trace Parser ingestion and schema gating In one sentence: This is the code-level route from bytes on disk to a canonical, indexed TraceStore. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Decode Parse JSON text into Rust's saved-trace
text: 47 · Trace Parser ingestion and schema gating In one sentence: This is the code-level route from bytes on disk to a canonical, indexed TraceStore. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Decode Parse JSON text into Rust's saved-trace types after input and schema checks. Gate A check that rejects something too large, malformed, journal-shaped or from an unsupported schema before it is trusted as a full trace. Example. A valid final JSON passes the input-size and schema gates and gets an index. A JSONL event journal fails reconstruction because it lacks some final reports and state. What not to assume: A successful decode is only a format result. Structural and semantic validation remain separate actions. The big picture The parser starts with bytes, not a live engine session. TP-1 decides whether those bytes are a schema-2 DebugSessionTrace document, applies resource gates, and constructs one immutable canonical store. It also exposes a separate journal reader for the engine's JSONL record stream. The two paths deliberately do not merge: a journal cannot supply final reports and computed state that only exist in a complete exported trace. src/trace_parser/mod.rs: loading and assembly Principal signatures: - pub fn open(path: impl AsRef<Path, options: TraceLoadOptions) - Result<TraceStore (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:240-258) - pub fn from_reader(reader: impl BufRead, options: TraceLoadOptions) - Result<TraceStore (:264-295) - pub fn from_json_bytes(bytes: impl AsRef<u8, options: TraceLoadOptions) - Result<TraceStore (:301-325) - pub fn from_trace(trace: DebugSessionTrace) - Result<TraceStore (:331-352) - fn assemble(trace: DebugSessionTrace, source: TraceSourceMetadata) - Self (:216-230) open and from_reader call read_trace_bytes, which rejects an input larger than options.max_bytes (:232-238). from_json_bytes does not read options.format: it applies the byte limit, runs content gates, decodes JSON, and always constructs a store. open/from_reader dispatch through load_trace_document, which accepts JSON, rejects journal-shaped input with JournalReconstructionUnsupported, and never silently reconstructs a journal (:973-995). gates rejects empty/whitespace-only bytes and non-UTF-8 input before dispatch (:990-995). assemble is the ownership boundary: rust let indexes = TraceIndexes::build(&trace); TraceStore { trace: Arc::new(trace), indexes: Arc::new(indexes), source, } (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:222-229). Index construction borrows the trace, then the trace and indexes become two separately shared Arcs. No record vector is cloned and no per-query index is rebuilt. from_trace takes an already constructed model, validates only its schema version, and then assembles. It does not call validate_deep. Loading order 1. Check size. 2. Reject empty or non-UTF-8. 3. Decode JSON and validate schema. 4. Build compact indexes. 5. Store the canonical trace and indexes behind Arcs. 6. Return a cheap-to-clone handle. Deep validation is a separate explicit operation (TraceStore::validate_deep, :406-408), and semantic validation is requested separately by validated_semantic(). src/trace_parser/json.rs: document decode Signatures: pub(crate) fn decode_document(text: &str) - Result<DebugSessionTrace (src/trace_parser/json.rs:19-29), pub(crate) fn validate_schema_version(trace: &DebugSessionTrace) - Result<() (:32-46), pub(crate) fn detect_format(text: &str) - DetectedFormat (:48-67). decode_document first uses serde to deserialize the existing DebugSessionTrace model, preserving the model's optional/additive V2.1/V2.2 fields, then calls the schema gate. A serde error becomes MalformedJson; a non-2 schema version becomes UnsupportedSchemaVersion. JSON object key order and whitespace are irrelevant. The parser never accepts a legacy removed required field merely because it is numerically similar. detect_format classifies complete JSON documents and journal-shaped text. It is content-based, not filename-based. A malformed final journal-shaped line can be classified as a journal candidate even if newline-terminated; the later typed journal parser still rejects that record. The detector is therefore a dispatch aid, not proof that the journal is valid. src/trace_parser/journal.rs: typed JSONL records Principal signatures: - pub(crate) fn parse_bytes(bytes: &u8, options: &TraceLoadOptions) - Result<JournalTrace (src/trace_parser/journal.rs:142-149) - pub(crate) fn parse_reader(mut reader: impl BufRead, options: &TraceLoadOptions) - Result<JournalTrace (:156-230) - fn push_record(...) - Result<() (:234-267) - fn decode_line(...) - Result<Option<JournalRecord (:270-361) JournalRecord preserves configuration, checkpoints, allocations, gaps, disassembly, instruction events, finalized markers, and optional unknown records in file order (:46-68). JournalTrace adds per-kind counts, a finalized flag, a torn_tail flag, and the physical line count (:108-122). It is evidence in recorded order, not a DebugSessionTrace. parse_reader buffers one line at a time and bounds a single record by options.max_bytes (:167-174). If a final line lacks a newline, it is accepted only when it fully decodes; otherwise it becomes torn_tail and is never interpreted (:180-207). push_record enforces max_journal_records and requires the first record to be configuration (:242-254). decode_line validates UTF-8, JSON object shape, string kind, and typed payload (:275-361). A concrete journal row This is an illustrative record shape, not captured output: json {"kind":"allocation","data":{"observed_at_stop":7,"event":{"event_type":"Allocated","allocation_id":1,"pid":100,"sequence":4,"address":"0x55d0a0002a10","size_bytes":32}}} The parser returns JournalRecord::Allocation { observed_at_stop: 7, event }. It does not infer that this allocation happened exactly at stop 7; the stop is the recorder's observation marker. parse_journal, parse_journal_bytes, and parse_journal_reader are public wrappers around this path (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:926-962). src/trace_parser/error.rs: failure categories TraceParseError separates input failure from query failure (src/trace_parser/error.rs:17-119): source wrapping, I/O, empty input, size limit, invalid encoding, malformed JSON, unrecognized format, unsupported schema, invalid trace, malformed/unsupported journal records, journal record limit, unsupported reconstruction, and missing journal configuration. File entry points wrap inner failures in Source { path, source } so the originating input remains visible. QueryError is a different type (:139-218): page limit, foreign trace, out-of-range position, invalid half-open range, unresolvable reference, unavailable evidence, and ordering violation. Ingestion success therefore does not imply query success. A partial execution is recorded data, not a TraceParseError. Tests and boundaries tests/trace_parser.rs covers file/reader/byte loading, schema rejection, format selection, journal fixtures and malformed inputs; tests/fixtures/journal/{calloc_demo_dual,finite_loop_dual}.jsonl exercise typed record streams. TraceLoadOptions::default() caps JSON input at 512 MiB and journals at two million records (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:141-184). Those limits do not bound an already assembled parser process. The engine's separate JSON export cap does not become a parser input guarantee. Diagram notes JSON ingestion sequence {{diagram:d3-ingest-json}} Schema gate {{diagram:d3-schema-gate}} Journal record lifecycle {{diagram:d3-journal}} Ingestion error classes {{diagram:d3-errors}}

title: Ownership, views & evidence references
summary: 48 · Canonical ownership, borrowed views, and evidence references In one sentence: This page explains who owns the saved trace and why queries can return original records without making copies. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------
text: 48 · Canonical ownership, borrowed views, and evidence references In one sentence: This page explains who owns the saved trace and why queries can return original records without making copies. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Canonical owner The one shared Arc<DebugSessionTrace holding the records for this loaded trace. Foreign trace A second independent load, even from identical JSON, with a different owner. Its citations cannot be used against the first load. Example. The parser returns a reference to snapshot 3's variable rather than copying its bytes. An EvidenceRef carries enough ownership context to reject a mistaken cross-trace lookup. What not to assume: A weak reference does not keep a dropped trace alive or make numeric IDs transferable between loads. The big picture The parser's central design is simple: own the trace once, build positions once, and let every higher layer borrow the original records. A view is organization, not a second trace. An evidence reference is a checked position plus a weak owner identity, not a copy of an observation. Canonical owner and cheap clones TraceStore has exactly three fields (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:191-214): rust pub struct TraceStore { trace: Arc<DebugSessionTrace, indexes: Arc<TraceIndexes, source: TraceSourceMetadata, } assemble builds indexes from &trace, then moves the trace and index sets into separate Arcs (:216-230). TraceStore derives Clone: cloning shares both Arcs and copies only the small source metadata. shared() returns the canonical trace Arc (:354-357), not another store or an index clone. This creates three ownership cases: Case Owner Query behavior --------- let alias = store.clone() Same Arc<DebugSessionTrace Same trace identity; all evidence references resolve Load the same JSON twice Two independent Arcs Equal content, different identity; references are foreign Drop every TraceStore clone Trace and indexes freed when last Arc drops Old EvidenceRef cannot become accidentally valid through address reuse The weak identity in EvidenceRef is what prevents a numeric position from becoming portable. Two stores can both have snapshots0; that does not make their records the same trace. Borrowed views Signatures: pub fn raw(&self) - RawTraceView<'_ (src/trace_parser/views.rs:433-435) and pub fn semantic_input(&self) - SemanticInputView<'_ (:438-440). Both views hold one &'a TraceStore; both are Clone, Copy and allocate no records. RawTraceView dereferences to TraceStore, exposing existing TP-1/TP-2 methods without duplicate APIs (:44-86). SemanticInputView adds checkpoint traversal and evidence resolution (:91-166). It does not infer C objects, pointer origins or state changes. Checkpoint contexts SemanticInputView::checkpoint_context(snapshot_index) resolves a snapshot and returns CheckpointContext with source_checkpoint_position = None (:114-122). source_checkpoint_context(position) first maps the explicit source-checkpoint position to a snapshot index (:128-133). snapshots() iterates all retained snapshots, including snapshots not in source_checkpoints (:137-144). source_checkpoints() iterates the explicit list and yields QueryResult items so a bad recorded reference is reported at its actual position rather than skipped (:149-154). CheckpointContext (:175-181) borrows the store, a snapshot, and the snapshot index. It keeps source-checkpoint position separate. Its stop_id() converts the model's zero sentinel to None (:196-200); source_location() rejects empty file/line 0 (:204-207). events_at_checkpoint and heap_events_in_snapshot_interval delegate to verified TP-2 searches (:273-290). snapshot_evidence, variable_evidence, global_evidence, caller evidence and heap-block evidence create trace-scoped references (:292-341). The distinction matters: a context reached through source_checkpoints has an explicit checkpoint position, while a context reached directly from snapshots() does not. Neither invents a checkpoint entry. EvidenceRef and EvidenceLocation EvidenceLocation enumerates canonical collection positions and nested positions (src/trace_parser/evidence.rs:21-66): snapshot, instruction event, disassembly, heap event/state, allocation lifetime, gap, frame, variable, caller frame/variable, global, heap block, event memory, compiler/Valgrind/internal diagnostic, and report markers. A caller-frame frame is a vector position, not a GDB level or activation ID. EvidenceRef stores a Weak<DebugSessionTrace and an EvidenceLocation (:68-75). It never owns the trace or a record. evidence_ref first calls resolve_location to reject invalid positions, then binds the location to this store's weak trace identity (src/trace_parser/evidence.rs:129-135; src/trace_parser/mod.rs:1026-1039). resolve_evidence checks Weak::ptr_eq before resolving the location (src/trace_parser/evidence.rs:140-145). This ordering is important: a reference from an independently loaded identical JSON document returns ForeignTrace, not a plausible-looking snapshot. Clones of the same store share the same Arc and resolve normally. resolve_location performs direct vector lookups for every supported category and returns Evidence<'_ borrowing the original record (:147-265). Optional reports return Unavailable; invalid indices return InvalidReference. Evidence has no owned payload, so raw bytes, addresses and statuses remain exactly as recorded. Valid and invalid example rust let store = TraceStore::open("trace.json", TraceLoadOptions::default())?; let context = store.semantic_input().checkpoint_context(0)?; let reference = context.variable_evidence(0)?; let evidence = store.resolve_evidence(&reference)?; let other = TraceStore::open("trace.json", TraceLoadOptions::default())?; assert!(matches!( other.resolve_evidence(&reference), Err(QueryError::ForeignTrace) )); The example uses the real API names. It is illustrative, not a checked-in test transcript. A reference is not serialized as a cross-session identity; its location alone is insufficient without the matching owner. Raw versus semantic input RawTraceView is for exact recorded access: ranges, instruction events, source/disassembly, heap events and diagnostics. SemanticInputView composes those records into checkpoint contexts without making semantic claims. ValidatedSemanticView is the next layer: it owns a ValidationReport and borrows the store (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:28-34). Creating it runs one deep-validation pass; queries do not rerun it. Performance and tests Creating either view copies one reference; creating a checkpoint context is O(1) and allocates no record buffer. Evidence creation validates a position and allocates an EvidenceRef with a weak pointer. Resolution is direct vector indexing. tests/trace_parser_views.rs exercises raw/semantic context separation, foreign-reference rejection, caller evidence, source declarations and process-scope annotations; tests/trace_parser.rs covers positional/range errors. title: Compact position indexes
summary: 49 · Compact position indexes In one sentence: These are the actual lookup-table designs behind the fast queries. Start with the book-index idea before reading the array layouts. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ CSR Compressed
text: 49 · Compact position indexes In one sentence: These are the actual lookup-table designs behind the fast queries. Start with the book-index idea before reading the array layouts. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ CSR Compressed sparse row: two compact arrays tell you where the positions for one key begin and end. Think of a table of contents pointing to a short run of page numbers. Canonical array The original trace's ordered list of events or snapshots; the index stores positions into it rather than duplicating records. Example. If static instruction 4 was observed at event positions 2, 9 and 20, CSR stores those positions together. Looking up instruction 4 retrieves the three original events in their saved order. What not to assume: Fast lookup is not validation. If an imported event names an invalid instruction, deep validation reports it instead of fixing it by guessing. The big picture TP-2 exists so repeated consumer questions do not rescan canonical arrays. The indexes store positions, interned path keys and small ordering facts; they never clone an InstructionEvent, snapshot, heap event or metadata record. TraceIndexes::build runs once during TraceStore::assemble, and every clone of the store shares the same index Arc. Index inventory Index Source collection Key Stored value Main consumers --------------- ExecutionsIndex instruction_events disassembly instruction_id CSR event positions instruction_execution_positions, instruction_executions SourceIndex instruction_events exact (file, line) and instruction ID CSR instruction IDs/event positions/source-key positions source lookup and reverse instruction→source AllocationIndex heap_events, heap_state, allocation_lifetimes allocation ID event positions, state position, lifetime position heap queries and TP-6/TP-7 MetadataIndex optional DWARF/AST registries trace-local type/declaration/expression IDs registry positions and candidate/ambiguity positions TP-3/TP-6 static lookup OrderingFacts snapshots, events, gaps recorded sequence booleans zero-memory binary searches TraceIndexes::build calls each builder in one construction pass (src/trace_parser/indexes.rs:94-116). It does not sort canonical arrays. estimated_bytes is an approximate payload estimate, not process RSS (:123-160). Disassembly executions: CSR ExecutionsIndex stores offsets: Vec<u32 and positions: Vec<u32 (:270-274). The build makes two passes over events: 1. Count events per valid instruction_id. 2. Build offsetsid..offsetsid+1, then fill positions using a cursor. The result is a compressed sparse row layout: repeated executions of one static instruction stay distinct and appear in ascending event order (:277-309). positions_of rejects an ID outside the disassembly table with InvalidReference and returns the borrowed slice (:313-326). Events with missing or out-of-range IDs are absent from the index; deep validation reports them, and direct queries surface invalid references rather than inventing a match. Lookup path text instruction_execution_positions(id) - ExecutionsIndex::positions_of(id) - offsetsid..offsetsid+1 - &positionsstart..end - canonical instruction_eventsposition There is no per-query scan and no cloned event vector. Complexity is O(1) slice lookup after O(events + disassembly entries) construction. Source locations: static and dynamic SourceIndex records exact file strings, not basenames (src/trace_parser/indexes.rs:343-397). Each distinct path is interned once; a (file_id, line) key maps to a slot. For each event with both source.file and source.line, the builder accumulates: - event_positions: every recorded event at that location, in event order; - instruction_ids: deduplicated disassembly IDs associated by those events; - reverse instruction→source-key positions. The transient slots are flattened into CSR arrays (:461-499). key_position scans only distinct recorded files, then uses a hash lookup for the line (:507-510). instruction_ids_of is the static side; event_positions_of is the dynamic side. They answer different questions and are never merged. source_key_positions_of returns source keys for a disassembly ID (:584-597). The disassembly table itself has no source fields in this schema; the association is resolved through recorded event evidence. A source line can therefore have several instructions, and one instruction can have several recorded source contexts. Allocation identity, never address AllocationIndex keys on allocation_id, not address and not vector position (:610-688). It stores: - events_by_id: chronological event positions per ID, including ID 0's untracked events; - state_by_id: first heap_state position per ID; - lifetime_by_id: first lifetime position per ID. event_positions_of returns an empty slice for an unknown ID, a valid empty result (:661-666). state_position_of and lifetime_position_of return Option, allowing callers to distinguish "not recorded" from an event history. Duplicate state/lifetime IDs are not silently merged; deep validation reports them. Metadata identities MetadataIndex holds hash maps from trace-local type/declaration/source declaration/source expression IDs to positions (src/trace_parser/indexes.rs:167-257). Candidate and ambiguity maps hold positions into the optional source registry. Duplicate IDs retain the first position; deep validation reports the structural contradiction before trusted semantic queries (:163-166). This is a static index, not an execution index. A source expression ID never becomes an executed-expression ID, and a heap-call candidate never becomes an allocation identity. Ordering facts and binary search OrderingFacts verifies five recorded orderings in one pass (:694-747): - snapshot stop_id strictly increasing; - event stop_id_before non-decreasing; - event checkpoint_id non-decreasing, with None first; - snapshot cumulative heap_event_count non-decreasing; - trace-gap instruction_position non-decreasing. TraceStore::snapshot_at_stop refuses to binary-search unless snapshots_by_stop_sorted is true (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:554-567). events_at_stop checks event stop order and returns a borrowed contiguous run (:578-589). events_at_checkpoint checks checkpoint order (:596-615). heap_events_at_stop checks heap counts and returns the slice between the previous retained snapshot and this one (:634-664). A broken ordering is QueryError::OrderingViolation, not a nearest-match guess. Position conversion and memory pos(index) converts usize to u32 with an assertion that a record count above u32::MAX is impossible under the ingestion byte cap (src/trace_parser/indexes.rs:755-759). Positions are u32 in compact arrays; canonical lookups convert back to usize. This is a checked implementation invariant, not an arbitrary truncation. estimated_bytes counts CSR arrays at four bytes per position, approximates hash overhead, and includes interned path bytes and metadata maps (:123-160). It excludes allocator bucket metadata, the canonical trace, and the validation report. The historical Stage 1 audit's 900-checkpoint/3,143-instruction workload is evidence about one release benchmark, not a universal RSS bound. Tests tests/trace_parser_indexes.rs covers execution positions, source keys, duplicate/invalid references, heap identity, ordering and iterators. tests/trace_parser.rs exercises public stop/checkpoint/source/heap queries. The tests validate implementation branches; they do not prove that a particular imported trace is semantically valid. title: Deep validation architecture
summary: 50 · Deep validation and finding classification In one sentence: This chapter shows how the parser checks imported records against one another and reports contradictions separately from missing evidence. Key terms Term Plain meani
text: 50 · Deep validation and finding classification In one sentence: This chapter shows how the parser checks imported records against one another and reports contradictions separately from missing evidence. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Validation finding A report entry with a code, severity and location saying what check failed or what evidence is missing. Aggregation Repeated findings can be counted together without erasing where they first appeared. Example. A trace that stops because of a time limit can be structurally sound and partial. A trace that claims one realloc has two incompatible predecessors is structurally corrupt. What not to assume: The parser retains the original raw fields for investigation; it does not turn a contradiction into a supported semantic link. The big picture Deep validation is an explicit audit of the imported trace. It is not part of deserialization, and it never rejects a trace. TraceStore::validate_deep() calls validation::validate_deep(&self.trace) and returns a report (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:401-408). TP-6 calls the same pass once when a ValidatedSemanticView is constructed. Report model ValidationSeverity has four categories (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:48-70): - StructuralCorruption: a guaranteed invariant is violated; dependent queries refuse to answer. - PartialCoverage: the trace legitimately lacks observations because of caps, retention or interruption. - UnavailableEvidence: a relationship cannot be established from recorded evidence. - OptionalAbsence: the schema permits the field to be absent. ValidationLocation identifies the first canonical position for a finding (:75-156). ValidationFinding carries severity, stable code, human detail, location and an occurrence count (:158-171). ValidationReport::findings() returns all findings; of_severity filters; is_structurally_sound() is true only when there are no corruption findings (:193-232). is_partial() is a separate question. Aggregation Builder::push aggregates by (code, severity), preserving the first location and incrementing occurrences (:814-841). finish sorts corruption first, then partial, unavailable and optional (:843-855). This keeps a 94k-event report compact instead of emitting one finding per record. Orchestration validate_deep runs the engine's structural validator first, then a fixed sequence of passes (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:243-267): 1. crate::processor::validate → ENGINE_STRUCTURAL_VALIDATION 2. instruction events 3. snapshots 4. source checkpoints 5. heap 6. DWARF registry 7. AST registry 8. source links 9. gaps 10. coverage 11. diagnostics The function is O(E + S + H + B + L + G) in retained records. It does not require TraceIndexes; it can validate a store built before the current index layer existed. Instruction events validate_instruction_events (:860-1120) checks the orderings used by zero-memory queries: stop_id_before non-decreasing, checkpoint_id non-decreasing, and event IDs/addresses/disassembly references consistent with the canonical arrays. It distinguishes a missing instruction_id (optional/unavailable) from an out-of-range ID (corruption). It also checks memory evidence shape and variable/event references without turning an unreadable read into corruption. A recorded gap is not an event. An attempted instruction count above the retained event count is a retention fact, not a reason to invent missing events. Snapshots and source checkpoints validate_snapshots (:1123-1250) checks snapshot positions, stop identity, frame/variable/caller references, heap counts, memory status and pointer evidence. It verifies that a snapshot's step_index is its vector position, that source locations are internally consistent, and that referenced records exist. Missing optional capture is unavailable/optional; a reference that cannot resolve is a structural finding. validate_source_checkpoints (:1419-1459) verifies that every entry in recording.source_checkpoints is a valid snapshot position. An out-of-range entry is corruption; an empty list is normal. Pointer checks are deep enough to preserve the corrected contract: - a heap target with an allocation ID but no recorded provenance status is POINTER_HEAP_PROVENANCE_UNRECORDED (unavailable); - a numeric-address, uncertain, freed or non-heap target claiming a definite ID is POINTER_HEAP_PROVENANCE_CONTRADICTORY (corruption); - a target identity must be definite, not unresolved:, and cannot also identify a heap allocation; - an inactive-only variable target, base+offset mismatch, or address outside every recorded extent is corruption; - a missing target variable at one checkpoint is unavailable, not proof that the activation died. See pointer and process coverage(parser-coverage-deep.html) for the decision tables. DWARF and AST registries validate_dwarf_registry checks duplicate trace-local type, declaration and CU IDs (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:270-315). validate_ast_registry checks duplicate AST declaration/expression IDs and verifies translation-unit, declaration, expression, DWARF and type references (:317-812). A missing optional registry returns without findings. A malformed reference is structural corruption; an absent optional provider is optional absence, not a failed execution. validate_source_links checks fusion references, member offsets and runtime-variable source bridges. A candidate source relationship is not promoted to execution proof. Invalid links are removed by the engine's construction-time audit and reported here when imported. Heap, gaps and diagnostics validate_heap checks unique state/lifetime IDs, per-PID sequence order, checkpoint intervals, realloc origins, terminal event shape, address presence and history completeness (:1568-1835). Realloc predecessor verification is substantial enough to have its own chapter(parser-realloc-deep.html). validate_gaps verifies gap positions and ordering; validate_coverage distinguishes configured user-code coverage from observed-PID heap coverage; validate_diagnostics checks report shapes and optional absence. A crash, step cap, missing Valgrind report or partial memory read is a recorded outcome, not corruption by itself. What this layer does not do It does not execute C, evaluate DWARF location expressions, infer an active union member, prove initialization from bytes, or turn an AST line match into a dynamic call. It does not certify all fork descendants. It does not make an independent Valgrind report a primary-run allocation ID. It reports corruption separately from incompleteness so consumers can refuse wrong answers without confusing them with missing evidence. Tests tests/trace_parser.rs and tests/trace_parser_realloc_f01.rs exercise malformed imports, forged pointer/process claims, realloc links and valid partial traces. examples/trace_parser_tp8_mutate.rs and examples/trace_parser_tp8_cycles.rs are preserved audit probes; they are not DOC-3 reruns. The historical TP-8 audit's conditional verdict predates F01; the current source includes the corroboration checks described here. title: Realloc verification and TP8-F01
summary: 51 · Realloc provenance and TP8-F01 In one sentence: realloc can resize or move a block, fail, or in the observed glibc case free it when asked for size zero. Those cases must not be confused. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ P
text: 51 · Realloc provenance and TP8-F01 In one sentence: realloc can resize or move a block, fail, or in the observed glibc case free it when asked for size zero. Those cases must not be confused. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Predecessor The older allocation lifetime that a successful realloc actually continued from, if supported by recorded events. Corroborate Check other independent records—creation events, PID, sequence and lifetime boundaries—instead of trusting just one old_id number. Example. An imported block says realloc_from_id=2, but its creation event is an ordinary malloc. The predecessor number exists, yet the event contradicts the claimed relationship; the parser rejects the link. What not to assume: A reused or unchanged address is never enough to establish a realloc edge. A failed realloc leaves the old block alive. The big picture The TP-8 audit found a correctness defect: an imported heap object could name an existing but wrong predecessor ID, and validation treated ID existence as sufficient. TP8-F01 changed both deep validation and TP-6 confidence to require recorded creation/event/lifetime corroboration. The repair is in realloc_link and validate_heap; the raw realloc_from_id field is preserved for investigation. The defect in one sentence An allocation ID is a number in a sparse identity space. It is not proof that a realloc event connected that predecessor to this successor. The old check could answer "the ID exists" and accidentally answer "the relationship is true." realloc_link Signature: pub(crate) fn realloc_link<'a(block: &HeapBlockInfo, current: Option<&AllocationLifetime, previous: Option<&AllocationLifetime, events: impl Iterator<Item = &'a HeapEvent, previous_events: impl Iterator<Item = &'a HeapEvent) - ReallocLink (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:1485-1566). ReallocLink is Verified, Unavailable, Ambiguous or Contradictory (:1467-1473). The function receives only events indexed for the successor and predecessor, not the whole log. The algorithm in execution order: 1. If block.realloc_from_id is None, return Unavailable: there is no recorded predecessor claim. 2. If the predecessor ID equals the successor ID, return Contradictory: a non-terminal realloc cannot be its own predecessor. 3. If the predecessor ID is 0, return Unavailable: 0 is the untracked domain, not a lifetime identity. 4. Scan successor creation events: - terminal realloc(ptr, 0) rows are skipped; - an Allocated event for the successor is contradictory; - only Reallocated events can establish the link; - a different old_allocation_id, a non-realloc block type, a PID mismatch, an allocation sequence that does not match, or a free boundary before the event is contradictory; - a missing old_allocation_id sets missing = true. 5. Count predecessor creation events (Allocated or Reallocated, excluding terminal zero realloc). A PID or sequence mismatch is contradictory. 6. More than one successor match or predecessor creation is Ambiguous. 7. Missing corroboration, missing current/previous lifetime, a zero allocation sequence, or a predecessor without a free boundary is Unavailable. 8. Exactly one compatible successor creation and one predecessor creation, with compatible lifetimes, is Verified. Terminal zero-size realloc terminal_zero_realloc recognizes the engine's recorded form: Reallocated, same ID as old_allocation_id, no address, and size 0 (:1475-1483). This is treated as a terminal free-shaped event, not a new lifetime or a self-link. The implementation does not claim this is universal C allocator behavior; it is the verified environment's recorded convention. Validation integration validate_heap builds known IDs from heap state and lifetimes, linked successor IDs, related predecessor/successor IDs, and creations event lists (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:1568-1638). For each block with realloc_from_id: - an unresolved origin is REALLOC_ORIGIN_UNRESOLVED (unavailable); - Contradictory becomes REALLOC_LINK_CONTRADICTORY (structural corruption); - Ambiguous or Unavailable becomes REALLOC_LINK_UNVERIFIED (unavailable); - Verified produces no finding. It also validates event-level origins (REALLOC_EVENT_ORIGIN_CONTRADICTORY) and walks predecessor chains with a visited/in_path set to report REALLOC_LINK_CYCLE (:1692-1834). A cycle is corruption even when events/lifetimes are missing. A terminal zero realloc is excluded from creation evidence at :1475-1483. Confidence propagation TP-6 uses the same helper rather than duplicating the rule. ValidatedSemanticView::heap computes identity_confidence and realloc_confidence (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:225-286): - contradictory PID or malformed scope → contradictory; - ID 0 or no lifetime/block → unavailable; - complete observed-PID history with a verified process scope → definite identity; - otherwise → candidate. realloc_link maps to confidence: Helper result Semantic confidence ------ Verified + definite identity Definite Verified + incomplete/legacy identity Candidate Ambiguous Ambiguous Unavailable / no block Unavailable Contradictory Contradictory qualify upgrades every result to Contradictory if the whole report has any structural corruption (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:61-67). This is deliberately conservative: one bad imported relationship prevents any query from claiming Definite, rather than letting a local lookup ignore a global contradiction. Special cases - In-place realloc: same address, new size; a new lifetime may be linked to the predecessor only through recorded events. - Moved realloc: predecessor closes at the recorded sequence; successor has a new ID and an explicit old ID. - Failed realloc: old block remains alive; no successor link. - Address reuse: two lifetimes may share an address; address equality never joins them. - Terminal realloc(ptr,0): the observed environment may free the old ID and return null; the event is terminal, not a predecessor edge. Tests and examples tests/trace_parser_realloc_f01.rs covers fresh in-place/moved realloc, forged predecessors, missing/ambiguous creation, cycles, terminal zero realloc and confidence. examples/trace_parser_tp8_audit.rs and examples/trace_parser_tp8_cycles.rs are preserved probes. tests/fixtures/stage1/realloc_move.json is a minimal recorded move fixture. These tests validate the implementation; they are not a rerun of the full Stage 1 corpus for DOC-3. title: Pointer provenance & process coverage
summary: 52 · Pointer provenance and process coverage In one sentence: Two attractive shortcuts are unsafe: guessing where a pointer originated from its address, and claiming every child process was seen because the observed event logs are
text: 52 · Pointer provenance and process coverage In one sentence: Two attractive shortcuts are unsafe: guessing where a pointer originated from its address, and claiming every child process was seen because the observed event logs are complete. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Address containment The number inside a pointer falls inside the current range of a recorded heap block. It does not tell us how the pointer was obtained. Observed-PID scope The particular processes that wrote events and whose available event history was checked; it is not a list of every fork descendant. Example. A silent child can run without an event line. The known parent PID's log might be complete while the child's activity is still unknown. What not to assume: Treat imported claims of a definite allocation ID from address_only, or of all-descendant completeness, as contradictions rather than convenient facts. The big picture Two imported claims are especially easy to forge because they look numeric: a pointer target with an allocation ID, and a heap history marked complete. TP-5 and TP8-F01 tightened both. The parser does not infer pointer origin from address containment, and it does not infer a process-tree census from event/ACK records. Pointer provenance decision table validate_pointer_reference receives the variable, an identity map and a finding builder (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:1306-1415). If there is no recorded target, it returns without manufacturing one. Recorded target Finding Meaning --------- Heap ID with no provenance_status POINTER_HEAP_PROVENANCE_UNRECORDED (unavailable) Legacy metadata; do not infer origin Any allocation ID with a status, or a non-heap definite ID POINTER_HEAP_PROVENANCE_CONTRADICTORY (corruption) Numeric/uncertain/freed/unknown evidence cannot claim definite identity ID and address_match_allocation_id disagree POINTER_HEAP_ADDRESS_MISMATCH (corruption) Two recorded identity claims conflict Resolved variable identity empty, unresolved:, or also a heap ID POINTER_VARIABLE_REFERENCE_INVALID (corruption) A variable target needs a definite non-heap identity Identity not observed at this checkpoint POINTER_VARIABLE_REFERENCE_UNRESOLVED (unavailable) Capture caps/omission, not death All same-identity candidates inactive POINTER_VARIABLE_REFERENCE_INACTIVE (corruption) A resolved pointer points only at inactive objects Base + offset does not equal pointer POINTER_VARIABLE_OFFSET_MISMATCH (corruption) Arithmetic inconsistency Pointer outside every recorded extent POINTER_VARIABLE_EXTENT_MISMATCH (corruption) Address cannot fit any observed object A numeric address match is always a candidate. address_only, ambiguous_reuse, known_freed_address and history_incomplete are not promoted to definite origin. A missing status is not blindly treated as corruption either: it becomes unavailable and tells the caller not to infer provenance. Forged address_only example Suppose an imported variable has points_to = "0x1000", target.kind = "heap", target.allocation_id = 7, target.address_match_allocation_id = 7, and no provenance_status. Validation emits POINTER_HEAP_PROVENANCE_UNRECORDED (unavailable). TP-6's PointerEvidence keeps definitive_allocation: None, reports address_candidate: Some(7), and assigns Candidate only for an address-only/known-freed status. It never returns allocation 7 as a definite origin. If the imported status is address_only but allocation_id is also present, the second row makes it contradictory. The raw pointer record remains available for inspection; the relationship is not accepted. Heap process scope HeapProcessScope is a typed view over the optional HeapHistoryCoverage (src/trace_parser/views.rs:14-42): - Unknown: legacy metadata has no process-scope annotation; - VerifiedObservedPidsOnly { observed_event_pids, followed_inferior_pid, observed_history_complete }: the explicit V2.2 scope; - Unsupported(other): an imported scope value outside the supported contract. TraceStore::heap_process_scope() simply parses the recorded annotation (:351-355). It is not itself validation. validate_heap_process_coverage then checks it (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:1839-1930): - Unsupported → HEAP_PROCESS_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED corruption; - Unknown plus an unobserved-process annotation → HEAP_PROCESS_SCOPE_UNRECORDED unavailable; - VerifiedObservedPidsOnly without an unobserved annotation → HEAP_UNOBSERVED_PROCESS_COVERAGE_UNRECORDED unavailable; - any unobserved annotation other than unknown → HEAP_PROCESS_COVERAGE_UNSUPPORTED corruption; - PID 0, duplicate observed PIDs, or an event PID absent from the observed list → corruption; - complete = true together with sequence gaps, missing events, malformed lines, transport errors, truncation or ID overflow → HEAP_OBSERVED_COVERAGE_CONTRADICTORY corruption. Silent-child mutation The adversarial example changes unobserved_process_coverage from unknown to all_children_observed while retaining only observed event PIDs and the followed inferior. Validation has no event/ACK evidence for a silent child, so it emits HEAP_PROCESS_COVERAGE_UNSUPPORTED (structural corruption). The history can still be complete for observed PIDs, but that is not a descendant census. What completeness means heap_history.complete is a flag about the verified observed-PID event history. It does not mean: - every fork child was traced; - every shared-library allocation was wrapped; - a missing ACK was invented; - a dropped snapshot was reconstructed. execution_status and coverage.complete_for_scope answer a different question about configured user-code recording. A complete heap history and a partial user-code recording can coexist. Tests tests/trace_parser_semantic_tp6.rs covers candidate pointers, forged imports, aliases, crash/gap and unsupported fork claims. tests/trace_parser_realloc_f01.rs covers process scope and sequence gates. examples/trace_parser_tp8_mutate.rs is the preserved mutation probe. These are source-verified tests, not a DOC-3 full-suite rerun. Diagram notes Pointer provenance decision flow {{diagram:d3-pointer}} Process coverage decision flow {{diagram:d3-process}}

title: TP-6 validated semantic evidence
summary: 53 · TP-6 validated semantic evidence In one sentence: This code turns validated raw records into answers with confidence labels. Each label belongs to the exact claim being made. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Evidence view
text: 53 · TP-6 validated semantic evidence In one sentence: This code turns validated raw records into answers with confidence labels. Each label belongs to the exact claim being made. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Evidence view A borrowed bundle of an original record, optional metadata and carefully scoped confidence about relationships. Valid byte range The captured prefix of an object's memory at one stop. It does not say the rest is zero or initialized. Example. A variable view can say the displayed value was observed, while the pointer origin is unavailable and the byte capture is partial. Those labels do not have to agree. What not to assume: An AST call is a source candidate; an independent Valgrind report has no exact primary-run allocation ID. The big picture TP-6 is not a C interpreter and not Stage 2's src/semantic/. It is a thin, validated evidence layer over the canonical trace. It borrows records, runs deep validation once, and attaches a confidence to each stated relationship. It never invents an object graph, an execution proof or a pointer origin. Construction and confidence Signature: pub fn validated_semantic(&self) - ValidatedSemanticView<'_ (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:36-44). It stores store: &'a TraceStore and an owned ValidationReport (:28-34). Construction calls validate_deep() once. Queries borrow the store and do not rerun validation. SemanticInputView::validated() delegates to the same method (:46-50). EvidenceConfidence is Definite, Candidate, Ambiguous, Unavailable or Contradictory (:17-26). It belongs to a specific relationship, not to the execution as a whole. A variable value can be definite while its pointer origin is unavailable. A heap identity can be definite while its realloc link is ambiguous. qualify is intentionally global for corruption: if the report is not structurally sound, every confidence becomes Contradictory (:61-67). Partial coverage and unavailable evidence do not trigger this; they remain local qualifications. This prevents a consumer from reading one clean-looking field while another imported relationship is contradictory. Variable evidence Signature: pub fn variable(&self, reference: &EvidenceRef) - QueryResult<VariableEvidence<'a (:72-129). It resolves the reference, accepts only snapshot-variable, snapshot-global or snapshot-caller-variable evidence, and rejects other categories with Unavailable. For the borrowed VariableInfo, it performs three independent metadata lookups: - type_ref → store.type_entry(id); - declaration_ref → store.dwarf_declaration(id); - source_declaration_ref → store.source_declaration(id). These are optional static links. A missing link is Unavailable, not a negative claim. Value confidence is Definite only when read_status == Valid and the recorded value is non-empty; this is a debugger observation, not proof of C initialization (:95-100). Memory and pointer views are built separately. variable_target resolves a recorded variable identity at the same checkpoint (:134-201). It scans frame-zero variables, globals and caller variables, counts duplicate identities, and returns Ambiguous if more than one match exists. A target that is inactive is Contradictory; an active target with unavailable source scope is Candidate; an active target with a valid pointer and recorded scope is Definite. It never searches another stop or equates names and addresses. Memory and pointer views MemoryEvidenceView::new treats valid_range as a prefix of captured bytes, not the object's full extent or initialized bytes (:444-484). Full captured bytes are Definite; a partial/truncated prefix is Candidate; missing or inconsistent bytes are Unavailable. unobserved_range records the requested-but-uncaptured tail. PointerEvidence::new (:499-540) maps the recorded provenance status: Status / evidence Confidence ------ ambiguous_reuse Ambiguous address_only, known_freed_address Candidate history_incomplete, unknown status Unavailable null target with no status Definite (null address, never heap identity) variable identity without status Candidate no usable target/read Unavailable definitive_allocation is always None under the present V2.2 status contract. An address candidate is exposed as address_candidate, not promoted. Heap evidence heap_reference resolves a trace-scoped allocation event/lifetime/block reference to its allocation ID and delegates to heap (:205-219). A foreign reference fails before any numeric ID join. heap(allocation_id) (:225-287) looks up the lifetime, final block, predecessor ID/lifetime and history through TP-2 indexes. pid_conflict is checked across events for the ID. Identity confidence is: - contradictory on a PID conflict; - unavailable for ID 0 or no lifetime/block; - definite when history is complete, the lifetime PID is in the observed event PIDs, and the process scope is VerifiedObservedPidsOnly; - candidate otherwise (recorded ID with incomplete/legacy scope). HeapEvidence exposes the lifetime, block, old ID/lifetime, history, historical memory at the block's observed stop, identity confidence and realloc confidence (:543-560). Its events() iterator returns the original chronological events. A final state never asserts that intermediate events were retained. Source expressions and diagnostics source_expression(id) (:291-317) borrows the AST expression, registry, candidate positions, ambiguities, referenced declaration and fusion summary. heap_call_confidence is Ambiguous if ambiguity records exist, Candidate if candidates exist, otherwise Unavailable; execution_confidence is always Unavailable. A source expression is static syntax, never a dynamic call proof. checkpoint(index) returns the canonical checkpoint and its stop-local source/attempted position (:321-328). execution() exposes status, coverage, gaps, attempted and retained counts; confidence is definite only for complete configured coverage (:330-343). diagnostics() borrows compiler diagnostics, stage results, crash, sanitizer and Valgrind reports (:345-353). These are session-wide reports, not causal joins to a stop. valgrind_error(index) returns an independent error plus trace-scoped reference. source_confidence is Candidate when source-site candidates exist, otherwise unavailable; primary_allocation_id is always None (:357-374). A Valgrind source line never becomes a primary-run allocation ID. process_coverage() returns the typed scope, optional history and an unavailable confidence for unobserved descendants (:378-384). Unknown child activity remains unknown even if observed-PID history is complete. Tests and boundaries tests/trace_parser_semantic_tp6.rs covers variable/pointer candidates, heap identity, source expressions, Valgrind, crash/gap and process scope. tests/trace_parser_realloc_f01.rs covers realloc confidence. The tests use real APIs and recorded traces; they do not prove every possible import. TP-6 deliberately stops at evidence: it does not infer C objects, initialization, active union members or complete process trees. title: TP-7 consumer composition
summary: 54 · TP-7 consumer evidence composition In one sentence: This chapter explains the bounded API a UI or analysis tool can call to inspect a checkpoint without creating a parallel evidence model. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------
text: 54 · TP-7 consumer evidence composition In one sentence: This chapter explains the bounded API a UI or analysis tool can call to inspect a checkpoint without creating a parallel evidence model. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Checkpoint summary A convenient starting point for one saved stop and its related, qualified questions. Explicit pagination The caller chooses a start and end for each slice, at most 128 records. More results require another request. Example. Request the first 128 variables, process them, and then request the next 128. The summary never quietly turns '300 available' into '128 total.' What not to assume: A nearby allocation event or source expression is not automatically the cause of this particular stop. The big picture TP-7 is the public composition layer. It takes one validated view and one checkpoint and returns borrowed evidence with explicit positions, bounded pages and confidence. It does not build a second trace, a global object graph or a guessed temporal join. checkpoint_summary() Signature: pub fn checkpoint_summary(&self, index: usize) - QueryResult<CheckpointSummary<'_, 'a (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:57-68). It calls checkpoint(index), creates a snapshot EvidenceRef, and stores both plus the validated view in CheckpointSummary (:50-55). CheckpointSummary fields are intentionally small: - checkpoint: CheckpointEvidence<'a — canonical observation and context; - reference: EvidenceRef — trace-scoped snapshot citation; - view: &'v ValidatedSemanticView<'a — one validation pass, reused. CheckpointEvidence itself contains the borrowed Observation, CheckpointContext and confidence. The summary does not clone the snapshot or variables. Summary methods CheckpointSummary exposes recorded facts directly: snapshot_index, stop_id, attempted_instruction_position, pid, observation_complete, source_location and coverage (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:116-144). session_diagnostics() returns session-wide reports and explicitly does not join them to this stop (:146-150). This is important: a Valgrind error at the same source line is not evidence about this checkpoint's allocation. Variables and frames VariableScope is Local, Global or Caller(position) (:41-46). scope_len resolves the selected vector (:205-211). variable(scope, index) checks bounds, creates the correct EvidenceLocation, and delegates to view.variable() (:213-235). variables_page(scope, range) applies the shared page gate and returns an iterator (:239-246). frame_activation(id) (:251-314) resolves a unique activation at this checkpoint, not a cross-stop lifetime. It rejects ID 0 as None, detects duplicate caller activations and local/caller collisions, and returns Unavailable for ambiguous cases. Local activation confidence is candidate if any local lacks an activation ID; caller confidence is definite only when the caller has no capture errors. Globals are available separately through VariableScope::Global. Events, heap and gaps instruction_events_page(range) (:319-344) uses only events explicitly tagged checkpoint_id = Some(snapshot_index). The tag is definite; it is not proof of exact stop causality or source-expression execution. It computes the canonical start position with partition_point and returns borrowed events with references. heap_interval_page(range) (:349-373) returns events between the previous retained snapshot's cumulative heap count and this one. The interval is a retained-snapshot boundary, not an exact event timestamp. Events inside it may belong to omitted stops; confidence is Candidate. gaps_in_attempted_window(range) (:379-416) checks gap ordering, computes the previous retained snapshot's attempted position, and binary-searches gaps in (previous, current. This is an attempted-position window, not a causal assignment to one stop. Source and reports source_expressions_page(range) (:422-470) requires an optional AST registry and a recorded source location. It prefers the frame's full_file over the checkpoint's possibly relative file, but never joins by basename. It counts and pages matching expressions with a bounded on-demand scan; missing AST is Unavailable. Match confidence is Unavailable if cross-provider correlation is marked unavailable, otherwise Candidate. It never proves execution. valgrind_errors_page(range) (:71-83) pages independent Valgrind errors. heap_events_page(allocation, range) (:88-113) resolves a trace-scoped allocation reference, pages its chronological event positions, and returns each event with its own reference. A foreign reference fails before numeric lookup. Bounded pagination MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE is 128 (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:16-18). page(range, len, collection): 1. rejects start end or end len with InvalidRange; 2. rejects end - start 128 with LimitExceeded; 3. returns the half-open range unchanged. There is no silent truncation and no clamping. 0..0 is a valid empty page. A page is a view into canonical positions; the iterator yields QueryResult items so a bad recorded reference is reported at its position. More-than-128 example For a collection of 300 events, valid calls are 0..128, 128..256, and 256..300. 0..129 returns LimitExceeded { requested: 129, max: 128 }; 250..400 returns InvalidRange if the collection has only 300 entries. The caller must advance pages explicitly. This is an illustrative API sequence, not a captured trace. Temporal relationships TP-7 keeps four different associations separate: Evidence Meaning ------ instruction_events_page Events explicitly tagged with the checkpoint ID heap_interval_page Heap events between retained snapshot counters gaps_in_attempted_window Gaps in an attempted-position interval source_expressions_page AST expressions whose source span contains the checkpoint line Only the first is a definite recorded tag. Heap and gap associations are candidate boundary windows. Source matches are static candidates. None is an exact instruction timestamp or a pointer provenance proof. Tests tests/trace_parser_consumer_tp7.rs covers summary construction, bounded pages, source-expression paging, heap intervals, allocations, crash/fork scopes and the 128-entry limit. examples/stage1_public_consumer_audit.rs is the stable public consumer example. The tests validate behavior; DOC-3 did not rerun the full Stage 1 suite. title: Parser data structures
summary: 55 · Parser data structures and ownership reference In one sentence: This page names the Rust containers that hold saved evidence and the small indexes that point into it. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Vector An ordered list
text: 55 · Parser data structures and ownership reference In one sentence: This page names the Rust containers that hold saved evidence and the small indexes that point into it. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Vector An ordered list; a position such as snapshots3 identifies the fourth saved snapshot, not necessarily debugger stop ID 3. Reference A checked pointer to an existing record. An EvidenceRef is also tied to its trace owner. Example. The trace owns the actual heap events. An allocation index keeps the positions of events with ID 7, so a query can borrow the original event records. What not to assume: Do not compare unrelated numbers—event position, allocation ID, PID and memory address—as if they were one identity. The big picture This page is a reference for the types that carry parser state. It is not a second schema manual: the authoritative wire definitions are in src/models.rs, and the parser-specific wrappers are in src/trace_parser/. The distinction between owned, shared, borrowed and indexed data is the key to reading the rest of the parser. DebugSessionTrace and RecordingData DebugSessionTrace is the canonical imported/exported model (src/models.rs:501-548). Important top-level fields include execution limits/outcome, flattened RecordingData, tracing configuration, schema version, compile success/errors, optional DWARF/AST/fusion registries, snapshots, heap events/state, optional crash/Valgrind/sanitizer reports, and stage results. RecordingData (:736-755) owns disassembly, instruction events, source checkpoint positions, gaps, instruction count, coverage, storage/profiling, allocation lifetimes and optional heap history. The parser never wraps this model in a second semantic object graph. TraceStore owns one Arc<DebugSessionTrace; indexes store positions into these vectors. A snapshot's large byte buffers are not cloned by TP-2. ExecutionSnapshot and VariableInfo ExecutionSnapshot (src/models.rs:68-122) owns the call stack, frame-zero variables, globals, caller frames, heap blocks, registers when present, and observation metadata. VariableInfo (:124-180) carries identity, scope/activation, type/declaration references, points-to target, raw bytes, memory evidence, read/bytes validity and source declaration reference. MemoryEvidence (:190-205) records requested/captured bytes, address, status and error. These records are evidence, not C objects. A variable's identity distinguishes activations; a MemoryEvidence prefix does not establish initialization. TraceStore TraceStore (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:191-214) is the public owner: Field Type Ownership --------- trace Arc<DebugSessionTrace Shared canonical trace indexes Arc<TraceIndexes Shared position indexes source TraceSourceMetadata Small path/provenance metadata TraceStore is cheap to clone; a clone shares both Arcs. shared() returns the trace Arc (:354-357). raw() and semantic_input() borrow the store; neither copies records. A ValidatedSemanticView borrows the store and owns one ValidationReport. TraceIndexes and friends TraceIndexes (src/trace_parser/indexes.rs:61-77) contains ExecutionsIndex, SourceIndex, AllocationIndex, MetadataIndex and OrderingFacts. - ExecutionsIndex owns two Vec<u32 CSR arrays (:270-274). - SourceIndex owns interned Arc<str paths, key lookup, CSR arrays and invalid-reference markers (:376-397). - AllocationIndex owns HashMap<u64, Vec<u32 and HashMap<u64, u32 (:613-624). - MetadataIndex owns hash maps of Arc<str keys to u32 positions (:167-175). - OrderingFacts is a Copy record of booleans (:702-716). All positions refer back to the canonical trace. None owns a snapshot, instruction event, heap event or metadata payload. estimated_bytes is an approximation, not RSS. EvidenceLocation, EvidenceRef, Evidence EvidenceLocation is a Copy enum of canonical collection positions and nested positions (src/trace_parser/evidence.rs:21-66). EvidenceRef owns a Weak<DebugSessionTrace plus a location (:68-75). Evidence<'a is a borrowed enum of references to original records (:85-109). The invariant is: a reference is meaningful only with its owner. resolve_evidence checks Weak::ptr_eq before resolving (:140-145). A reference cannot outlive the store because the result borrows 'a; a clone of the same store shares identity, while an independent load is foreign. ValidationReport and ValidationFinding ValidationReport owns a vector of findings (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:187-232). ValidationFinding contains severity, code, detail, ValidationLocation and occurrence count (:158-171). ValidationLocation is a position in a canonical collection (:75-156). The report is owned by the validated view, not stored in the trace. is_structurally_sound and is_partial are separate queries. ValidatedSemanticView and EvidenceConfidence ValidatedSemanticView<'a (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:28-34) owns a ValidationReport and borrows &'a TraceStore. EvidenceConfidence (:17-26) is a relationship qualifier: Definite, Candidate, Ambiguous, Unavailable, Contradictory. The lifetime relationship is: text TraceStore (owns Arc trace) ^ borrowed by ValidatedSemanticView<'a (owns report) ^ borrowed by VariableEvidence<'a / HeapEvidence<'a / CheckpointSummary<'v, 'a A validated view cannot outlive its store. Evidence values borrow canonical records and cannot turn into owned semantic objects. HeapEvidence and HeapProcessScope HeapEvidence<'a (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:543-560) borrows the store and exposes allocation ID, optional lifetime/block/old lifetime, history, historical memory, identity confidence and realloc confidence. Its events() method returns the TP-2 borrowed event iterator. HeapProcessScope<'a (src/trace_parser/views.rs:14-42) borrows the recorded observed PID list and followed inferior PID. It has Unknown, VerifiedObservedPidsOnly and Unsupported variants. It is a view, not a validator and not a descendant census. CheckpointSummary and evidence items CheckpointSummary<'v, 'a (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:50-55) borrows a validated view and owns a CheckpointEvidence<'a plus an EvidenceRef. CheckpointEvidence contains the canonical observation, context and confidence. The summary's methods return borrowed records or page iterators; they do not clone snapshots. The item types (VariableEvidence, InstructionEvidence, HeapIntervalEvidence, GapEvidence, SourceLocationEvidence) carry a reference and a confidence. Their exact fields are in semantic.rs and consumer.rs; the common invariant is that a position plus an owner, not a copied payload, is the evidence identity. Invariants to check when changing code - Every index position remains in bounds of its canonical collection. - EvidenceRef is created only after position validation and retains the owner. - TraceStore clones share Arc identity; independent loads do not. - Deep validation is explicit and its report is not silently cached on the trace. - A page range is half-open, bounded and never clamped. - A confidence describes the stated relationship, not the whole execution. - Source/AST/Valgrind metadata never becomes a primary runtime identity without the documented evidence. title: Parser algorithms & invariants
summary: 56 · Parser algorithms and invariants In one sentence: The parser's algorithms explain how loading, indexing and checking work; none of them is a replay of the C program. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Binary search A fast se
text: 56 · Parser algorithms and invariants In one sentence: The parser's algorithms explain how loading, indexing and checking work; none of them is a replay of the C program. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Binary search A fast search on a list whose order was checked first. If imported ordering is broken, the parser refuses this shortcut. Invariant A rule a query depends on, such as stop IDs increasing in the recorded order. Example. To find a stop by ID, the parser first needs evidence that the snapshot list is ordered. An unsorted import produces an ordering error instead of a guessed nearest stop. What not to assume: Performance of an index does not make malformed imported relationships trustworthy. The big picture This page collects the algorithms that are easy to misread from a method name: content detection, index construction, ordering-gated lookup, evidence resolution, deep-validation aggregation, realloc corroboration, confidence qualification and bounded paging. Each section names the invariant that makes the implementation correct. Content detection and ingestion gates from_reader/open first reject oversized input, then gates rejects empty/whitespace and non-UTF-8 bytes (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:232-238,990-995). load_trace_document uses json::detect_format to distinguish a JSON document from journal-shaped text; journal-shaped input is rejected with JournalReconstructionUnsupported (:973-985). The detector is a dispatch aid, not a validation result. A malformed final journal line can classify as journal-shaped, but the typed journal parser still rejects it (src/trace_parser/json.rs:69-105; src/trace_parser/journal.rs:180-220). Invariant: format classification never upgrades malformed evidence into a valid trace. Eager position indexes TraceIndexes::build constructs five structures in one pass each (src/trace_parser/indexes.rs:94-116). The CSR builders use counting/prefix sums and a cursor; the source builder interns paths and deduplicates instruction IDs per source key (:400-500). The allocation builder maps IDs to positions without sorting canonical arrays (:626-656). Invariant: an index stores a position, not a record. A canonical vector is never reordered or cloned to satisfy a query. pos() checks the u32 bound against the ingestion cap (:755-759). Ordering-gated binary search OrderingFacts verifies snapshot stop order, event stop/checkpoint order, heap counters and gap positions (:694-747). A query that needs binary search first checks the relevant boolean: - snapshot_at_stop checks snapshots_by_stop_sorted (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:554-567); - events_at_stop checks events_by_stop_sorted (:578-589); - events_at_checkpoint checks events_by_checkpoint_sorted (:596-615); - heap_events_at_stop checks heap_counts_sorted (:634-664). Invariant: a broken recorded ordering is corruption, not permission to guess a nearest match. The dependent query returns OrderingViolation; raw canonical arrays remain available for investigation. Evidence reference resolution evidence_ref validates a location with resolve_location, then binds the location to Arc::downgrade(&self.trace) (src/trace_parser/evidence.rs:129-135). resolve_evidence checks Weak::ptr_eq before resolving (:140-145). resolve_location performs direct get lookups and maps optional reports to Unavailable. Invariant: identity is owner + location. Equal numeric positions from two independent loads are foreign. A reference cannot be serialized as a portable identity. Deep-validation aggregation validate_deep runs the engine validator and a fixed sequence of passes (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:243-267). Builder::push groups by (code, severity), keeps the first location and increments a count (:814-841). finish orders corruption first (:843-855). Invariant: missing evidence and corruption are different severities. A partial trace can be structurally sound; an optional field can be absent; a malformed reference can be corruption. is_structurally_sound() only checks corruption. Realloc corroboration realloc_link requires a recorded predecessor ID, one compatible successor creation, one predecessor creation, matching PID/sequence/lifetime boundaries, and no cycle (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:1485-1566). Terminal realloc(ptr,0) rows are excluded from creation evidence (:1475-1483). validate_heap reports contradictions, ambiguity/unverified links and cycles (:1778-1834). Invariant: ID existence is not relationship proof. The semantic layer maps Verified to definite only when identity is also definite; otherwise it remains candidate (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:264-285). Confidence qualification ValidatedSemanticView::qualify changes every confidence to Contradictory if the report has any structural corruption (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:61-67). Otherwise, each method supplies a relationship-specific confidence: value validity for a variable, observed PID scope for a heap identity, source candidate status for an AST call, and so on. Invariant: confidence is local in normal cases, global only for corruption. A complete observed-PID heap history does not make a source expression executed or a silent child observed. Bounded consumer pages page validates half-open bounds and rejects ranges wider than 128 (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:20-37). Callers pass a canonical collection length; the iterator yields QueryResult items with positions and references. checkpoint_summary composes one checkpoint and one snapshot reference (:57-68); variable, event, heap, gap and source pages all use the same gate. Invariant: no silent truncation. A 300-item collection is traversed as 0..128, 128..256, 256..300; 0..129 is an explicit limit error. Performance boundaries Loading is monolithic JSON deserialization plus one index build. Queries borrow canonical records; most are O(1) or O(log n) after ordering checks. A source-expression page is a bounded scan over the optional registry (capped at 4,096 expressions), not a line-expanded index. The parser's input byte cap and estimated index bytes are not a process RSS guarantee, and the engine's JSON export cap is not a parser memory cap. The historical 3,143-instruction workload is a benchmark input, not a universal bound. Diagram notes Parser pipeline {{diagram:d3-pipeline}} Performance boundaries {{diagram:d3-performance}}

title: Parser walkthroughs
summary: 57 · Parser cross-file walkthroughs In one sentence: These are short guided routes through parser code: start with one question and follow the records it touches. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Entry point The public function
text: 57 · Parser cross-file walkthroughs In one sentence: These are short guided routes through parser code: start with one question and follow the records it touches. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Entry point The public function a caller uses first, such as TraceStore::open or validated_semantic(). Intermediate record An existing trace value or index position examined along the way; not a reconstructed missing observation. Example. To inspect one variable, open the trace, validate it, locate its exact checkpoint reference, then ask TP-6 for a borrowed variable view and qualified memory evidence. What not to assume: An illustrated path shows how code can work, not that its optional branch ran in every trace. The big picture These are source-guided subsystem sequences, not DOC-4 end-to-end execution stories. They follow real functions and name the data at each boundary. Unless a section explicitly cites a checked-in fixture or a fresh run, the sequence is illustrative. No walkthrough changes the trace or invents a missing relationship. A. Loading a JSON trace Entry: TraceStore::open(path, options). Call path: open → read_trace_bytes → load_trace_document → gates → json::decode_document → validate_schema_version → assemble → TraceIndexes::build (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:240-258,973-995; src/trace_parser/json.rs:19-46). Input: a schema-2 JSON file, or bytes/reader. Intermediate: UTF-8 &str, deserialized DebugSessionTrace, index builders over borrowed vectors. Output: TraceStore { trace: Arc, indexes: Arc, source }. Branches: empty/non-UTF-8 fails before decode; oversized input fails at the byte gate; journal-shaped input fails reconstruction; schema 1/3 fails the schema gate. Errors: EmptyInput, InvalidEncoding, LimitExceeded, MalformedJson, UnsupportedSchemaVersion, JournalReconstructionUnsupported. Sequence: text open - read_trace_bytes - load_trace_document - gates - json::decode_document - schema gate - assemble - TraceIndexes::build - TraceStore Why: loading is intentionally permissive about recorded partiality but strict about input identity. It does not run deep validation. A diagram {{diagram:d3-story-load}} B. Resolving an instruction event Entry: TraceStore::instruction_event(index) or instruction_execution_positions(id). Call path: direct vector get for an event (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:448-458); for a static instruction, ExecutionsIndex::positions_of → CSR slice → instruction_eventsposition (:744-756; src/trace_parser/indexes.rs:313-326). Input: a retained event index or a disassembly ID. Intermediate: CSR offsets/positions. Output: &InstructionEvent or a borrowed event iterator. Branches: an out-of-range event index is OutOfRange; an invalid disassembly ID is InvalidReference; a missing source context is simply not indexed. Why: a static instruction can execute many times; the CSR preserves every event position in ascending order. B diagram {{diagram:d3-story-instruction}} C. Resolving a variable Entry: ValidatedSemanticView::variable(&EvidenceRef). Call path: variable → resolve_evidence → owner check → resolve_location → type_entry/dwarf_declaration/source_declaration → VariableEvidence (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:72-129). Input: a snapshot-variable, global or caller-variable reference. Intermediate: borrowed VariableInfo, optional static metadata. Output: value/type/declaration/source confidences, memory and pointer views. Branches: wrong evidence category is Unavailable; missing static metadata is Unavailable; a valid debugger value is Definite as an observation; pointer status controls candidate/ambiguous/unavailable. Why: static links are optional, while the recorded value is primary evidence at that stop. C diagram {{diagram:d3-story-variable}} D. Validating imported corruption Entry: TraceStore::validate_deep(). Call path: validation::validate_deep → validate_snapshots → validate_pointer_reference; validate_heap → validate_heap_process_coverage (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:243-267,1306-1415,1839-1930). Input: a forged heap target with an allocation ID but no provenance status, or a process annotation claiming all children observed. Intermediate: identity map, recorded history, finding builder. Output: ValidationReport with unavailable/corruption findings. Branches: missing status → POINTER_HEAP_PROVENANCE_UNRECORDED; definite claim from address-only → contradictory; unsupported child claim → HEAP_PROCESS_COVERAGE_UNSUPPORTED. Why: an address or a complete observed-PID flag cannot certify a process tree. D diagram {{diagram:d3-story-corruption}} E. Realloc provenance: valid versus forged Entry: validate_heap and TP-6 heap. Call path: validate_heap → realloc_link → Verified/Ambiguous/Unavailable/Contradictory; TP-6 heap uses the same helper and maps it to confidence (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:1485-1566,1778-1795; src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:264-285). Input: successor block, current/previous lifetimes, creation event iterators. Intermediate: match counts, PID/sequence checks, terminal-zero filter. Output: validation finding and/or heap confidence. Branches: missing predecessor/creation → unavailable; multiple matches → ambiguous; contradictory type/PID/sequence/cycle → corruption; one compatible chain → verified. Why: the audit defect was treating an existing ID as proof; the repair requires event and lifetime corroboration. E diagram {{diagram:d3-story-realloc}} F. Building a consumer checkpoint summary Entry: TraceStore::open → validated_semantic() → checkpoint_summary(index). Call path: checkpoint_summary → checkpoint → evidence_ref(Snapshot); then variables_page, heap_events_page, valgrind_errors_page (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:57-113,239-246). Input: one retained snapshot and a validated view. Intermediate: checkpoint evidence, snapshot reference, page ranges. Output: borrowed variables, heap events and independent diagnostics with confidences. Branches: invalid snapshot → OutOfRange; foreign allocation reference → ForeignTrace; page 128 → LimitExceeded; missing optional report → Unavailable. Why: composition reuses one validation pass and never clones the checkpoint. F diagram {{diagram:d3-story-summary}} G. Independent Valgrind evidence Entry: ValidatedSemanticView::valgrind_error(index). Call path: evidence_ref(ValgrindError(index)) → resolve_evidence → ValgrindEvidence (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:357-374). Input: an independent Valgrind report recorded by the engine. Intermediate: a trace-scoped error reference. Output: source-site candidates and primary_allocation_id: None. Branches: missing report → Unavailable; candidates → Candidate; no candidates → Unavailable. Why: Valgrind ran in a separate process. A matching source line is not a primary-run allocation identity. G diagram {{diagram:d3-story-valgrind}} H. Partial execution Entry: TraceStore::open on a crash, timeout or step-limited trace. Call path: load/index → validate_deep → validated_semantic → raw views and page queries (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:240-408; src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:36-44). Input: a trace with execution_status such as Crashed, Timeout or StepLimitReached. Intermediate: report findings for partial coverage/unavailable evidence. Output: original records remain available; confidence is qualified; gaps and coverage stay explicit. Branches: structural corruption only for broken invariants; partial coverage for caps/interruption; unavailable for absent optional evidence. Why: a partial trace is valid data, not a failed ingestion. H diagram {{diagram:d3-story-partial}} Fixture and verification note tests/fixtures/stage1/realloc_move.json and tests/fixtures/journal/.jsonl are checked-in inputs used by parser tests. The Stage 1 audit's 383-test/16-trace corpus is historical evidence, not a DOC-3 rerun. The walkthroughs above are source-guided; DOC-4 will add fresh end-to-end execution stories.
