title: Parser source file handbook
summary: 58 · Trace Parser source file handbook In one sentence: This is a guide to where parser behavior lives in the repository, organized by the question you are trying to answer. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ TP Trace Parser phas
text: 58 · Trace Parser source file handbook In one sentence: This is a guide to where parser behavior lives in the repository, organized by the question you are trying to answer. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ TP Trace Parser phase; the numbered phases introduced loading, indexes, validation, evidence views and bounded consumer queries. Source chapter A focused explanation of the implementation in one parser file. Example. If TraceStore::open rejects a file, read the ingestion chapter. If it loads but a realloc link is rejected, read validation and the realloc repair chapter. What not to assume: Finding a type or helper in the handbook does not mean that a particular imported trace passed its checks. The big picture This is the DOC-3 coverage index. Every Stage 1 parser production file has a detailed chapter or a dedicated section; the table records the ownership boundary and where to read the implementation. src/semantic/ is Stage 2 and is deliberately excluded. src/trace_parser/semantic.rs is the Stage 1 TP-6 evidence layer, not the Stage 2 semantic engine. How to read the parser Start with ingestion(parser-ingestion-deep.html), then ownership and evidence references(parser-ownership-deep.html), then indexes(parser-indexes-deep.html). Read deep validation(parser-validation-deep.html) before relying on TP-6 confidence(parser-semantic-deep.html), and finish with TP-7 consumer composition(parser-consumer-deep.html). The algorithm reference(parser-algorithms.html) collects cross-file invariants; the function reference(parser-functions.html) is generated from reviewed graph nodes. Production files and detailed treatment File Responsibility Detailed treatment --------- src/trace_parser/mod.rs Loading, gates, schema dispatch, canonical store, raw queries, journal wrappers Ingestion(parser-ingestion-deep.html), ownership(parser-ownership-deep.html), indexes(parser-indexes-deep.html) src/trace_parser/json.rs JSON document decode, schema gate, content-based format detection Ingestion(parser-ingestion-deep.html) src/trace_parser/journal.rs Typed JSONL records, ordering, torn tail, record limits Ingestion(parser-ingestion-deep.html) src/trace_parser/error.rs TraceParseError, QueryError, ingestion/query boundary Ingestion(parser-ingestion-deep.html) src/trace_parser/indexes.rs Position-only execution/source/allocation/metadata indexes and ordering facts Indexes(parser-indexes-deep.html) src/trace_parser/evidence.rs EvidenceLocation, EvidenceRef, borrowed Evidence resolution Ownership and references(parser-ownership-deep.html) src/trace_parser/views.rs Raw/semantic input views, checkpoint contexts, process scope Ownership and references(parser-ownership-deep.html) src/trace_parser/validation.rs Deep validation passes, report model, pointer/process/realloc checks Validation(parser-validation-deep.html), realloc(parser-realloc-deep.html), coverage(parser-coverage-deep.html) src/trace_parser/semantic.rs TP-6 validated evidence, confidence, variable/heap/source/diagnostic views TP-6(parser-semantic-deep.html) src/trace_parser/consumer.rs TP-7 checkpoint summaries, bounded pages and evidence items TP-7(parser-consumer-deep.html) Shared model boundary The parser borrows the engine's DebugSessionTrace model from src/models.rs. DOC-2 covers how the engine constructs that model; DOC-3 only documents how the parser reads and validates it. The engine's JSON export limit is not a parser memory bound, and a schema-valid import is not a semantic validation result. Coverage status The machine-readable inventory(assets/data/stage1-inventory.json) marks these files as having a detailed chapter. Graph-linked functions carry reviewed purpose and classified relationships. Other indexed functions remain source-located but not independently walked through; DOC-3 does not turn a lexical definition into a behavioral proof. Excluded src/semantic/ (SE-1/SE-2), Stage 2 tests/reports, frontend implementation and Trace Engine internals are outside DOC-3. Cross-links to DOC-2 are intentional and do not duplicate engine documentation.

title: Parser function reference
summary: 59 · Trace Parser function reference In one sentence: This catalog helps you find reviewed parser functions and the source lines that implement them. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Public query A function other code may call
text: 59 · Trace Parser function reference In one sentence: This catalog helps you find reviewed parser functions and the source lines that implement them. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Public query A function other code may call to read existing trace evidence. Reviewed relationship A call or data link checked against source and labeled by what it actually means. Example. Find checkpoint_summary, then follow its source link. Its page queries keep the original evidence references and enforce the 128-record page limit. What not to assume: A function list is not a run log. Look at the trace to see which observations actually exist. The big picture This page lists parser functions with a reviewed entry in the DOC-3 call-flow graph. Each entry shows the source location, actual signature, purpose, inputs/outputs, qualification and classified incoming/outgoing relationships. It is a navigation aid, not a claim that every parser helper has an independent walkthrough. Scope A reviewed entry is not a runtime trace claim. Direct edges were checked at call expressions; borrowed-data, index/reference and validation dependencies retain their own labels. Functions absent here can be found in the complete function index(functions.html) or the source handbook(parser-handbook.html). DOC-3 prioritizes ingestion, ownership, indexing, validation, TP-6 and TP-7; less central helpers remain source-located for later expansion. Review status The inventory marks graph-matched symbols as explained_and_graph_linked. Other parser symbols remain file_chapter_indexed_only. This distinction prevents a large but unsupported function encyclopedia. Parser graph entries {{inventory:parser-functions}} Related reading See algorithms and invariants(parser-algorithms.html), the eight walkthroughs(parser-walkthroughs.html), and the interactive call-flow explorer(call-flow.html). Engine counterparts remain in the DOC-2 function reference(engine-functions.html).

title: Execution walkthroughs
summary: 60 · End-to-end execution walkthroughs In one sentence: These are complete stories from a C example through recording and later reading. Use one story at a time rather than memorizing every subsystem first. Key terms Term Plain me
text: 60 · End-to-end execution walkthroughs In one sentence: These are complete stories from a C example through recording and later reading. Use one story at a time rather than memorizing every subsystem first. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Route The ordered steps from a C action, through GCC/GDB/wrapper, into saved JSON and finally a parser query. Oracle An independently checked expected fact used by a test, such as C's sizeof or a native GDB value. Example. In the heap story, follow malloc to a wrapper event, then a lifetime record, then an indexed query. Ask at each arrow whether the next tool saw this same execution. What not to assume: Illustrative event rows and historical audit measurements are labeled; do not treat them as the current program's addresses or complete importable JSON. The big picture These twelve stories connect the DOC-2 engine chapters and DOC-3 parser chapters into continuous source-guided paths. They are not a replacement for the subsystem pages. The normal-execution and parser stories reuse fresh smoke runs recorded in DOC-2/DOC-3; the crash, recursion, fork, heap and adversarial cases use the final Stage 1 audit corpus and are explicitly labeled as historical audit evidence where applicable. Illustrative data is marked as such. 1. Complete normal C execution Scenario. fixtures/c/phase8b_defined.c defines a struct, global, alias, heap array, recursion and realloc. The DOC-2 smoke run and the final audit both report 45 snapshots, 157 retained instruction events and 3 heap events for this fixture. The trace is a normal dual-mode recording with optional AST metadata. Route. CLI/config → GCC → DWARF → GDB stop loop → trace assembly → JSON export → parser load/index → validation → TP-6/TP-7. Call path. 1. main parses CLI and calls Cli::to_config (src/main.rs:26-34; src/cli.rs:197). 2. trace::trace_program creates the supervisor scope and calls trace_program_inner (src/trace.rs:132-167). 3. compiler::compile_project builds the wrapped debug binary and optional sanitizer artifacts (src/trace.rs:235; src/compiler.rs:529-581). 4. dwarf::extract_excluding records static metadata (src/trace.rs:355; src/dwarf.rs:584). 5. run_gdb_phase launches GDB and enters the stop loop (src/trace.rs:1113-1191). The MI reader parses asynchronous stops; a tokened ^done is not a stop (src/gdb_mi.rs:533-671). 6. At a stop, the loop drains event rows, captures state and appends a snapshot/checkpoint (src/trace.rs:1387-1405,1577-1677; src/gdb_mi.rs:1840-2227). 7. trace_program_inner reconstructs heap history, associates DWARF and runs evidence::fuse (src/trace.rs:851-968). 8. main exports the returned DebugSessionTrace through json_export (src/main.rs:50-57; src/json_export.rs:152-167). 9. TraceStore::open gates, decodes and assembles the canonical store (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:240-258). 10. validated_semantic runs one deep pass; checkpoint_summary composes a bounded consumer view (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:38; src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:58). Intermediate data. A stopped frame has stop_id, source location, frame PC and activation path. A snapshot owns variables, caller frames, heap blocks and raw bytes. The JSON has instruction events, source-checkpoint positions, heap events/lifetimes, stage results and coverage. The parser adds only indexes and reports; it does not change the trace. Failure and uncertainty. A missing optional AST registry, a partial memory read or a nonterminal limit remains partial/unavailable. A crash or timeout can still produce a valid trace. The parser's schema load does not certify structural soundness. Why this design. The engine is a recorder, not an interpreter. The parser is an immutable reader. Separating export from load prevents a live debugger from becoming a query dependency. Navigate. Engine architecture(engine-architecture.html), GDB controller(engine-gdb-deep.html), parser ingestion(parser-ingestion-deep.html), parser walkthroughs(parser-walkthroughs.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-1}} 2. Function calls, stack frames and recursion Scenario. fixtures/c/recursive.c calls recurse(3); the final audit records 26 snapshots, 69 retained instructions and 45 caller-frame records with max_caller_frames=3. Route. GCC → GDB frame query → activation path → snapshot caller frames → parser frame-scoped variables. Call path. run_gdb_phase observes a user-code stop (src/trace.rs:1518-1568); GdbSession::capture_state requests -stack-list-frames 0 200 and computes an oldest-to-youngest activation path (src/gdb_mi.rs:1840-1910); capture_caller records caller frames without changing GDB's selected frame (:1753-1834); Recorder::checkpoint retains the snapshot (src/recorder.rs:259-265); TraceStore::checkpoint_summary and CheckpointSummary::frame_activation expose one activation (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:58,251). Intermediate data. Each frame has a level, function, file/line, PC and activation ID. A local variable identity is activation:<id:<scope:<name; two recursive activations with the same name remain distinct. A caller variable is stored in caller_frames, not merged into frame zero. Failure and uncertainty. A truncated frame chain clears activation continuity rather than reusing a sliding prefix. A duplicate caller activation is ambiguous; an ID 0 is no activation. A caller capture error remains visible. Why this design. GDB can print the same function name at several levels. Activation IDs preserve the observed distinction without inventing a cross-stop variable lifetime. Navigate. Stack and memory(engine-stack-deep.html), GDB capture(engine-gdb-deep.html), TP-7 frames(parser-consumer-deep.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-2}} 3. Heap allocation Scenario. phase8b_defined.c performs malloc(3 sizeof(int)); the audit records 3 heap events for the run. Route. C wrapper → event file → Rust reader → HeapTimeline → trace lifetime → parser index → consumer allocation page. Call path. __wrap_malloc calls the real allocator and cte_emit_locked (c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c:343-353,266); the event is appended to the PID-local event file. EventFileReader::read_new accepts complete rows (src/allocation_tracker.rs:293); HeapTimeline::ingest verifies the per-PID sequence and updates block state (:521); push_snapshot records alive blocks (src/trace.rs:2179). The parser builds AllocationIndex by allocation ID (src/trace_parser/indexes.rs:627), ValidatedSemanticView::heap joins lifetime/state/events (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:225), and heap_events_page returns borrowed events (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:88). Intermediate data. An illustrative event row is: json {"kind":"malloc","id":1,"addr":"0x55d0a0002a10","size":32,"pid":100,"seq":4,"caller":"0x401136"} The parser indexes the numeric ID, never the address. A final trace may widen IDs when multiple PIDs are observed; raw event IDs remain PID-local. Failure and uncertainty. A partial write, malformed row, sequence gap or missing ACK lowers completeness. A later event cannot retroactively certify missing rows. An allocation ID is not an exact instruction timestamp. Why this design. Address reuse is legal in C, so identity must come from wrapper events and lifetimes. A file boundary keeps the C runtime independent of Rust. Navigate. C allocator runtime(engine-allocator-deep.html), heap reconstruction(engine-heap-deep.html), parser indexes(parser-indexes-deep.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-3}} 4. Free, address reuse and realloc Scenario. fixtures/c/heap_provenance.c frees and reallocates at a reused address; realloc_move.c moves a block; heap_provenance_realloc.c covers success, failure and glibc's terminal realloc(ptr,0). The final audit reports 44/125/7 for reuse, 12/37/5 for moved and 51/153/15 for the realloc fixture. Route. Wrapper status rows → HeapTimeline → lifetime records → realloc_link → TP-6 confidence. Call path. __wrap_realloc emits failed, ok_same, ok_moved or the observed terminal zero form (c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c:387-419). HeapTimeline::ingest applies status-specific transitions (src/allocation_tracker.rs:606-699). validate_heap calls realloc_link (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:1568-1795), and ValidatedSemanticView::heap maps the helper result to confidence (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:264-285). Valid and rejected relationships. A moved realloc has one compatible successor creation, one predecessor creation, matching PID/sequence and compatible lifetimes; realloc_link returns Verified. A forged realloc_from_id with no compatible creation is Unavailable; conflicting type/PID/sequence or a cycle is Contradictory. A terminal realloc(ptr,0) is a free-shaped terminal event, not a predecessor edge. A failed realloc leaves the old block alive. Intermediate data. A lifetime records allocation ID, PID, native sequence, address, size, free boundary and optional realloc_from_id. Equal addresses across two lifetimes do not merge them. Why this design. The TP8-F01 audit showed that ID existence is not relationship proof. The repair requires event and lifetime corroboration and preserves raw fields for investigation. Navigate. Realloc and TP8-F01(parser-realloc-deep.html), heap evidence(parser-semantic-deep.html), heap reconstruction(engine-heap-deep.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-4}} 5. Pointer observation and provenance Scenario. heap_provenance.c keeps a stale pointer after free, then observes a new allocation at the same address. The audit records ambiguous pointer evidence, not a definite origin. Route. GDB variable read → pointer target → observed maps/heap candidates → validation → PointerEvidence. Call path. GdbSession::capture_state records the variable's value/address/extent (src/gdb_mi.rs:2054-2171); memory::pointer_target compares the numeric address with heap/stack/global extents (src/memory.rs:260-340); validate_pointer_reference checks status, identity, offset and extent (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:1306-1415); PointerEvidence::new maps status to confidence (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:499-540). Intermediate data. A pointer target may contain kind, address, allocation_id, address_match_allocation_id, provenance_status and points_to. A numeric match is address_only/ambiguous_reuse; a definite ID requires compatible recorded provenance. A freed address is not a live object. Failure and uncertainty. A missing status is unavailable, not permission to infer. A definite ID with address-only evidence is contradictory. A pointer variable is not its target object; a target variable identity is resolved only at the same checkpoint. Why this design. Address containment is cheap and useful, but C permits reuse and pointer arithmetic. The parser preserves the observation and refuses to upgrade a candidate. Navigate. Pointer and process coverage(parser-coverage-deep.html), stack and memory(engine-stack-deep.html), TP-6 heap/pointer evidence(parser-semantic-deep.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-5}} 6. DWARF type information Scenario. fixtures/c/dwarf_types.c defines struct Node, struct Container, arrays, bitfields, typedefs and a union. phase8b_defined.c defines struct Packet. Route. GCC debug ELF → DWARF CU/DIE traversal → type/declaration registry → runtime variable association → parser metadata lookup. Call path. compiler::compile_project produces the debug binary; dwarf::extract_excluding enumerates CUs and DIEs (src/dwarf.rs:584); OriginResolver follows specification/abstract-origin references with a four-hop/cycle bound (:213-423); dwarf::associate links unique runtime declarations (:1045); the parser indexes type/declaration IDs (src/trace_parser/indexes.rs:178) and type_entry borrows a record (src/trace_parser/views.rs:369); ValidatedSemanticView::variable exposes optional type/declaration confidence (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:72). Intermediate data. A type entry records kind, size/alignment where known, members, array bounds, bitfields, declaration refs and CU identity. A variable's type_ref/declaration_ref are trace-local IDs, not pointers into the engine process. Failure and uncertainty. Missing optional DWARF is unavailable. An unresolved cross-CU chain is not replaced by a same-name declaration in another CU. A type does not prove initialization or an active union member. Why this design. Static metadata must remain CU-qualified and bounded. The parser borrows it rather than decoding a Stage 2 typed-memory graph. Navigate. DWARF extraction(engine-dwarf-deep.html), Clang AST(engine-ast-deep.html), parser data structures(parser-data-structures.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-6}} 7. Optional Clang AST and evidence fusion Scenario. fixtures/c/ast_source.c contains declarations, a macro allocation, direct calls and source expressions. Route. GCC flags → optional Clang JSON AST → AST registry → evidence fusion → trace cross-references → parser source expression. Call path. trace_program_inner invokes the optional Clang pass (src/trace.rs:371; src/clang_ast.rs:228); evidence::fuse runs once after runtime/heap records (src/evidence/mod.rs:33-91); declaration linking uses CU/DIE-compatible unique matches (src/evidence/declarations.rs:132-153); heap-call correlation is site-only and records candidates/ambiguities (src/clang_ast.rs:947-1054); the parser exposes source_expression (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:291) and TP-7 source pages (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:422). Intermediate data. An AST expression has a source span, declaration/expression IDs and optional macro spelling location. A heap-call candidate is a source line plus ambiguity records, not an allocation ID. Failure and uncertainty. Unsupported GNU extensions or preprocessing differences make correlation unavailable. Multiple calls on one line are ambiguous. A source expression never proves dynamic execution. Why this design. AST syntax is valuable for navigation, but C execution is observed by GDB and allocation telemetry. Fusion is additive and audited. Navigate. Clang AST(engine-ast-deep.html), evidence fusion(engine-fusion-deep.html), parser source expressions(parser-consumer-deep.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-7}} 8. Crash or segmentation fault Scenario. fixtures/c/phase8r3_crash.c writes through a null pointer. The final audit records 3 snapshots, 5 retained instructions and 0 heap events; the run is a crash with partial evidence. Route. GDB fatal-signal stop → partial capture → crash report → optional diagnostics → partial JSON → parser validation → diagnostic query. Call path. run_gdb_phase classifies a fatal signal, captures state and builds a crash report (src/trace.rs:1441-1518); optional sanitizer/Valgrind passes run separately when configured (src/trace.rs:644-849); final assembly preserves coverage and stage results (src/trace.rs:851-1070); the parser's validate_deep reports partial/unavailable evidence (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:243-267); diagnostics() and valgrind_error() expose reports (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:345-374). Intermediate data. A crash report has a signal, source/PC site and optional notes. A snapshot at the fatal stop may be partial. Sanitizer/Valgrind reports are independent diagnostics, not primary-run heap identities. Failure and uncertainty. A missing report is unavailable. A crash does not prove every earlier instruction was retained. A source line in Valgrind is not a primary allocation ID. Why this design. A crash is a valid recorded outcome, not an ingestion error. Partiality is preserved so consumers can distinguish missing evidence from corruption. Navigate. GDB controller(engine-gdb-deep.html), diagnostics(engine-diagnostics-deep.html), parser coverage(parser-coverage-deep.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-8}} 9. Infinite loop and resource limits Scenario. fixtures/c/infinite_loop.c loops on a volatile counter. The final audit records 60 snapshots and 203 retained instructions for infinite_loop, with step_limit_reached and incomplete execution scope. Route. Supervisor deadline/step caps → stop loop → gaps/partial events → partial JSON → parser partial view. Call path. supervisor::scope owns the deadline (src/trace.rs:132-164); run_gdb_phase checks command/step/terminal limits and records a gap when it stops early (src/trace.rs:1371-1568,1954-2024); Recorder::gap stores an attempted-position interval (src/recorder.rs:287-305); export preserves Timeout/StepLimitReached and coverage; the parser reports partial coverage and retains raw events (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:1934-2014). Intermediate data. Attempted instruction count can exceed retained event count. A gap has an origin/reason and instruction position, not invented events. The trace may have snapshots but no proof of termination. Failure and uncertainty. A step limit is not a proof of nontermination. A missing after-stop is not completion. A partial trace is valid data; the parser does not synthesize the unrecorded tail. Why this design. Resource controls are separate from evidence completeness. The engine records what it observed and why it stopped. Navigate. Supervision and limits(engine-supervision-deep.html), GDB stop loop(engine-gdb-deep.html), parser algorithms(parser-algorithms.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-9}} 10. Forked process and heap coverage Scenario. fixtures/c/phase8dr_fork.c supports parent, observed-child, silent-child and incomplete-ACK modes. The final audit reports two event PIDs for observed, one event PID for silent, and two with incomplete ACK; none proves a descendant census. Route. fork/atfork child reset → PID-local event files → reader/ACK verification → heap history → parser process scope. Call path. The C runtime resets child lock/counters/IDs and defers table clearing (c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c:128-143); parent and logged child append PID-local rows; EventFileReader reads rows and verify_event_status checks per-observed-PID ACKs (src/allocation_tracker.rs:178-400); HeapTimeline keeps per-PID sequences; HeapProcessScope::from_history exposes the recorded scope (src/trace_parser/views.rs:28); validate_heap_process_coverage rejects unsupported child claims (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:1839-1930). Intermediate data. The history has observed event PIDs, followed inferior PID, unobserved-process annotation and completeness. Final JSON may widen allocation IDs when multiple PIDs are observed; raw event IDs remain PID-local. Failure and uncertainty. A silent child may produce no events/ACK. A missing ACK lowers completeness. Complete observed-PID history is not all-descendant coverage. Why this design. Fork can duplicate locks and allocator state. PID-local events prevent cross-process identity collisions; absence of evidence remains unknown. Navigate. C allocator runtime(engine-allocator-deep.html), heap reconstruction(engine-heap-deep.html), parser coverage(parser-coverage-deep.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-10}} 11. Trace Parser from the inside Scenario. A completed schema-2 JSON trace, such as examples/v21_heap.json used by the DOC-3 smoke run. Route. Load → schema gate → Arc store → indexes → views → deep validation → TP-6 → TP-7 pages. Call path. TraceStore::open reads/gates/decodes and calls assemble (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:240-258,973-995); TraceIndexes::build constructs position indexes (src/trace_parser/indexes.rs:94); raw()/semantic_input() borrow the store (src/trace_parser/views.rs:433-440); validate_deep runs explicit passes (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:243); validated_semantic retains one report (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:38); checkpoint_summary composes a snapshot reference (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:58); variables_page and heap_events_page return bounded borrowed items (:239,88). Intermediate data. A TraceStore owns Arc<DebugSessionTrace and Arc<TraceIndexes; a CheckpointContext borrows one snapshot; an EvidenceRef holds a weak owner identity plus a location. The parser never clones the trace to answer a query. Failure and uncertainty. A foreign reference fails before numeric lookup; an invalid range/page fails explicitly; a partial trace can be structurally sound but partial. Loading does not run deep validation. Why this design. Canonical ownership makes references safe and cheap. Indexes store positions, not payloads. Validation is explicit and confidence is relationship-specific. Navigate. Parser ingestion(parser-ingestion-deep.html), ownership(parser-ownership-deep.html), indexes(parser-indexes-deep.html), TP-6(parser-semantic-deep.html), TP-7(parser-consumer-deep.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-11}} 12. Corrupted imported evidence Scenario. Schema-compatible mutations of fresh traces: a pointer given a matching address candidate's allocation ID, a silent-fork trace claiming all children observed, and a forged realloc predecessor. The final audit reports structural findings and no definite semantic promotion. Route. Mutated JSON → schema-only load → indexes → deep validation → finding → confidence downgrade → consumer result. Call path. TraceStore::open accepts schema-compatible bytes; validate_deep runs validate_snapshots → validate_pointer_reference, validate_heap → validate_heap_process_coverage, and validate_heap → realloc_link (src/trace_parser/validation.rs:243-267,1306-1415,1568-1930); validated_semantic retains the report; qualify forces Contradictory when structural corruption exists (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:61-67); TP-7 pages still expose raw records but do not claim definite relationships. Observed outcomes. Mutation Finding / disposition ------ Pointer address_only given matching address candidate's ID POINTER_HEAP_PROVENANCE_CONTRADICTORY; structurally unsound Silent fork unobserved_process_coverage forged as all children observed HEAP_PROCESS_COVERAGE_UNSUPPORTED; observed-PID scope remains distinct realloc_from_id forged to successor ID REALLOC_LINK_CONTRADICTORY and/or REALLOC_LINK_CYCLE; not definite Intermediate data. The raw mutated field remains in the trace. Validation reports the first location and occurrence count; semantic confidence describes the relationship, not the whole trace. Failure and uncertainty. Deserialization success is not evidence trustworthiness. A consumer must inspect is_structurally_sound() and is_partial() separately. A missing optional field is not corruption; a contradictory relationship is. Why this design. Raw preservation supports debugging; confidence prevents false certainty. TP8-F01's shared helper ensures parser validation and TP-6 agree. Navigate. Validation(parser-validation-deep.html), realloc(parser-realloc-deep.html), coverage(parser-coverage-deep.html), TP-6(parser-semantic-deep.html). Diagram {{diagram:d4-12}} Source navigation and verification note The normal-execution counts and parser smoke are fresh DOC-2/DOC-3 runs. The recursion, heap, crash, loop, fork and adversarial counts are from docs/stage1-final-audit.md and are historical audit evidence, not DOC-4 reruns. Source links use the inspected dirty worktree at 558037c0da180e152a3e6cc3f351edf0b0583215. Illustrative JSON/MI rows are labeled and are not claimed as captured output.

title: Worked API walkthrough
summary: 61 · Practical usage · from C file to borrowed evidence In one sentence: This page is the hands-on route: record a small C program, open the resulting JSON, and ask one careful question at a time. Key terms Term Plain meaning ----
text: 61 · Practical usage · from C file to borrowed evidence In one sentence: This page is the hands-on route: record a small C program, open the resulting JSON, and ask one careful question at a time. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ CLI The commands and flags you type to run the trace engine. Consumer Your Rust code reading the finished trace through the parser's public API. Example. After recording, check the program's outcome and the validation report. Then request a checkpoint's first page; if there are more than 128 results, request the next page explicitly. What not to assume: The example's chosen stop and address are observations from one run, not identifiers you can reuse in another run. Level 1 · Intuition Run the engine to obtain a JSON document, then parse that document and check its deep-validation report before asking what happened at a checkpoint. One parser store can serve many readers. Observations stay historical; a missing diagnosis or event is not a proven absence. {{diagram:consumer}} Level 2 · Run a recording From the repository root on the supported Linux toolchain: sh cargo build --release target/release/c-trace-engine fixtures/c/phase8b_defined.c \ --trace-mode dual --max-steps 350 --timeout 50 \ --clang-ast --sanitizer-trigger never \ --journal /tmp/visual-c-session.jsonl \ --no-pretty --output /tmp/visual-c-session.json python3 -m json.tool /tmp/visual-c-session.json /tmp/visual-c-readable.json GCC/GDB must be installed; Clang is optional for this command's --clang-ast pass (without it, remove the flag). Valgrind may run as an independent stage if available; --sanitizer-trigger never disables the separate sanitizer run. Do not pass -- before engine options; only program arguments follow --. The engine writes one full JSON document to --output; JSONL can be parsed for records but not loaded as a complete TraceStore. Journals are never overwritten: choose a fresh --journal path for each repeat run (or remove your previous audit-owned temporary file first). See compilation(engine-build.html), deadline policy(engine-limits.html) and the input schema(parser-ingestion.html). A real captured pointer, carefully read The audited phase8b_defined.c trace's frame-0 heap variable at snapshot 4 recorded points_to="0x705010" and the following abridged, exact-field pointer target: json {"kind":"heap","allocation_id":null,"base_address":"0x705010","offset_bytes":0,"active":true,"within_extent":true,"variable_identity":null,"address_match_allocation_id":1,"provenance_status":"address_only"} The raw event at sequence 1 created allocation ID 1 at 0x705010. Matching the numeric address did not certify the pointer's provenance: allocation_id stayed null and the evidence layer's definitive_allocation remains None. Addresses/PIDs can change in new runs; do not hardcode these values. At the same run's checkpoint line 15, snapshot 36 / GDB stop 119 / attempted instruction position 116 are different identifiers; sum displayed "10" with bytes "0a000000". Level 3 · Load and validate The following is a complete Rust example body for examples/stage1_docs_consumer.rs; it uses only public APIs. Save it there and run cargo run --example stage1_docs_consumer -- /tmp/visual-c-session.json (or use the checked-in larger audit consumer cargo run --release --example stage1_public_consumer_audit -- /tmp/visual-c-session.json). rust use c_trace_engine::trace_parser::{ EvidenceLocation, TraceLoadOptions, TraceStore, VariableScope, MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE, }; fn main() - Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error { let path = std::env::args().nth(1).ok_or("provide trace JSON path")?; let store = TraceStore::open(&path, TraceLoadOptions::default())?; let view = store.validated_semantic(); // one deep validation pass for finding in view.report().findings() { eprintln!("{}: {} ({})", finding.severity.label(), finding.code, finding.location); } if !view.report().is_structurally_sound() { return Err("contradictory imported relationships; inspect raw evidence".into()); } println!("status={:?} partial={}", view.execution().status, view.report().is_partial()); for index in 0..store.trace().snapshots.len() { let stop = view.checkpoint_summary(index)?; assert_eq!(stop.reference.location(), EvidenceLocation::Snapshot(index)); let locals = stop.checkpoint.context.variables().len(); for start in (0..locals).step_by(MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE) { let end = (start + MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE).min(locals); for entry in stop.variables_page(VariableScope::Local, start..end)? { let var = entry?; println!("{}: {:?}", var.info.name, var.value_confidence); if let Some(ptr) = &var.pointer { println!("address candidate={:?}; provenance={:?}", ptr.address_candidate, ptr.definitive_allocation); } } } } let process = view.process_coverage(); println!("observed scope={:?}; descendants={:?}", process.scope, process.unobserved_descendants); Ok(()) } Checkpoints and paging This example iterates all retained checkpoints and requests half-open pages of ≤128 locals. It never suppresses a page error or promotes address containment to provenance. Other page lengths come from the actual context (globals(), caller_frames()), event slice (events_at_checkpoint()?) or allocation-position index (heap_event_positions_for_allocation(id)); always request subsequent ranges explicitly. Use view.heap_reference(&ref) for trace-scoped heap evidence, view.diagnostics() for independent reports, and CheckpointSummary(parser-consumer.html) for per-stop composition. The API reference(api.html) details the signatures. Troubleshooting Symptom What to check ------ CompileFailed, no snapshots compile_errors, stage_results.compiler and tool versions; a syntax error is not an empty successful run ForeignTrace Do not pass EvidenceRef from a separately loaded JSON, even if bytes are identical Unavailable AST/bytes Was --clang-ast enabled? Was memory readable and within its budget? Unknown is not zero StepLimitReached / missing heap ACK Consult coverage, gaps, heap history, stage results and partial findings InvalidRange / LimitExceeded Use start..end with end≤len and end-start≤128; do not truncate silently REALLOC_LINK_CONTRADICTORY Imported predecessor disagrees with event/lifetime; inspect verification rules(parser-validation.htmlrealloc-link-verification) NOTE: A structurally sound report can still be partial or missing optional evidence. Treat the report and each per-relationship confidence as different questions.

title: Public API reference
summary: 62 · Public API reference · Trace Engine and Parser In one sentence: An API is the set of functions another Rust program is allowed to call. This reference states their inputs, outputs and limits. Key terms Term Plain meaning ----
text: 62 · Public API reference · Trace Engine and Parser In one sentence: An API is the set of functions another Rust program is allowed to call. This reference states their inputs, outputs and limits. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Borrowed The returned view points to records owned by the TraceStore; it cannot outlive that store. Out of range A request for a position that does not exist in a recorded collection; it is an error, not an empty fabricated record. Example. Load a trace, call validated_semantic(), then ask for an actual snapshot index and an explicitly bounded page of its variables. The result points into the same saved trace. What not to assume: An API signature is not a runnable full example; use the practical usage page for imports and setup. Level 1 · Intuition The engine creates a DebugSessionTrace from C source; the parser makes that finished recording navigable. Loading, deep validation and semantic confidence are three separate operations. Use trace-scoped references for identity, explicit bounded pages for display, and the report for import integrity. {{diagram:handoff}} Level 2 · Ownership and query path TraceConfig/BuildConfig → async trace_program → JSON export; then TraceStore::open → Arc<DebugSessionTrace + Arc<TraceIndexes → validated_semantic() → borrowed CheckpointSummary/EvidenceRef. Cloning a store shares owners; constructing an independent store changes reference identity. All queries borrow canonical records; source_expression(id) and bare heap(id) are trace-local string/numeric lookups, not portable identity tokens. A whole-trace ValidationReport is created once per validated view; pages do not revalidate. Level 3 · Signatures and contracts Record and load Public item (path) Result / contract ------ trace_program(config: TraceConfig) - Result<DebugSessionTrace (src/trace.rs, async) Runs supervised engine; failure trace is still a structured result when possible TraceStore::open(path: impl AsRef<Path, options: TraceLoadOptions) - Result<Self Schema-2 JSON file; 512 MiB default input cap TraceStore::from_json_bytes(bytes: &u8, options: TraceLoadOptions) - Result<Self Explicit one JSON document TraceStore::from_reader(reader: impl Read, options: TraceLoadOptions) - Result<Self Bounded stream read TraceStore::from_trace(trace: DebugSessionTrace) - Result<Self Schema-only gate; does not run validate_deep parse_journal(path, options) - Result<JournalTrace Ordered JSONL records only, no reconstructed TraceStore store.trace() - &DebugSessionTrace, store.shared() - Arc<DebugSessionTrace Canonical immutable owner; clone shares indexes Raw and referenced navigation Public item Use ------ store.snapshot(index), instruction_event(index), instruction_range(range) Original position/half-open borrowed records; raw TP-2 ranges are not TP-7 pages store.events_at_checkpoint(snapshot_index), snapshot_at_stop(stop_id) Explicit tag run and verified-order stop lookup; stop ID is not snapshot index store.instruction_executions(instruction_id), executed_events_for_source(file,line) Preserve repeated dynamic visits; exact recorded source strings store.heap_events_for_allocation(id), heap_block(id), allocation_lifetime(id) Trace-local allocation ID, not address or event position store.raw(), store.semantic_input().checkpoint_context(index) Borrowed canonical source and checkpoint context store.evidence_ref(location), store.resolve_evidence(&reference) Trace-scoped EvidenceRef; foreign store → ForeignTrace Validation and qualified evidence Public item Contract ------ store.validate_deep() - ValidationReport Opt-in structural, partial, unavailable and optional findings store.validated_semantic() - ValidatedSemanticView<'_ Once-deep-validated borrower; view.report() must be inspected view.variable(&EvidenceRef), view.variable_target(&VariableEvidence) Variable/byte/pointer and same-stop variable-identity relationship view.heap(id), view.heap_reference(&EvidenceRef) Identity and separate realloc predecessor confidence view.source_expression(id) Static metadata and call candidates; not execution view.checkpoint(index), view.execution(), view.process_coverage() Stop and independent execution/process dimensions view.diagnostics(), view.valgrind_error(index) Independent reports; never a primary-run Valgrind allocation ID TP-7 pages (all range: Range<usize are half-open) Public item Returned evidence ------ view.checkpoint_summary(index) Borrowed CheckpointSummary<'_, '_ and snapshot reference stop.variables_page(VariableScope::{Local, Global, Caller(position)}, range) TP-6 variable confidence; caller position is not GDB level stop.instruction_events_page(range), stop.heap_interval_page(range) Explicit tag / candidate interval; not exact event cause stop.gaps_in_attempted_window(range), stop.source_expressions_page(range) Position-window gaps / optional static syntax stop.caller_frame(position), stop.frame_activation(id) Same-snapshot activation; missing association is not guessed view.heap_events_page(&EvidenceRef, range), view.valgrind_errors_page(range) Trace-scoped allocation event rows / independent diagnostics stop.coverage(), stop.session_diagnostics(), stop.first_location_findings() Distinct scope, session reports and finding's first location All TP-7 page widths are ≤ MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE (128); an oversize request returns QueryError::LimitExceeded, not a truncated iterator. Raw TraceStore::instruction_range has its separate slice API; do not misstate the TP-7 bound as a universal input/trace-size cap. See pagination implementation(parser-consumer.htmllevel-3-real-signatures-and-bounded-traversal) and the runnable example(usage.htmllevel-3-load-and-validate). NOTE: Type annotations above summarize the public methods; some pages return impl Iterator<Item=QueryResult<_ rather than a copied vector. Consult the named Rust source for complete generic and lifetime parameters.

title: Stage 1 public API
summary: 63 · Stage 1 public API reference In one sentence: This is a compact map of what Stage 1 gives to other code. It distinguishes loading the recording from checking its claims. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ TraceStore The owne
text: 63 · Stage 1 public API reference In one sentence: This is a compact map of what Stage 1 gives to other code. It distinguishes loading the recording from checking its claims. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ TraceStore The owner of one loaded trace and its lookup indexes. Validated view A read-only interface made after the deeper consistency check, with confidence attached to specific questions. Example. A consumer can follow an evidence reference to a variable at stop 4, inspect its captured bytes, and still report the variable's pointer origin as unknown. What not to assume: Do not treat TraceStore::from_trace or successful JSON import as a deep semantic validation. The big picture This is the downstream boundary for a recorded Stage 1 trace. It is not a Stage 2 semantic engine. The API returns borrowed evidence, explicit confidence and bounded pages; it does not infer C objects, pointer origin, initialization or process-tree completeness. Imports and ownership rust use c_trace_engine::trace_parser::{ EvidenceConfidence, EvidenceRef, QueryError, TraceLoadOptions, TraceStore, }; TraceStore::open(path, options) returns an owned handle with Arc<DebugSessionTrace and Arc<TraceIndexes (src/trace_parser/mod.rs:240-258). Cloning the store is cheap and shares the same trace identity. Loading the same JSON again creates an independent owner; its references are foreign. Load and validate rust let store = TraceStore::open("trace.json", TraceLoadOptions::default())?; let validated = store.validated_semantic(); let report = store.validate_deep(); assert!(report.is_structurally_sound()); validated_semantic() runs validate_deep() once and retains the report (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:38). Queries do not rerun validation. is_structurally_sound() is separate from is_partial(): a partial trace can be structurally sound, and an optional field can be absent without corruption. Checkpoint summary rust let summary = validated.checkpoint_summary(index)?; let stop = summary.stop_id(); let source = summary.source_location(); let locals = summary.variables_page( c_trace_engine::trace_parser::VariableScope::Local, 0..16, )?; checkpoint_summary(index) resolves a snapshot and creates a trace-scoped snapshot EvidenceRef (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:58). The summary borrows the validated view and the canonical store; it does not clone the snapshot. stop_id() converts the model's zero sentinel to None. Variables, frames and pages VariableScope is Local, Global or Caller(position) (src/trace_parser/consumer.rs:41-46). variables_page returns an exact-size iterator of QueryResult<VariableEvidence; frame_activation(id) resolves a unique activation at that checkpoint, not a cross-stop lifetime (:251). instruction_events_page(range) pages events explicitly tagged with the checkpoint ID (:319). heap_interval_page(range) pages heap events between retained snapshot counters and is a candidate temporal association (:349). source_expressions_page(range) pages AST source-span candidates and never proves execution (:422). All pages use MAX_CONSUMER_PAGE = 128 and a half-open range. A page wider than 128 returns QueryError::LimitExceeded; an invalid or reversed range returns InvalidRange. There is no silent truncation. Heap and diagnostics validated.heap(allocation_id) joins lifetime, final block, history and realloc confidence (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:225). validated.heap_reference(&evidence_ref) resolves a trace-scoped allocation reference first (:205). validated.valgrind_error(index) returns an independent Valgrind error; primary_allocation_id is always None (:357). validated.diagnostics() borrows compiler/crash/sanitizer/Valgrind reports (:345). validated.process_coverage() exposes the recorded observed-PID scope and leaves unknown descendants unavailable (:378). Confidence handling EvidenceConfidence is Definite, Candidate, Ambiguous, Unavailable or Contradictory (src/trace_parser/semantic.rs:20). It belongs to a relationship. A variable value can be definite while its pointer origin is unavailable. A heap identity can be definite while its realloc link is ambiguous. Any structural corruption makes qualify return Contradictory for all relationships (:61-67). Do not merge confidence with execution status, memory readability, initialization, scope activity, heap coverage or process-tree completeness. Evidence references and errors An EvidenceRef stores a Weak<DebugSessionTrace and an EvidenceLocation (src/trace_parser/evidence.rs:68-75). resolve_evidence checks owner identity before resolving the position (:140-145). A reference from an independent load is QueryError::ForeignTrace; an invalid position is InvalidReference; missing optional evidence is Unavailable. Raw records remain accessible through store.raw() even when a semantic relationship is unavailable. Deliberate limits Stage 1 leaves C-language interpretation to downstream code. It does not execute source, evaluate DWARF location expressions, infer an active union member, turn a source candidate into an executed expression, turn an address match into allocation origin, or turn observed-PID completeness into a descendant census. Those are not missing convenience features; they are evidence-contract boundaries. Diagram {{diagram:d3-pipeline}} Related reading Parser ingestion(parser-ingestion-deep.html), ownership and evidence references(parser-ownership-deep.html), TP-6(parser-semantic-deep.html), TP-7(parser-consumer-deep.html), limitations(limitations.html).

title: Schema & identity reference
summary: 64 · Schema v2 and identity reference In one sentence: The schema lists the JSON fields that save a recording. The most important reading habit is to ask what each number identifies. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Schema vers
text: 64 · Schema v2 and identity reference In one sentence: The schema lists the JSON fields that save a recording. The most important reading habit is to ask what each number identifies. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Schema version The format version. The supported V2.1 and V2.2 traces here use version 2; not every older example file can be imported. Nullable A field can say 'no value recorded.' That is not the same as 'the value was zero' or 'nothing happened.' Example. An event can have allocation_id=2, while its address is 0x705010. A later block can also live at 0x705010 with a different ID. Keep the ID and address separate. What not to assume: Short JSON projections show selected fields for study, not full documents to paste into the parser. Level 1 · Intuition A source line, stopped PC, snapshot position, instruction attempt, allocation lifetime and process address are different kinds of information. Mixing their integers creates convincing but false explanations. The model deliberately records explicit references, nullable fields, scopes and gaps so readers can say what was observed and what remains unknown. {{diagram:records}} Level 2 · Top-level JSON The complete JSON trace is represented in Rust by DebugSessionTrace in src/models.rs. Its RecordingData fields are flattened: instead of appearing under a recording object, items such as snapshots appear at the top level. Think of the fields in groups. compiled_successfully and compile_errors describe the build; snapshots, instruction_events, source_checkpoints, trace_gaps and coverage describe the debugger recording; heap_events, heap_state, allocation_lifetimes and heap_history describe observed allocator activity. stage_results, execution_status, resource_usage, execution_limits and storage describe outcomes and limits. type_registry, source_metadata, evidence_fusion and crash or memory-error reports may be optional. Null or missing optional data does not mean the check succeeded. schema_version=2 works for supported V2.1/V2.2 files, not every older schema-2 example: four pre-V2.1 files contain a removed limit key and do not import. Older register fields may be parsed for compatibility but are no longer exported for each instruction. Identity domains Domain Where recorded What it is not --------- Snapshot vector index / step_index snapshotsi GDB stop counter or instruction attempt GDB stop_id Snapshot observation, event before/after, journal wrapper Snapshot index; not necessarily consecutive instruction_position, instruction_count Stop/gap/trace Retained event position; journal-only can retain zero in JSON event_id / event vector position instruction_eventsj instruction_id (disassembly table) or unique source line checkpoint_id InstructionEvent Exact execution at that stop; only most recent checkpoint tag source_checkpointsn RecordingData Duplicated snapshot; it stores snapshot index allocation_id, old_allocation_id Heap events, state, lifetime Process address, event index or pointer provenance; 0 untracked sequence, pid Heap runtime Stop/event positions; sequences start per PID activation_id, lexical_scope_id Frame/variable Source variable name or address address, points_to, next_address Memory/event/variable Identity; numeric addresses can recur Heap records HeapEvent stores event_type=allocatedreallocatedfreedallocation_failed, per-PID sequence, pid, allocation_id, optional old_allocation_id, address, size, caller and detail. AllocationLifetime stores allocation ID, PID, allocation sequence and optional free sequence. HeapBlockInfo stores final/historical state and optionally realloc_from_id; each snapshot can store alive heap_blocks as observed at a stop. These are complementary, not one-to-one byte replicas. Successful realloc requires relationship verification(parser-validation.htmlrealloc-link-verification). HeapHistoryCoverage.complete is scoped to verified observed event PIDs plus followed inferior, with unknown descendants. Level 3 · Accurate field-level examples The following is a projection of fields from a captured phase8b_defined.c run, not a complete importable trace. OS-specific PID/address values differ between runs. Its first two events describe an in-place realloc that starts a new lifetime ID; the third frees the successor: json {"sequence":1,"allocation_id":1,"old_allocation_id":null,"event_type":"allocated","address":"0x705010","size_bytes":12} {"sequence":2,"allocation_id":2,"old_allocation_id":1,"event_type":"reallocated","address":"0x705010","size_bytes":16} {"sequence":3,"allocation_id":2,"old_allocation_id":null,"event_type":"freed","address":"0x705010","size_bytes":16} raw_bytes_hex="0a000000" at an audited stop is a byte capture, not proof the C initializer ran. A separately recorded PointerTarget can report address_match_allocation_id=1 and allocation_id=null, because address containment is not origin. To load a full trace, run the CLI walkthrough(usage.htmllevel-2-run-a-recording); do not paste these projections into TraceStore::open. NOTE: JSON export's max_json_export_bytes bounds the serialized document; neither that nor the parser's input cap bounds already assembled engine trace RAM. Resource policy(engine-limits.htmllevel-2-budgets-across-stages) lists the separate limits.

title: Stage 2 handoff & limits
summary: 65 · Stage 2 handoff · guarantees, limits and glossary In one sentence: Stage 1 hands later code evidence, not unquestionable conclusions. This page says exactly where that handoff ends. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Freeze
text: 65 · Stage 2 handoff · guarantees, limits and glossary In one sentence: Stage 1 hands later code evidence, not unquestionable conclusions. This page says exactly where that handoff ends. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Freeze contract The agreed, tested behavior and limits downstream code must preserve rather than silently broaden. Qualified evidence A recorded fact together with its scope, confidence, source and missing-data conditions. Example. Stage 2 may draw a variable's observed bytes and label their capture status. It must not infer that a pointer owns the heap block whose current address matches it. What not to assume: Stage 1 is not a sandbox, a whole-process-tree recorder, an initialized-memory oracle or a guarantee of assembled-trace RAM. Level 1 · Intuition Stage 1 hands future consumers a validated, immutable, bounded-query evidence source, not a complete reconstruction of C program meaning. A sound trace can be partial; an observed object can have uncertain origin. Stage 2 may derive explanations while displaying their evidence and qualifications, but must never turn a missing observation into a fact. {{diagram:handoff}} Level 2 · The freeze contract - Load a supported schema-v2 document through TraceStore; remember ingestion is schema-only. Call validated_semantic() and inspect report().is_structurally_sound(), is_partial() and individual findings. - Share the canonical Arc<DebugSessionTrace/Arc<TraceIndexes via cloned TraceStore; use borrowed records and same-trace EvidenceRef, not numeric IDs from another execution. - Page checkpoint variables, events and diagnostics using explicit half-open ranges no wider than 128; request all subsequent pages. Distinguish Unavailable, empty evidence and an actual error. - Maintain separate execution status, attempted/retained events, gaps, byte readability, lexical scope, initialization (often unknown), heap-history/observed PID scope and semantic relationship confidence. - Keep heap realloc links dependent on recorded event and same-PID lifetime boundaries; no predecessor from numeric address equality. Never equate pointer containment to origin, AST syntax to execution, Valgrind source site to primary-run allocation ID or scoped PID completion to complete descendants. Level 3 · Concrete API handoff rust let view = store.validated_semantic(); if !view.report().is_structurally_sound() { // Display contradictory imported relationships, not a definite explanation. } let scope = view.process_coverage(); // descendants remain unavailable let stop = view.checkpoint_summary(snapshot_index)?; let _ = (scope.unobserved_descendants, stop.reference.location()); This is a body excerpt using public APIs from src/trace_parser/{semantic,consumer,evidence}.rs; follow the complete runnable example(usage.htmllevel-3-load-and-validate). The API tables(api.htmllevel-3-signatures-and-contracts) list query signatures; validation(parser-validation.htmlrealloc-link-verification) covers adversarial realloc imports. Stage 2 implementation is outside the scope of this site; this public boundary does not provide an execution interpreter, provenance graph or GUI. Performance (not a guarantee) In the independent Stage 1 release-profile audit, a 3.337 MB, 900-snapshot / 3,143-real-instruction-event trace took approximately 48 ms median typed parse, 1.13 ms index build, 0.555 ms once-only semantic validation and ~17 MiB parser-process RSS after indexing across three runs. A 461 KB small trace took ~8.27 ms parse and ~0.264 ms index build. The index estimate for the heavy sample was 28,369 bytes, not process RSS; per-query TP-7 measurements reported zero allocations but once-only validation allocated. Host, allocator and workload variation are material; these are not Stage 2 latency commitments. Input/JSON byte limits do not bound total RAM. See limits(engine-limits.html). Known limitations 1. Coverage: user-code, selected-thread and followed-inferior stop scope; gaps, no complete all-thread or fork-descendant instruction timeline; silent children unknown. 2. Heap: only linked-object allocator wrappers and accepted telemetry; incomplete transport/ACK or legacy metadata lowers confidence. Pointer address containment is not allocation provenance. Historical bytes never get rewritten by later frees/reuse. 3. Static/diagnostic: AST candidates do not prove expression execution. DWARF metadata may be missing. Valgrind and sanitizers are independent processes; equal source/address does not establish primary allocation identity. 4. Memory: readable GDB bytes and lexical scope do not prove C initialization; unattempted or capped tails are not silently decoded. 5. Resources/portability: no sandbox, hard total-engine-RAM guarantee or full parser streaming/seek index. Linux x86-64/GCC/GDB-supported evidence is not a universal cross-platform promise. Four pre-V2.1 files with removed fields remain unsupported on import. Glossary Term Meaning ------ Checkpoint Retained stopped snapshot; not every program instruction or stop Stop ID Processed GDB stop counter, distinct from vector/attempt indices Event position Index into canonical retained event array; never invent missing entries Gap Interval where instruction capture lacks exact events; unknown count Allocation lifetime Trace-local observed identity with PID/sequence boundaries, not an address Provenance Evidence of where a pointer originated; containment alone is insufficient EvidenceRef Weak-trace-identity citation to a canonical record; not portable Definite Verified specific observation/relation under its documented scope Candidate / Ambiguous Plausible unproved relation / multiple compatible relations Unavailable / Contradictory Insufficient evidence / structurally rejected relationship Partial coverage Some observations missing; does not mean record corruption Independent diagnostic Valgrind or sanitizer output from another execution WARNING: The approved Stage 1 freeze authorizes a qualified input for future semantic work, not permission to collapse these terms into a single “trace complete” flag. See the final integrated audit(../stage1-final-audit.md) for verification scope.

title: Terminology and glossary
summary: 66 · Terminology and glossary In one sentence: Use this as a quick translation when you meet a technical word elsewhere. Return to its linked chapter for the full example. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Evidence Something act
text: 66 · Terminology and glossary In one sentence: Use this as a quick translation when you meet a technical word elsewhere. Return to its linked chapter for the full example. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Evidence Something actually recorded or statically described, with a source and limits. Inference A conclusion drawn from evidence. It may be useful, but it should never be relabeled as a directly recorded fact. Example. GDB recorded raw_bytes_hex=0a000000. 'Four bytes were read' describes evidence. 'The C initializer ran' would be an inference that those bytes alone do not support. What not to assume: A word such as 'complete' always needs a scope: complete for which processes, time interval and kind of record? The big picture The same numeric value can identify different things at different boundaries. Start with a type's owner and scope before joining two records. Recording terms Term Meaning ------ Checkpoint Retained source-level snapshot at one observed stop, not every executed instruction. Stop ID Debugger stop counter, not a snapshot vector position. Attempted instruction An attempt to record/advance at a PC; retention and gaps have separate accounting. Retained event Actual indexed record in the instruction-event array. Gap Explicit interval of execution not recorded as exact instructions. Allocation lifetime Wrapper-derived, scoped identity; an address may be reused by another lifetime. Evidence terms Term Meaning ------ Structural finding Imported trace contradicts a supported invariant; not simply an incomplete run. Partial Some observation scope is absent, capped or interrupted. Unavailable Evidence does not establish the requested relationship. Candidate Compatible evidence without an exact proof under the documented scope. EvidenceRef Citation bound to the same canonical trace owner and original record position. Source-site candidate Shared source file/line from an independent process; no primary allocation ID. Continue reading See identity domains(identity-contracts.html), schema(schema.html) and public API(api.html) for concrete fields and confidence qualifiers. DOC-2/3 will expand individual terms next to the code paths where they are produced.

title: Known limitations
summary: 67 · Known limitations In one sentence: This page is part of the explanation, not fine print. A good UI shows what a trace cannot say alongside what it can. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Partial trace A recording in which so
text: 67 · Known limitations In one sentence: This page is part of the explanation, not fine print. A good UI shows what a trace cannot say alongside what it can. Key terms Term Plain meaning ------ Partial trace A recording in which some intended observations were not retained, perhaps after a crash, timeout or budget limit. Unknown The system lacks sufficient evidence. It is not equivalent to false, zero, freed or no bug. Example. A silent child might create allocations without producing wrapper log lines. A complete log for the parent does not make that child's history appear. What not to assume: Missing observations, independent diagnostic runs and RAM limits remain real even when the JSON file loaded successfully. The big picture Stage 1 is an evidence recorder and immutable reader, not a complete semantics oracle or a security sandbox. These limits apply even when a trace loads and deep validation reports no structural corruption. Observation limits GDB follows one inferior and its chosen execution scope; unstepped libraries, threads and fork descendants may be missing. Heap wrappers intercept the linked program's allocator calls, not all allocations inside shared libraries. heap_history.complete covers verified observed event PIDs and the followed inferior, not silent descendants. Memory reads can be partial or unavailable; complete bytes do not prove initialization, union activity or a pointer's origin. Independent providers Clang AST syntax does not show that an expression ran. DWARF declarations and source lines can be ambiguous. Valgrind and sanitizer passes execute separately and cannot supply exact primary-run allocation IDs by matching an address, source line or function. Reallocation confidence requires recorded event/lifetime corroboration, not mere agreement between addresses. Resource and compatibility limits Resource budgets are not hostile-program isolation. The 128 MiB default JSON export budget limits a serialized document, not already assembled trace RAM. Parser JSON input is not streaming; its input cap and estimated index bytes do not bound process RSS. Journals contain ordered records but not enough final-state fields for full trace reconstruction. The four historical pre-V2.1 examples/v2_.json traces with removed limit fields remain unsupported imports; the six named V2.1 traces are the compatible corpus. Inspection caveats The historical TP-8 conditional audit predates the TP8-F01 repair and the final integrated Stage 1 audit. A source review found that json::detect_format treats a malformed final journal-shaped line as a journal candidate even when newline-terminated, while typed journal::parse_reader still rejects that complete malformed record. Separately, journal::parse_reader reapplies Take(max_bytes) per line, so its arbitrary-reader route does not enforce an aggregate stream-byte cap. These are source-inspection observations, not DOC-1 production fixes or claims of an executed exploit; see src/trace_parser/json.rs:69 and src/trace_parser/journal.rs:167. DOC-2/3 should reproduce and characterize them before changing contractual claims.
